authors: Mohottige D. Neranjan Tharuka;Dai-Hua Chen;Maria Luisa Jurgensen Amaral;Tianchen Ren;Yixuan Kuang;Shih-Ting Huang;Nikhil Chilakapati;Bing Ren;Stephen P. Schoenberger;Ye Zheng;Yuan Chen
title: SUMO2 deletion changes chromatin accessibility and enhances cytotoxic T cell activation and tumor infiltration
abstract: Cytotoxic T cells [cytotoxic lymphocytes (CTLs)] are crucial for adaptive immunity leading to prolonged survival and potential cures for cancer. Recent clinical data have shown that pharmacological inhibition modifies the tumor microenvironment (TME) and activates CTLs, although the mechanism is not well described. In this study, we found that T cell–specific knockout (KO) of the most prevalent SUMO paralog,Sumo2/SUMO2, in both mouse and human CD8+T cells significantly enhanced CD8+T cell activation without enhanced IFN-I (type I interferon)–responsive genes in vitro but increased chromatin accessibility at enhancer regions for AP-1 (activating protein 1) family members, including BATF and JunB, which are known to promote T cell activation and proliferation. Using antigen-specific OT1 and CAR (chimeric antigen receptor) T cell models, we found thatSumo2KO CD8+T cells had significantly higher tumor infiltration, as revealed by flow cytometry, immunofluorescence staining, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), and conferred greater tumor growth inhibition than wild-type control T cells. snRNA-seq also revealed thatSumo2KO in CD8+T cells increased the expression of TRAIL (tumor necrosis factor–related apoptosis-inducing ligand) in vivo and activated the antitumor immune microenvironment, likely through cell-cell interaction involving more activated CTLs. These findings elucidate a novel mechanism by which SUMOylation controls CTL activation and tumor infiltration that activate antitumor immunity in the TME. SUMO2 KO can also be a potential strategy to enhance adoptive T cell therapies for solid tumors by enhancing their activation, tumor infiltration and ability to modulate the TME.

authors: Jing Tao;Yuzhen Guo;Fengzhi Zhang;Jiahui Wu;Liyun Xing;Jinxia Kong;Lian Li;Zhou Zhou;Yuan Huang
title: Senescent tumor cell membrane–based “time engine” nanosystem amplifies endoplasmic reticulum targeting for metastasis blockade
abstract: As an important component of biomimetic drug delivery systems, cell membrane–coated nanoparticles are widely used for subcellular delivery. However, the influence of cell membranes at different life cycles on subcellular delivery remains unexplored. Our previous study demonstrated that senescent tumor cell membrane–coated nanoparticles (SNP) displayed superior endoplasmic reticulum (ER) targeting efficiency in tumor cells. After inducing tumor cells into senescence, SNP showed greater accumulation in ER. Herein, we design a “time engine” nanosystem for amplified ER targeting: Firstly, ribociclib is encapsulated into SNP (R@SNP) to induce tumor cell senescence; then, SNP loaded with brefeldin A (B@SNP) is used to trigger ER stress. By sequential therapy, R@SNP disrupts the cytoskeleton of 4T1 tumor cells to eliminate ER-targeting barriers and remodels the tumor immune microenvironment; B@SNP boosts ER-targeting efficiency and triggers intense ER stress. Collectively, such time engine nanosystem achieves excellent ER accumulation and antimetastatic efficacy in 4T1 tumor–bearing mice, providing an innovative perspective for subcellular delivery and tumor treatment.

title: On-fault and remote observations of exceptionally long, supershear rupture in the 2025 M 7.7 Mandalay earthquake
abstract: Straight faults are considered prone to large supershear ruptures and seismic gaps to likely host future earthquakes. Both predictions may have been fulfilled in the magnitude (M) 7.7 Mandalay earthquake of 28 March 2025 on the Sagaing Fault. Exceptional video footage of the fault rupture, high-rate Global Navigation Satellite System, and seismological and remote sensing data reveal a supershear slip pulse that formed early and ruptured a well-identified seismic gap but propagated well beyond it, resulting in an exceptional rupture length of 510 kilometers. By contrast, the slip pulse observed in the video footage has subshear characteristics. These observations can be reconciled by a preferred conceptual interpretation invoking depth-dependent weakening properties, stress heterogeneity, and possible dynamic triggering. These properties allow for energetic ruptures that stay confined to the depth range locked in the interseismic period but are not confined to seismic gaps along strike.

title: Chromatin interaction landscape of epimorphic regeneration in teleost fish
abstract: Reorganization of chromatin architecture—including chromatin loops, topologically associating domains (TADs), and A/B compartments—has been increasingly linked to development and cell differentiation. However, how chromatin architecture reorganizes during the shift from homeostasis to regeneration remains poorly characterized. Here, we used zebrafish fin regeneration as a model to systematically investigate, via micro-C, the chromatin architecture associated with blastema formation. Our analyses unveiled that the alteration of chromatin looping upon amputation was dominant compared with that of TADs and compartments. Genes directly linked to injury-altered loop interactions, including essential regeneration regulators, were mainly related to morphogenesis and cell division. A side-by-side comparison between zebrafish and African killifish uncovered conserved and species-specific chromatin reorganization following injury. Notably, perturbing injury-altered loop interactions at theil11alocus suppressed its expression and impaired fin regeneration efficiency. Further, CTCF/CTCFL and Atf7 binding motifs were the top shared motifs enriched in regeneration-altered loop anchors. Our study uncovers the landscape of chromatin interactions during fin regeneration.

title: Multidegree fluorescence–optical rotatory dispersion (F-ORD) from submonolayer interfacial chiral films
abstract: Homochiral monomolecular thin films adsorbed to fused silica produced fluorescence–optical rotatory dispersion (F-ORD; i.e., optical rotation of the fluorescence emission relative to the excitation beam) more than seven orders of magnitude greater than anticipated by conventional origins of optical rotatory dispersion (i.e., optical rotation of the excitation beam after passing through a chiral film relative to its initial plane of polarization). Optical rotation of −4.5 ± 0.5° was observed in the principal axis of fluorescence emission relative to that of excitation for submonolayer dip-coated thin films of (S)-naproxen, with the sign of the rotation inverting for comparable films of (R)-naproxen. The chiral-specific F-ORD response was nonreciprocal, inverting in sign upon flipping of the sample orientation (i.e., source-facing versus detector-facing), suggesting selectivity to chiral molecules oriented at the interface. The interface selectivity, chiral selectivity, and large magnitude of the response were in excellent agreement with a fully electric-dipole–allowed orientational mechanism for chiral-specific fluorescence in uniaxial systems. These observations elevate fluorescence as a novel chiral-specific probe with exquisite sensitivity to chirality and interface specificity akin to that normally reserved for even-ordered nonlinear optical interactions, such as second harmonic and sum-frequency spectroscopy.

title: Carbonic anhydrase VIII regulates IP3R1-dependent Ca2+ signaling to coordinate insulin secretion and hepatic glucose production
abstract: Intracellular Ca2+signaling is essential for glucose-induced insulin secretion (GIIS) and hepatic glucose production (HGP), yet how Ca2+dynamics are coordinated across organs remains unclear. Carbonic anhydrase VIII (CA8), an endogenous inhibitor of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor 1 (IP3R1), was identified as a shared regulator of pancreatic and hepatic glucose metabolism. UsingCar8wdlmice, we showed that CA8 deficiency enhanced GIIS and HGP in vivo and ex vivo. In islets and hepatocytes, CA8 loss augments Ca2+oscillations, an effect abolished by IP3R inhibition orCar8reexpression. Enhanced HGP persists independently of glucagon receptor, PLC, or PKA signaling and occurs without increased IP1, indicating heightened IP3R1 sensitivity rather than increased IP3production. In hepatocytes, chronic glucagon exposure attenuated acute glucagon responsiveness in a CA8-dependent manner. In obese diabetic mice, CA8 increased in islets but decreased in hepatocytes; hepatic CA8 restoration reduced excessive HGP. Collectively, these findings identify CA8 as a cross-organ regulator of IP3R1-dependent Ca2+signaling with translational relevance to diabetes.

title: Mesoscale structures in signed networks
abstract: Mesoscale structures in signed networks have been studied under the limiting assumption of the validity of social balance theory, which predicts positive connections within groups and negative connections between groups. Here, we propose and apply a methodology that overcomes this limitation and is able to find and characterize also the different possible unbalanced structures in signed networks. Applying our methodology to 24 empirical networks, from social-political, financial, and biological domains, we find that unbalanced mesoscale structures are prevalent in real-world networks, including cases with substantial balance at the microscale of triangles. In particular, we find that assortativity often prevails regardless of the interaction sign and that core-periphery structures are typical in online social networks. Our findings highlight the complexity of mesoscale relational structures, the importance of using computational methods that are a priori agnostic to specific patterns, and the importance of independently evaluating micro- and mesoscale predictions of social balance theory.

title: Magnetic omniconversion: Source-independent molding of magnetostatic fields
abstract: Magnetic fields are constrained by the geometry and location of their sources, limiting the ability to freely tailor their spatial distribution. We introduce a general framework to passively convert the magnetic field generated by arbitrary sources into any prescribed desired field within a finite source-free region. Our method relies on field shaping using linear magnetic materials, enabling source-independent magnetic field molding. We provide the general recipe, analytical and numerical demonstrations for some paradigmatic examples, and a proof-of-concept experiment that validates the idea and materials implementation. This approach enables original possibilities in magnetic shielding, targeted field delivery, advanced imaging technologies, and a broad range of field-control applications.

title: Standardizing Cell Ontology terms for cross-study integration in the female reproductive tract
abstract: The female reproductive tract is essential for fertility, pregnancy, and overall health, yet many of its cellular components remain poorly defined. Recent advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics have begun to reveal this complexity, but inconsistent naming of cell types and states has limited the ability to compare findings across studies. To address this challenge, an international group of reproductive biologists and ontology experts collaborated to harmonize annotations within Cell Ontology, focusing on the ovary, fallopian tube, and uterus. Standardized terms are proposed for major epithelial, stromal, and germ cell populations, supported by marker gene sets and anatomical linkages. This framework provides a shared reference that can be used to harmonize existing datasets and guide annotation of future studies, enabling consistent classification of oocytes, granulosa, theca, luteal, epithelial, stromal, and immune cells across tissues. By establishing a unified taxonomy, this work lays the foundation for integrating datasets, supporting cross-tissue comparisons, and advancing the understanding of reproductive biology, health, and disease.

title: Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
abstract:
Superconducting diodes can provide nonreciprocal elements for superconducting and quantum circuits, but the role of diode efficiency in quantum-device performance remains unclear. Here, the authors demonstrate an enhanced superconducting diode effect in twisted NbSe2 and show that even a moderate degree of nonreciprocity is sufficient to stabilize anharmonic qubit circuits. 
 In superconducting circuits, bidirectional signal propagation can cause back-reflections and back-action that couple environmental noise back to coherent elements, degrading fidelity. Nonreciprocal superconducting diodes provide an intrinsic route to suppress such back-scattering at the circuit level. However, their diode efficiency and quantum integration remain limited. Here, we realize a quantum diode in twisted NbSe2 under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields. A mere 1∘ twist yields an efficiency enhancement over pristine devices, reaching 27.6%. Quantum simulations reveal that this intermediate efficiency, well below 100% ideal, is both experimentally practical and optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and stabilizing two-level systems. These findings show that maximal rectification is not always beneficial for quantum information, establishing a new principle for designing the fundamental properties of twisted superconductors towards low-power, high-fidelity quantum circuits. Superconducting diodes can provide nonreciprocal elements for superconducting and quantum circuits, but the role of diode efficiency in quantum-device performance remains unclear. Here, the authors demonstrate an enhanced superconducting diode effect in twisted NbSe2 and show that even a moderate degree of nonreciprocity is sufficient to stabilize anharmonic qubit circuits.

title: Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus
abstract:
The authors show that, when detecting the presence of tactile stimuli, mouse primary somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decisions through the midbrain superior colliculus, primarily by shifting decision bias rather than the ability to detect the stimulus. 
 Sensory inputs reach cortical and subcortical areas in parallel, but how they coordinate to guide decisions remains unknown. We examined the roles of the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and the superior colliculus (SC) in mice performing whisker-mediated tactile detection. While inactivating S1 contralateral to the stimulus increased detection threshold, inactivating ipsilateral S1 decreased it. These opposing effects reflected shifts in choice bias rather than sensitivity. Unilateral SC inactivation produced similar directional effects, whereas bilateral inactivation of either S1 or SC neutralized bias. Furthermore, SC lesions impaired detection performance, and combined S1 inactivation caused no further impairment, indicating that S1-mediated shifts in bias were SC-dependent. S1 inactivation also decreased sensory-evoked neural activity in SC, and choice decoding revealed that behavioral impairment was more closely associated with changes in SC population activity than with loss of sensory encoding in S1. Thus, S1 shapes perceptual bias by modulating SC-dependent circuits that transform sensory evidence into perceptual decisions. The authors show that, when detecting the presence of tactile stimuli, mouse primary somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decisions through the midbrain superior colliculus, primarily by shifting decision bias rather than the ability to detect the stimulus.

title: H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
abstract:
Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) cause aggressive DMGs by preventing radial glial progenitor cell differentiation into oligodendrocytes. Here, the authors show that the transcription factor ASCL1 works with K27M to guide BRG1, maintaining cells in an oligodendrocyte precursor state. 
 Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) drive aggressive diffuse midline gliomas by blocking differentiation of radial glial progenitor cells committed to oligodendrogenesis. We establish prolonged differentiation as a powerful tool to uncover regulators of glioma cell states and demonstrate that the pioneer transcription factor (TF) ASCL1 is a key mediator of H3K27M-driven plasticity and tumorigenesis. H3K27M prevents Polycomb silencing of ASCL1, co-opting this TF to maintain oligodendroglial progenitor states. Consistently, ASCL1 loss drastically impairs tumor formation in vivo. Mechanistically, ASCL1 synergizes with H3K27M to redistribute the chromatin remodeler BRG1 to regulatory elements co-enriched for ASCL1 and SOX motifs, promoting expression of stem and neural progenitor genes at the expense of mesenchymal genes in DMGs. ASCL1 loss acts as a “fire exit”, enabling alternative differentiation despite H3K27M, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting stalled differentiation and tumor plasticity in histone-mutant gliomas and cancers with a stem cell hierarchy. Here, the authors show that the transcription factor ASCL1 works with K27M to guide BRG1, maintaining cells in an oligodendrocyte precursor state.

title: Transposable element-mediated structural variations shape gene expression and agronomic trait diversity in Brassica napus
abstract:
This study develops a comprehensive pan-genome resource for Brassica napus and reveals how structural variations shape gene regulation and seed quality traits. The findings provide insights into genome diversity and crop improvement. 
 Brassica napus is a globally important allotetraploid oilseed crop with a complex genome and extensive structural diversity that remains incompletely characterized. Here, we present gap-free reference genome assemblies for Zhongshuang 11 (ZS11) and Westar, and assemble six additional accessions. We harmonize gene annotations across 22 genomes and develop BnaScope (https://rgmi.hzau.edu.cn/bnascope), a gene-centric functional genomics platform. Gene-based and graph-based pan-genomes identify 123,107 non-redundant gene clusters and 188,218 structural variants, including 112,417 transposable element-mediated structural variants (TEMSVs). TEMSVs show asymmetric distributions between An and Cn subgenomes and are associated with increased homoeolog expression imbalance, particularly for CDS-TEMSVs. SV-based genome-wide association analyses identify candidate genes underlying seed quality traits, and functional analyses demonstrate that BnaPYRDs negatively regulate seed glucosinolate content. These findings establish structural variation as an important contributor to homoeolog regulation and seed-quality variation in B. napus. This study develops a comprehensive pan-genome resource for Brassica napus and reveals how structural variations shape gene regulation and seed quality traits. The findings provide insights into genome diversity and crop improvement.

title: Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
abstract:
Mentalising is essential for social interaction and is thought to rely on the medial prefrontal cortex. Here, the authors show that damage to the medial prefrontal cortex leaves mentalising intact but alters how quickly people make social decisions. 
 Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact. title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
abstract:
Dinosaurs coexisted with flowering plants, but it’s unclear whether they ate them. The study presents a new small theropod dinosaur with remarkable jaw adaptations for eating fruit, providing one of the strongest evidence of dinosaur-angiosperm interaction. 
 The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi—the first for the clade—reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit—which shaped early Cenozoic flora—remains unclear. Dinosaurs coexisted with flowering plants, but it’s unclear whether they ate them. The study presents a new small theropod dinosaur with remarkable jaw adaptations for eating fruit, providing one of the strongest evidence of dinosaur-angiosperm interaction.

title: Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation
abstract:
Fuel cells rely on catalysts made of metal nanoparticles, but tracking how these particles wear down individually has been difficult. Here, the authors build an automated image analysis pipeline to track hundreds of platinum-cobalt nanoparticles and classify the degradation pathways they undergo. 
 Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale. title: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis is concomitant with reduced metacognitive efficiency and sensitivity across multiple cohorts and modalities
abstract:
Corpus collosum dysgenesis is an umbrella term for all congenital malformations of the corpus callosum. Here, the authors show that corpus callosum dysgenesis is associated with intact visual perception but impaired metacognition. 
 The corpus callosum is the largest commissure in the mammalian brain and has been implicated in supporting cognitive processes required for adapting to complex environments. Individuals born with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis, characterized by malformations of the corpus callosum, commonly exhibit deficits in social navigation, abstract problem-solving, decision-making, and self-awareness. Metacognition is a key cognitive process that supports these functions; however, it has yet to be tested comprehensively in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis. Over three experiments, and three Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis cohorts, we examine perceptual accuracy, confidence judgments, and metacognitive efficiency in individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis using two variants of a Random Dot Kinematogram task within lab, online, and virtual reality conditions. We find that individuals with Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis typically display normal perceptual accuracy but fail to adjust their confidence judgments in line with task difficulty. Computational modeling reveal that this difference is characterized by lower metacognitive efficiency concomitant with lower metacognitive sensitivity. Together, these results provide evidence that the corpus callosum is consistently associated with reduced metacognitive efficiency. Corpus collosum dysgenesis is an umbrella term for all congenital malformations of the corpus callosum. Here, the authors show that corpus callosum dysgenesis is associated with intact visual perception but impaired metacognition.

title: Limited agricultural gains but high flood risk from global wetland reclamation
abstract:
As food demand increases, global wetlands are being reclaimed as croplands; however, these reclaimed croplands are not only less productive, but also face substantially higher flood exposure. This dual vulnerability highlights the urgency of balancing food security with wetland conservation. 
 In recent decades, wetland reclamation for agricultural cultivation has remained as one solution to meet rising food demand; however, its agricultural benefits and broader sustainability implications are poorly understood. Here we identify wetland-reclaimed croplands (WRC) globally from 2000 to 2022 and assess their crop production performance and flood exposure risk. Results show that nearly half of WRC exhibited lower crop yields than existing croplands, especially when cultivated with upland crops. WRC contributed only 0.1% to total crop production, yet more than half faced severe flood hazards, with an average flood exposure probability 23 times higher than that of all croplands. Globally, 60% of WRC are subject to dual vulnerabilities of limited agricultural gains and high flood exposure, especially in food-importing or low-income countries. These findings reveal the unsustainability of wetland reclamation as an agricultural expansion strategy and underscore the pressing need to reconcile food security with wetland conservation. As food demand increases, global wetlands are being reclaimed as croplands; however, these reclaimed croplands are not only less productive, but also face substantially higher flood exposure. This dual vulnerability highlights the urgency of balancing food security with wetland conservation.

title: Onset of zircon decomposition during saprolitic weathering
abstract:
Zircon is altered during saprolitic weathering through dissolution-precipitation reactions, during which U, Th, and REEs are incorporated into the zircon structure, enhancing metamictization and facilitating progressive zircon dissolution, according to geochemical analysis. 
 Zircon is conventionally considered as refractory in supergene environments, enabling the preservation of geochemical records for tracing various Earth’s processes and the use of the zircon structure as a nuclear waste form. However, how refractory zircon is during weathering, especially when crystalline and in an early stage of weathering, is unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that crystalline zircon would start to weather during an early-stage saprolitic weathering. Nano-scale examination reveals that weathering of zircon proceeds through dissolution of primary, crystalline zircon and precipitation of secondary, amorphous zircon. Non-formula elements, like U, Th and heavy rare earth elements, are uptake and structurally incorporated in this process. Thereby, metamictisation of the zircon would accelerate and eventually promote the dissolution of zircon. In supergene environments, zircon would steadily weather, calling for further evaluation on the geological and environmental applications of zircon. title: Assessing the potential and cost of enhanced rock weathering in China
abstract:
Enhanced rock weathering contributes 5 to 30 percent of China’s negative emissions needs by 2060 at a net cost of 127 to 226 dollars per tonne of carbon dioxide removed, according to a spatially explicit grid-level analysis of croplands using basalt application scenarios 
 Large-scale carbon dioxide removal is essential for carbon neutrality, but current options face constraints. Enhanced rock weathering is a promising alternative, yet its viability at a national scale in China remains unquantified. Here we show, using a spatially explicit analysis across China’s croplands, that a single-year basalt application could remove 0.44–0.79 billion tonnes of CO2 by 2100, at a net life-cycle-adjusted cost of 127–226 US dollars per tonne of CO2 removed. Particles finer than those typically used commercially provide the most favorable balance between removal potential and cost. Multi-year application has the potential to contribute 5–30% of China’s negative emissions needs by 2060, with priority areas in Northeast, Central-South, and East China. As an initial spatially resolved assessment, this study supports considering enhanced rock weathering in China’s carbon-management portfolio and motivates field trials and coupled soil–river geochemical modeling to constrain weathering, downstream carbon retention, and losses. title: TreeMap 2020, 2022, and 2023: Improved species range mapping in a tree-level forest dataset for the conterminous United States
abstract:
New TreeMap datasets provide imputed 30 m gridded maps with modeled tree-level detail for forests across the conterminous United States in 2020, 2022, and 2023. Updated methods improve climate data inputs, independent validation approaches, and species range mapping. These improvements strengthen TreeMap’s use in Earth system applications such as carbon cycling, wildfire behavior, and habitat distribution modeling, which depend on accurate representations of forest composition and structure. 
 TreeMap is a tree-level model of the forests of the conterminous United States (CONUS) that provides a spatially continuous, 30 m resolution representation of forest structure and composition. It uses a random forests imputation approach to assign the most similar Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) plot to each forested pixel in gridded LANDFIRE data based on a suite of predictor variables that include vegetation, topographic, biophysical, and disturbance characteristics. By linking every mapped pixel to an FIA plot identifier for all forested areas in CONUS, TreeMap bridges localized inventory measurements with national-scale analyses and provides high-resolution estimates of forest structure and composition. In this update, TreeMap 2020, 2022, and 2023 incorporate climatic variables from Daymet in place of LANDFIRE biophysical variables. Further, we refined the independent validation by limiting the analysis to FIA plots where heterogeneity was administrative rather than ecological, excluding plots previously used to validate TreeMap versions that spanned heterogeneous forest conditions.  TreeMap 2020, 2022, and 2023 also implement a new process constraining the pool of FIA plots available for imputation within each LANDFIRE zone to species documented within that zone and its adjacent zones, thereby reducing implausible species assignments across CONUS. TreeMap 2020, 2022, and 2023 are publicly available at https://doi.org/10.2737/RDS-2025-0031 (Zimmer et al., 2025) and https://doi.org/10.2737/RDS-2025-0032 (Houtman et al., 2025), and https://doi.org/10.2737/RDS-2026-0038 (Zimmer et al., 2026), respectively.

title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
abstract:
A method developed to directly measure fungal melanin in soil, reveals a strong link between melanin and soil carbon and providing evidence for its role in long-term carbon stabilization 
 Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization. A method developed to directly measure fungal melanin in soil, reveals a strong link between melanin and soil carbon and providing evidence for its role in long-term carbon stabilization

title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
abstract:
Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems. 
 Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. We further show that these trends in Atlantic NICs are primarily driven by changes in near-inertial wind forcing, particularly those associated with mesoscale weather systems, while variations in mixed-layer depth playing a minor role. This observed intensification of Atlantic NICs may have important implications for ocean transport and mixing, and needs to be properly represented in the current generation of climate models. Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems.

title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
abstract:
Authors show in 2013-2023 France saw a substantial reduction in hepatitis C virus prevalence and incidence among people who use drugs. Widespread treatment and harm reduction drove the decline, bringing France closer to WHO 2030 elimination targets. 
 Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions. Authors show in 2013-2023 France saw a substantial reduction in hepatitis C virus prevalence and incidence among people who use drugs. Widespread treatment and harm reduction drove the decline, bringing France closer to WHO 2030 elimination targets.

title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
abstract:
Existing approaches for biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) discovery are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that an automated platform for one-step assembly and refactoring of BGCs facilitates facile novel product discovery. 
 Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that OSAR (One-Step Assembly and Refactoring)—an automated platform integrating algorithmic primer design with yeast homologous-recombination cloning—directly assembles and refactors NRPS clusters without custom DNA synthesis. We apply OSAR to 34 low- to medium-GC bacterial NRPS clusters (7–78 kb) and successfully assemble 31. Expression in Bacillus subtilis yields 29 peptides from 10 clusters. Several products arose from cryptic biosynthetic behaviors such as potential module skipping and premature release. OSAR provides a practical workflow for assembly and refactoring of NRPS clusters and may facilitate the translation of sequence information into natural products. title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
abstract:
Sub-nanometer heterostructures offer opportunities to tune interfacial reactivity, but their precise construction remains challenging. Here, the authors report alternating Ni/NiMoO₄ heterostructures that promote hydrogen evolution and sustain durable high-current electrolysis. 
 Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. Oleylamine ligands adsorbed on NiMoO4 sub-nanowires act as mild reductants, selectively reducing Ni2+ to spatially confined metallic Ni domains and forming coherent Ni/NiMoO4 heterointerfaces. Experimental and theoretical analyses suggest that the Ni/NiMoO4 interfaces modify the local electronic structure and facilitate the adsorption and activation of hydrogen evolution intermediates. The resulting catalyst requires an overpotential of 14.4 ± 2.9 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and delivers 2 A cm−2 at 1.62 V in an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer at 80 oC, with stable operation over 2200 h at 25 °C. These findings provide insights into the construction and interfacial regulation of sub-nanometer heterostructures through in situ reduction. Sub-nanometer heterostructures offer opportunities to tune interfacial reactivity, but their precise construction remains challenging. Here, the authors report alternating Ni/NiMoO₄ heterostructures that promote hydrogen evolution and sustain durable high-current electrolysis.

title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
abstract:
Adaptive radiations produce striking phenotypic diversity over remarkably short evolutionary timescales. This study uses genomic analyses of Darwin’s tree finches to reveal a cryptic lineage, in which autosomal differentiation with another sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus (G03) that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. 
 Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin’s finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We identify several highly differentiated loci, including G03, a supergene affecting beak and body size. We reveal a striking example of genomic mosaicism, in which autosomal differentiation between two sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus -(G03)- that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. Contextualized in a broader phylogenetic framework, we also reveal an unexpected diversity of G03 haplotypes and show that the small and large G03 alleles diverged early in the radiation, suggesting a key genetic innovation enabling ecological expansion among species of Darwin’s finches. Our results further establish Camarhynchus as a model example of speciation with gene flow, underscoring the broader role of hybridization in generating biodiversity. Adaptive radiations produce striking phenotypic diversity over remarkably short evolutionary timescales. title: Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
abstract:
The authors use two deep-learning methods for RESOLFT nanoscopy: HDN denoising enables five-fold longer live-cell imaging, while spatial upsampling with temporal context restores subsampled data for fourfold higher frame rates and reduced artifacts. 
 Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation. The authors use two deep-learning methods for RESOLFT nanoscopy: HDN denoising enables five-fold longer live-cell imaging, while spatial upsampling with temporal context restores subsampled data for fourfold higher frame rates and reduced artifacts.

title: Distinct drivers control trace metal distributions through the Atlantic Ocean
abstract:
Transport through water masses formed in high latitudes can explain 60–90% of dissolved trace metal distributions and higher than 75% of trace metal inventories in the interior of the Atlantic Ocean, based on water mass analysis. 
 Trace metals (TMs) including iron, manganese, cobalt, nickel, copper, zinc, cadmium, and lead have important biogeochemical roles in the ocean. However, the controlling factors of TM distributions have not yet been quantified and investigated on an ocean scale. Here we take a holistic approach to demonstrate that transport through water masses formed in high latitudes can explain 60–90% of dissolved TM distributions and >75% of TM inventories in the interior Atlantic. Water mass signatures were slightly modified by sinking organic matter remineralization mainly for iron, cobalt, nickel, cadmium, scavenging removal for iron, manganese, cobalt, lead, and hydrothermal inputs for iron and manganese. Our approach allowed prediction of the baseline TM distributions through the Atlantic at high spatial resolution. Through quantification, our findings emphasize the important role of large-scale oceanic circulation in determining global TM distributions once the water mass endmembers are set, despite the distinctive geochemical behaviors of the assessed TMs. Climate-related changes in a future ocean that impact endmember concentrations or relative water mass contributions may therefore perturb downstream TM inventories and ultimately affect ocean productivity and ocean carbon pump. title: Episodic isolation of the Arctic Mediterranean from the North Atlantic during late Pleistocene glacials
abstract:
Highly dynamic coupling between the Arctic Mediterranean and the North Atlantic during late Pleistocene glaciations; as shown using Beryllium isotopes from sediment cores from the Arctic Ocean, the Nordic Seas and the North Atlantic. 
 It has been proposed that the Arctic Ocean and Nordic Seas (“the Arctic Mediterranean”) were not only episodically covered by an ice shelf during late Pleistocene glaciations, but disconnected from the North Atlantic and filled with freshwater. Originally based on the widespread occurrence of marine sediments with intervals barren of 230Thxs (a function of salinity) and low in cosmogenic 10Be (interpreted as ice cover), this interpretation is highly debated. Alternative explanations state that sediment pulses could instead have diluted both isotopes. Here, we trace the connection between the Arctic Mediterranean and the North Atlantic using reactive 10Be/9Be, a water mass tracer resilient to sedimentation variations. We find uniformly low 10Be/9Be that coincide with the 230Thxs-minima and more than one order of magnitude below the coeval North Atlantic, consistent with an isolated Arctic Mediterranean. Our findings suggest a highly dynamic coupling between the Arctic Mediterranean and the North Atlantic, opening questions about its impact on global climate. title: Impact of climate change on the photovoltaic power potential in Sweden across 21st century
abstract:
Future climate change is projected to increase solar photovoltaic power generation in Sweden by about 5% compared to historical periods, while optimized panel tilt can boost output by 3 to 6%; according to a validated installation model incorporating air temperature, solar radiation, and snow conditions across four cities under future climate scenarios. 
 Solar photovoltaic generation strongly relies on weather conditions, which will be affected by future climate change. Traditional methods for estimating photovoltaic generation potential often overlook detailed installation factors and snow impacts, leading to inaccuracies in high-latitude areas. We assess future photovoltaic system performance in Sweden using a validated photovoltaic installation model that incorporates air temperature, radiation and snow conditions. Applying this model to four Swedish cities under low- and high-emission climate change scenarios and three climate simulations, we project an approximate 5% increase in photovoltaic generation relative to the historical period with optimal installation angle. The combined effects of air temperature and snowfall are as crucial as solar radiation for photovoltaic generation in Sweden, so the photovoltaic generation change will be relatively limited by 2100. Optimized tilt angles are obtained for all the four cities, which could increase photovoltaic generation by 3-6% compared to the commercial angle. The findings also provide valuable insights into photovoltaic potential in a changing climate. title: Revisiting the urban past virtually to enhance well-being for older adults
abstract:
As development progresses, urban landmarks may be lost to history, resulting in the disconnection and isolation of older adults from their contemporary city. Huang and colleagues virtually reconstructed immersive past urban scenes from Hong Kong to understand the physiological and psychological effects and support mental health for aging populations. 
 Cities are more than physical infrastructure; they are dynamic repositories of collective memories. Rapid urbanization, however, threatens to erase cherished landmarks, severing the connection between communities and their history. To address this loss, we created immersive virtual heritage environments based on CITY IN TIME, a digital platform that uses immersive technology to reconstruct 44 iconic Hong Kong landmarks as they existed between 1900 and 1970 from archival sources. Here we demonstrate that a virtual experience of historical Hong Kong significantly enhanced memory recall, reduced stress and increased social connectedness in older adults, supported by consistent physiological and psychological measures. Semi-structured interviews further revealed the multidimensional nature of urban memory, encompassing both tangible places and intangible narratives. Taken together, our findings illustrate how urban heritage can safeguard collective memory and foster community well-being, offering a scalable approach to preserving the layered histories that shape inclusive and emotionally resonant cities. title: Global meta-analysis and machine learning uncover region-specific salinity thresholds and risks for sustainable wheat production under saline irrigation
abstract: Saline irrigation represents a pivotal alternative strategy for enhancing crop production under freshwater scarcity. However, previous assessments have mainly quantified average yield responses, while how interacting environmental and management conditions shape region-specific irrigation-water salinity thresholds and associated spatial risks remain elusive across global major breadbaskets. This study combined a meta-analysis of 551 field observations with machine learning (ML) to quantify global wheat yield responses to saline irrigation, identify optimal region-specific thresholds, and evaluate spatial risks in four major wheat-producing areas: the North China Plain (NCP), Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP), Middle East (ME), and Central California Valley (CCV). Meta-analysis revealed that saline irrigation led to significant average yield reductions ranging from 12.4% in the NCP to 31.4% in the CCV. ML further showed that irrigation water salinity, growing-season temperature, and irrigation amount emerged as the dominant drivers, collectively explaining more than 54% of yield variation. An optimum irrigation amount of 500 mm was optimal for maximizing yield under saline conditions. Region-specific best practices included border irrigation at flowering (FL) and grain-filling stages for the NCP, drip irrigation at these stages for the IGP, and drip irrigation at the FL stage for the ME and CCV. Spatial risk assessment revealed a mismatch between salinity tolerance thresholds and actual exposure. Under a conservative 5% yield-loss scenario, the IGP exhibited the highest model-derived salinity threshold of 4.14 dS m−1 but the largest risk area proportion due to elevated background salinity, whereas the ME faced the lowest risk, with a risk area of 7.7%, indicating high potential for saline water utilization. These findings highlight the limitations of universal water quality guidelines and demonstrate the necessity of localized management. By establishing a data-driven framework, this study provides actionable insights to safeguard global wheat supply, build climate resilience, and ensure agricultural sustainability in salt-affected environments.

title: Atlas of geochemical, petrophysical and mechanical rock properties of the crystalline basement in Germany – first release
abstract:
The AMPEDEK database is the first standardized, open-access database of rock properties for Germany's crystalline basement. By combining published data with new laboratory measurements, it provides 25,700 petrophysical and mechanical data points, as well as geochemical and mineralogical data, from more than 8,200 samples collected across eight federal states. The database supports preliminary reservoir assessments and future exploration campaigns for a wide range of geological applications. 
 A comprehensive and statistically robust understanding of rock characteristics is essential for reservoir characterization of the deep subsurface to accurately plan exploration campaigns, parameterize predictive 3D geological models, interpret geophysical data, and execute numerical thermo-hydraulic-mechanical-chemical simulations, thereby reducing economic risks and project uncertainties. Despite growing interest in the crystalline basement in Germany for e.g., geothermal energy applications and the safe storage of high-radioactive nuclear waste, systematic datasets covering the major crystalline and metamorphic basement units and their physiomechanical characteristics remain scarce, fragmented, or lack the metadata required for robust evaluation. To address this data gap, the AMPEDEK project established a unified, multi-scale national reference database for geochemical, petrophysical, and mechanical rock properties of crystalline rocks in Germany. The framework integrated extensive literature reviews, data from geological surveys, and newly conducted sampling and measurement campaigns, linking metadata, geochemistry, petrography, and physiomechanical rock properties through unique sample IDs.

title: marinedb: An open-source, flexible and scalable Python workflow for curating, standardizing, and integrating marine biodiversity data
abstract:
Knowing where marine species live helps us understand and protect ocean life, but the underlying records are spread across sources, vary widely in how they were collected, described, and formatted, and are affected by data-quality issues. We developed marinedb, an open tool for cleaning biodiversity data, and used it to build a global dataset of nearly 159 million records covering more than 139,000 species, making large-scale studies of marine species distributions easier and more reproducible. 
 The digital era and the emergence of data-aggregation initiatives have greatly expanded access to biodiversity occurrence records, but accessibility alone does not ensure usability for ecological modeling. Marine occurrence data must be cleaned and reconciled across spatial, temporal, and taxonomic dimensions before they can be reliably linked to environmental predictors and used to model species distributions. Here, we introduce marinedb, an open-source, modular, and scalable Python package for curating marine occurrence data. The package provides a suite of tools that can be freely combined into user-defined workflows tailored to study objectives and data characteristics. We applied marinedb to three major biodiversity resources: the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF), the Ocean Biogeographic Information System (OBIS), and the Jellyfish Database Initiative (JeDI). Together, these resources span hundreds of millions of occurrence records located at sea and more than one hundred thousand species. First, we used the framework to assess data quality non-destructively across the three sources. The analysis revealed substantial and source-dependent issues, including records located on land, missing depth information, heterogeneous, incomplete, or low-precision temporal information, records lacking species-level information or referring to non-marine taxa, weak or unspecified evidential support, absence records, and strong taxonomic imbalance. Second, we applied a tailored dataset-production workflow to produce a ready-to-use global marine occurrence dataset for large-scale modeling of present-day species distributions, which comprises 158,910,536 records representing 139,844 species. Together, the reusable Python tools and the curated dataset derived from GBIF, OBIS, and JeDI lower the technical barrier for multi-species and deep-learning approaches, both of which require extensive and diverse occurrence records, while preserving flexibility for future use-case-specific curation.

title: A High-Resolution Gridded Dataset of Vertically Resolved Fine Root Biomass Across China
abstract:
Fine roots help plants take up water and nutrients and store carbon in soil. We developed a dataset showing the vertical distribution of fine roots across China from 2005–2025. Using thousands of field measurements and environmental data, we mapped root biomass in 20 cm layers down to 2 m. The dataset reveals strong differences in root distribution among regions and plant types and provides a new resource for understanding belowground carbon storage and ecosystem change. 
 Fine root plays a critical role in ecosystem biogeochemical cycles, serving as the primary organs for water and nutrient uptake and exhibiting rapid turnover. However, a spatially explicit dataset of fine root biomass (FRB) across soil profiles and vegetation types remains lacking. To address this knowledge gap, we compiled 2,311 in-situ measurements of woody FRB and 3,580 measurements of herbaceous FRB from peer-reviewed studies across China. Using these observations, we developed random forest models to estimate surface-layer (0–20 cm) FRB and the vertical attenuation coefficient (k) of FRB for woody and herbaceous ecosystems, respectively. By integrating the predicted surface-layer FRB and vertical distribution functions, we finally generated a gridded dataset of FRB across 0–2 m soil depth (at 20 cm intervals) at 1 km spatial resolution for all woody and herbaceous ecosystems in China for 2005–2025. Model evaluation showed that our models explain approximately 86 % and 81 % of the observed variations in surface FRB across woody and herbaceous ecosystems, respectively, and reasonablely capture the interannual dynamics of observed FRB. Model predictions reveal substantial spatial and vertical variations in both woody and herbaceous FRB across China. Woody FRB density was generally higher in southern China than in central and northern China, whereas herbaceous FRB density was highest on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. Woody plants exhibit deeper root distributions in arid regions, whereas herbaceous species show consistently surface-concentrated rooting patterns across climate zones. The environmental controls of FRB also differed between vegetation types, with woody FRB being more strongly influenced by root traits and nutrient availability, whereas herbaceous FRB was more closely associated with climatic conditions. This dataset provides an observation-constrained, spatially explicit benchmark for quantifying belowground carbon stocks and dynamics, and it is archived and publicly available at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.32353257 (Zheng et al., 2026).

title: Improving the CLASSIC (v1.8) snow model  to better simulate Arctic snowpacks
abstract:
This study enhances a snow model for Arctic environments by improving the heat exchanges within the snowpack and at its interfaces, revising the compaction scheme, and adding consideration of blowing snow sublimation losses. Simulations at ten Arctic, mid-latitude, and Alpine sites show significant reductions in simulated soil and snow temperature biases and improved simulated snow depth and density, which are key features to improve simulated energy, water, and carbon budgets in the Arctic. 
 This study enhances the snow model of the Canadian Land Surface Scheme including Biogeochemical Cycles (CLASSIC), with a particular focus on Arctic environments. Key snow model physics improvements include adjustments to the thermal conductivity at the top of the first soil layer, a revised computation of the temperature at the snow–soil interface (hereafter, bottom snow temperature), and the addition of a windless exchange coefficient in sensible heat flux calculations. Arctic-specific adaptations include blowing-snow sublimation losses, a new snow compaction scheme, and snow thermal conductivity parameterization. Evaluations at seven mid-latitude and alpine sites (SnowMIP sites) and three Arctic sites (Bylot Island, Umiujaq, and Trail Valley Creek) show that these enhancements improve the overall simulated snowpack characteristics and soil temperatures across both SnowMIP and Arctic sites. The revised bottom snow temperature yields better agreement between simulated and observed snow and bottom snow temperatures. The new windless exchange coefficient reduced the surface temperature RMSE from 3.50 to 1.93 °C on average across all sites. The improved snow compaction scheme reduces the snow depth biases from 12.0 to 0.1 cm on average across the Arctic sites and improves the simulated snow densities while not degrading the overall model performance at the SnowMIP sites. Blowing-snow sublimation had a negligible effect at most sites, except at the wind-exposed sites of Umiujaq, Trail Valley Creek, and Senator Beck, decreasing snow depth on average by 2–4 cm. Adding a new snow thermal conductivity parameterization – combined with all previous developments – reduces the RMSE of the simulated soil temperatures from 5.3 to 3.0 °C on average at all Arctic sites. Our new developments demonstrate the ability of a single-layer snow model to reasonably reproduce Arctic bulk snowpack characteristics, while maintaining good performance at the SnowMIP sites. Inherent uncertainties remain in the forcing datasets, especially due to the harsh Arctic environment characterized by strong winds, snow redistribution, frost, and polar night. Future model developments will focus on spatial-scale simulations across the whole Arctic, with particular attention to snow cover fraction parameterizations to better capture sub-grid-scale spatial heterogeneity in Arctic environments.

title: Towards high-fidelity simulations of coastal submesoscale  baroclinic instabilities with MPAS–O (vE3SM3.0.0)  – Part 2: Realistic experiments
abstract:
River plumes can strongly influence coastal dynamics but are poorly resolved in global ocean models. Building on a companion study, we perform high-resolution simulations of the Mississippi–Atchafalaya (M–A) plume with the Model for Prediction Across Scales–Ocean (MPAS–O), a global model, and compare with a limited-domain Regional Ocean Modeling System configuration. MPAS–O qualitatively captures the M–A plume seasonality but fails to generate realistic eddies on the Texas–Louisiana shelf. 
 River plumes can strongly influence coastal dynamics but are poorly represented in global ocean models due to stringent resolution requirements. Following the idealized simulations presented in a companion paper (Hinson et al., 2026), this study presents submesoscale-permitting realistic simulations using unprecedented regional refinement with MPAS–O. We assess MPAS–O's ability to represent river plume dynamics by comparing with a validated ROMS configuration focused on the Mississippi–Atchafalaya (M–A) plume in the northern Gulf of Mexico (GoM). The variable-resolution mesh spans 1.4 km in the GoM to 100 km in the Pacific and Indian Oceans. We incorporate several improvements to the representation of river forcing in MPAS–O: the pseudo point source treatment of runoff, river temperature prescribed from air temperature, and passive tracers to track freshwater transport. MPAS–O generates vigorous submesoscales in the open GoM, as quantified by probability density functions of surface relative vorticity and divergence. While the model qualitatively captures the M–A plume's seasonal evolution, it does not realistically reproduce the summer submesoscale eddy field on the Texas–Louisiana shelf. A persistent brackish lens associated with reduced vertical mixing forms and is present throughout the M–A plume. We hypothesize that this arises from interacting parameterization and structural design choices within MPAS–O that affect plume stratification and instability growth under realistic forcing, rather than from deficiencies in numerics. Our results demonstrate MPAS–O's potential for simulating submesoscale processes in the open ocean while highlighting challenges in using regional refinement to model coastal dynamics.

title: Antiviral immunity via telomerase-like reverse transcription in bacteria
abstract:
Antiviral immunity via telomerase-like reverse transcription in bacteria 
 Defense-associated reverse transcriptases (DRTs) employ diverse and distinctive mechanisms of cDNA synthesis to protect bacteria against viral infection1. However, the functions and mechanisms of many DRTs remain unknown2. Here we identify a new antiviral defense system, DRT10, that associates with a noncoding RNA (ncRNA) to catalyze processive, protein-primed synthesis of tandem-repeat DNA. Reverse transcription is templated by a defined ncRNA region with a characteristic sequence pattern and template boundary elements, both of which are conserved and essential for DNA repeat addition. Cryo-EM reconstructions reveal an unanticipated 2:1 architecture, wherein two RT monomers bind opposite sides of a pseudo-symmetric ncRNA. Biochemical experiments further demonstrate that each RT monomer reverse transcribes the template encoded on its respective side of the ncRNA, but only one generates the long repetitive product, whose template is defined by the distance between two flanking stem-loop anchors. This mode of iterative, boundary-delimited cDNA synthesis exhibits direct parallels to the mechanism of telomeric repeat addition by eukaryotic telomerase, and phylogenetic analyses of RTs across domains of life place telomerase in a monophyletic clade with the DRT family, suggesting a common origin for their DNA polymerization activities. Together with earlier studies of DRT2, DRT3, and DRT93–5, our findings identify a conserved mechanistic logic underlying RNA-templated DNA repeat addition across diverse DRTs, despite vastly different architectural solutions, and expand the repertoire of reverse transcription-based strategies for antiviral immunity in bacteria.

title: Continuous-time noise mitigation in analogue quantum simulation
abstract:
Mitigating errors in analogue quantum simulators - that is, reducing noise-induced bias in expectation values - would greatly improve their operation and scalability. Here, the authors propose a time-continuous error cancellation protocol, based on introducing an auxiliary system and engineering the joint dissipation of the new, extended system. 
 Analogue quantum simulators offer a promising route to explore quantum many-body dynamics beyond classical reach in the near term. However, their vulnerability to noise limits the accuracy of simulations. Here, we establish a continuous-time framework for mitigating noise in analogue quantum simulation. Our protocol fully preserves the continuous-time nature by avoiding any active control or measurement of the system during the dynamics, while achieving exact noise cancellation. This requires a small number of ancillary qubits, whose interaction with the system, combined with classical post-processing of joint measurement data, is tailored to cancel the effect of noise. Furthermore, the protocol is Hamiltonian-independent and robust to realistic ancilla noise. This work points to a promising direction for achieving high-fidelity analogue quantum simulation in the presence of noise. title: Neuronal signatures of successful one-shot memory in mid-level visual cortex
abstract:
Neural mechanisms underlying one-shot memory are not fully understood. In this study, macaque monkeys were trained to perform a continuous image recognition task and simultaneously recorded from groups of neurons in area V4. The authors found that the perceptual building blocks of fast, high-capacity memory are present in mid-level sensory cortex. 
 High-capacity, one-shot visual recognition memory challenges theories of learning and neural coding because it requires rapid, robust, and durable representations. Most studies have focused on the hippocampus and other higher areas. However, behavioral evidence demonstrating links between image properties and memorability and revealing image specificity of visual memory suggests an important role for mid-level visual cortex. We tested the hypothesis that area V4 contains signals critical for recognition memory in two male rhesus macaques. Our task increased difficulty, allowing comparisons of neuronal population responses on correct and error trials. We observed signatures of several proposed memory mechanisms including magnitude coding, repetition suppression, sparse coding, and population response consistency, but only sparse coding and population response consistency predicted behavior. Familiar images also evoked faster dynamics, consistent with pattern completion. These findings demonstrate that fast, high-capacity memory is supported by neural codes in mid-level sensory cortex independent of stimulus features per se, highlighting its role in distributed memory networks. title: The mechanosensitive PIEZO1 channel promotes CD54<sup>+</sup>/iNOS<sup>+</sup> neutrophil expansion in pulmonary fibrosis
abstract:
Neutrophils have been shown to be involved in pulmonary fibrosis (PF). Here, the authors identify an expanded pro-inflammatory neutrophil state marked by CD54 in human PF and by iNOS in murine PF, demonstrate that iNOS+ neutrophils promote PF whilst Arg+ neutrophils are less effective, and show that mechanical activation of the PIEZO1 channel contributes to the promotion of PF by CD54 + /iNOS+ neutrophils. 
 Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) represents the common end-stage outcome of a broad range of interstitial lung diseases. The shared pathophysiologic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify two phenotypically distinct neutrophil subsets in PF: a pro-inflammatory subset characterized by CD54 (human) or iNOS (mouse) expression, and an alternative subset marked by Arg1 expression. Notably, CD54+ and iNOS+ neutrophils were markedly expanded in PF patients and mice with bleomycin-induced PF, respectively. Adoptive transfer of iNOS+ neutrophils exacerbated fibrosis in bleomycin-induced PF, whereas transfer of Arg1+ neutrophils had no significant effect. Further, the expression of PIEZO1, a mechanically activated ion channel, is predominantly upregulated in CD54+ neutrophils from PF patients or iNOS+ neutrophils from PF mice. Piezo1 ablation in neutrophils selectively impairs iNOS+ neutrophil differentiation, thereby attenuating fibrosis progression. Mechanistically, PIEZO1 promotes the differentiation of these pro-inflammatory subsets through the transcription factor IRF4 in a calcium-dependent manner. We further identify the JAK/STAT pathway as an upstream regulator of PIEZO1 expression in neutrophils. Consequently, PIEZO1 expression and CD54+ neutrophils are markedly decreased in patients treated with JAK inhibitor baricitinib. Importantly, combined inhibition of JAK/STAT and calcium signaling exerts synergistic suppression on the iNOS+ neutrophil expansion and PF progression. Together, our findings reveal a mechanism in which PIEZO1 promotes PF by specifically driving the expansion of CD54+/iNOS+ neutrophils. title: Serine-65 phosphorylated ubiquitin associates with soluble tau and seeding activity in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract:
Not all selective markers of seeding-competent Tau are known. Here, the authors identify pS65-Ub-associated tau linked to pathological Tau spreading and elevated in Alzheimer’s disease. Removal of pS65-Ub reduces tau seeding activity. 
 Tau propagation is a key driver of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet selective markers of seeding-competent tau remain elusive. Ubiquitin phosphorylated at Serine-65 (pS65-Ub) is a PINK1-derived cellular stress signal that accumulates in AD with elevated tau pathology, but its relationship to tau seeding is unknown. Here, using postmortem brain tissue from female and male donors, we show that a subset of tau is covalently modified by pS65-Ub in AD brain. The pS65-Ub-associated tau population is elevated in AD and is enriched in soluble, high-molecular-weight, oligomeric, and hyperphosphorylated tau species. Across AD cases, soluble pS65-Ub-associated tau levels strongly correlate with tau seeding activity. Tau species isolated with pS65-Ub antibodies exhibit seeding activity, whereas removal of pS65-Ub-associated material markedly reduces seeding from AD brain extracts. Together, these findings identify pS65-Ub as a disease-enriched molecular feature of a seed-competent tau population and link cellular stress signaling with pathological tau propagation in AD. Not all selective markers of seeding-competent Tau are known. Here, the authors identify pS65-Ub-associated tau linked to pathological Tau spreading and elevated in Alzheimer’s disease. Removal of pS65-Ub reduces tau seeding activity.

title: Interpretable AI-guided discovery of degradable ionizable lipids with enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery in vivo
abstract:
Ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical. Here, the authors integrate interpretable machine learning with modular degradable lipid chemistry to prioritize candidates for experimental testing and identify a lead lipid for hepatic mRNA delivery. 
 Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable RNA medicines, yet ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical, particularly when in vitro activity must be translated into functional hepatic delivery in vivo. Here we establish an interpretable discovery framework that combines modular degradable lipid chemistry, high-throughput phenotyping, machine learning, virtual library expansion, and independent in vivo validation to define a learnable ionizable-lipid design space. Starting from a 520-member library, we train an XGBoost model on firefly luciferase (Fluc) expression in HeLa cells and use physicochemical descriptors and molecular fingerprints to prospectively prioritize candidates with higher predicted in vitro transfection activity across a 10,920-member virtual space. In vivo phenotyping subsequently identifies PA97MD101 as a lead ionizable lipid. In mice, PA97MD101 enhances hepatic mRNA expression and Cre-dependent recombination and supports Cas9/sgTtr-mediated TTR suppression. Its performance is associated with pH-dependent membrane activity and reduced lysosomal colocalization. These findings support further evaluation of PA97MD101 for functional hepatic RNA delivery. Here, the authors integrate interpretable machine learning with modular degradable lipid chemistry to prioritize candidates for experimental testing and identify a lead lipid for hepatic mRNA delivery.

title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation
abstract:
What is the mechanism by which ClpXP utilizes ATP to unfold proteins? Using single-molecule, biochemical and structural methods, the authors find that the central coupler facilitates the conversion of chemical energy into a quick motion of substrate translocating loops to generate force. 
 ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor. What is the mechanism by which ClpXP utilizes ATP to unfold proteins? Using single-molecule, biochemical and structural methods, the authors find that the central coupler facilitates the conversion of chemical energy into a quick motion of substrate translocating loops to generate force.
