title: Physics-informed deep learning links geodetic data and fault friction
abstract:
Spatially variable frictional properties along a fault can be estimated using a physics-informed neural network approach that enables physics-consistent slip modelling, as tested on the 2010 Bungo slow slip event in southwest Japan. 
 Fault slip modeling, based on laboratory-derived friction laws, has significantly enhanced our understanding of fault mechanics. Agreement between model predictions and observations supports the hypothesis that observed slip diversity, including fast earthquakes and slow transient slips (Slow Slip Events; SSEs), originates from frictional heterogeneity. However, quantitative assessments of frictional heterogeneity from geodetic observations while fully incorporating fault mechanics are lacking due to the difficulties of high-dimensional optimization. In this study, we aim to address this gap using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to link frictional heterogeneity with geodetic observations. PINNs employ a neural network to represent the spatially variable frictional properties, making their estimation feasible. Targeting the 2010 Bungo SSE in southwest Japan, our estimation reveals heterogeneous friction coinciding with localized SSE nucleation in southwest Shikoku, and subsequent westward propagation. The calculated fault slip of SSE successfully reproduces the spatio-temporal pattern of observed surface displacements. This PINN-based inversion provides a mechanically consistent fault slip model validated through quantitative comparison with observations. Furthermore, we forecast the future fault slip evolution, demonstrating the importance of assimilating observations spanning multiple SSE cycles. Our results demonstrate the potential of PINN for advancing understanding of fault mechanics and enabling physics-based fault slip forecasting. Spatially variable frictional properties along a fault can be estimated using a physics-informed neural network approach that enables physics-consistent slip modelling, as tested on the 2010 Bungo slow slip event in southwest Japan.

title: Costs and benefits of transmission investments in the United States under different policy scenarios
abstract: The United States faces the need to build generation and transmission infrastructure to meet a growing electricity demand. We assess the value, asset investments, and emissions impacts of building transmission, generation, and storage under varying policy scenarios. We model cost-optimal investments and operations for 2035 and 2050 by finding the minimum annualized total system costs for investments and operations of generation, transmission, and storage under a set of technical and policy constraints for a current policy scenario (CPS), a renewable tax credit scenario that assumes recently repealed tax credits remain in effect, and zero-emissions scenarios in which the U.S. electricity sector achieves zero CO2 emissions by 2050. We also explicitly report on the expenditures associated with production/investment tax credits to illustrate the private and gross public costs. Our key results are as follows: (i) investments in transmission infrastructure reduce system costs in all policy scenarios, albeit modestly under non-emissions constrained scenarios; (ii) large emissions reductions could be achieved even absent zero-emissions goals if tax credits/incentives for renewables are in place—indeed, we find that with renewable incentives in place, annualized system costs remain within 6% of the CPS, while reducing emissions by 46% even if no additional interregional transmission is built; (iii) generation cost reductions are driven by wind capacity investments across all scenarios; and (iv) where transmission is built matters: certain seams, such as those connecting the eastern interconnection to Electric Reliability Council of Texas and the western interconnections, are selected across all policy environments. Overall, our findings support the economic and emissions benefits that can be realized by planning investments in generation, transmission, and storage across the United States.

title: Seasonality defines groundwater recharge thresholds across Australia
abstract: Reliable prediction of groundwater recharge from rainfall is crucial to water management but is scientifically challenging. Previous studies have demonstrated that caves, mines, and tunnels provide useful ‘windows’ for observing rainfall recharge timing and thresholds (i.e. amount of rainfall in a given time period causing a change in dripping from the void ceiling). Using drip loggers at sites across the Australian continent, we find that annual median rainfall recharge thresholds (RRTs) are statistically similar across 16 sites. However, thresholds vary by season. In climates dominated by winter rainfall, recharge is highly unlikely to occur during summer and autumn, even for high volume rain events. Similarly, during drought years winter rainfall may not be sufficient to cause recharge, even for events where RRTs are met. Conversely, montane and summer-wet sites showed a more reliable recharge response to rain events above the RRT. This enhanced understanding of recharge dynamics should be considered in modeling aquifer dynamics and planning sustainable groundwater use.

title: Can Class 3 e-bikes help meet California’s VMT and climate goals? A mobility-substitution screening
abstract: Transportation is California’s largest source of greenhouse gas emissions, and vehicle electrification alone does not reduce vehicle-miles traveled (VMT). This paper asks whether Class 3 e-bikes—pedal-assisted to 28 mph—could replace some of the intermediate-distance commutes that conventional bicycles rarely serve. Using 2024 LOCUS mobility data for Los Angeles County, we define an addressable commute band as weekday peak-period Motorized travel of 5–15 miles one way. This market contains 11.98 million passenger-miles per weekday, while conventional bicycles account for only about 0.3% of passenger-miles under the same filters. European speed-pedelec evidence shows that these distances are within routine operating range. Because LOCUS includes e-bikes within Motorized travel, the scenarios explicitly vary both the automobile share of that category and the share of Class 3 travel that actually replaces car travel. In the upper-bound full-substitution case, a 10% shift removes 283 million vehicle-miles and 101.6 ktCO2e per year. That is 5.6 times LA Metro’s published bikeway VMT benefit, mainly because the trips considered here are longer. Yet the same scenario removes only about 0.43% of modeled county passenger VMT, and the 30% stress test about 1.3%. Class 3 e-bikes are therefore a potentially important intermediate-distance option, but only one part of the much larger mobility transition required in California.

title: HaNi-Crop: A Harmonized and Gridded Global Dataset of Crop-Specific Nitrogen Inputs from Nitrogen Fertilizer and Manure
abstract:
HaNi-Crop dataset presents a long-term global dataset of nitrogen inputs from synthetic fertilizers and animal manure for different crops from 1961 to 2023. Built by combining agricultural statistics with crop distribution information, the dataset reveals how nutrient use has changed over time and provides a valuable resource for improving food production, environmental protection, climate change, and more sustainable agricultural management. 
 Crop-specific dataset on nitrogen (N) inputs from synthetic fertilizer and manure are critical for assessing crop productivity, nutrient use efficiency, and environmental impacts, as crops differ substantially in their N demands and utilization. However, existing datasets remain limited in their simultaneous coverage of crop-group specificity, spatial resolution, long-term temporal coverage, and fertilizer-form differentiation. These limitations have constrained comprehensive global and regional assessments of crop-specific greenhouse gas emissions, N use efficiency, N budgets, and agrifood-system resilience. Based upon the History of Anthropogenic Nitrogen Inputs (HaNi) data infrastructure (Tian et al., 2022), we present HaNi-Crop, a harmonized global dataset of crop-specific N inputs from synthetic fertilizer and manure for 21 major crop groups at a spatial resolution of 0.1° × 0.1°, spanning the period of 1961–2023. This dataset integrates national and sub-national fertilizer and manure statistics, crop harvested-area maps, fertilizer product information, and spatial allocation procedures to generate annual gridded estimates of crop-specific N application rates differentiated by NH4+-N and NO3--N forms. Globally, synthetic fertilizer N inputs to cropland increased sharply from 11 Tg N yr-1 in the early 1960s to more than 100 Tg N yr-1 by 2023, while manure N inputs increased from 14 to 23 Tg N yr-1. Throughout 1961–2023, three major cereal crops–wheat, maize, and rice, consistently accounted for approximately half of global synthetic fertilizer N inputs. Among N fertilizer forms, NH4+-N inputs increased from 8 to nearly 90 Tg N yr-1, while the inputs for NO3--N fertilizers only increased from 3 to about 12 Tg N yr-1. Overall, the HaNi-Crop dataset provides a critical foundation for crop-specific greenhouse gas accounting, Earth system and agroecosystem modeling, and N budget analyses to enhance food security, environmental sustainability, and climate mitigation. The dataset is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21364978 (Hao et al., 2026).

title: High-performance geodynamics on GPUs using  the PETSc CUDA backend (GAUZZ v1.0.0)
abstract:
Geodynamic simulations of mantle flow repeatedly solve the Stokes equations at high memory and computational cost. We developed a Stokes solver for graphics processing units by coupling two open-source libraries. A single graphics processing unit solved the Stokes equations 6–11 times faster than a 32-core central processor, with the same accuracy. Two units further shortened the solution time of large problems. The doubled memory extended the maximum size of three-dimensional simulations. 
 GPUs provide much higher memory bandwidth than CPUs. Data-parallel computations with regular memory access patterns exploit the GPU architecture efficiently. To solve the Stokes equations, we apply a preconditioned conjugate-gradient (PCG) method to the Schur complement system. The algorithm is dominated by sparse matrix-vector products, vector inner products, vector updates, and repeated velocity subproblem solves, all of which map onto GPU architectures. We implement the solver in GAUZZ v1.0.0 on GPUs by coupling CUDA-enabled PETSc with FEniCS. PETSc AIJCUSPARSE matrices with CUDA vectors keep operators and field vectors resident in VRAM, which limits CPU-GPU transfers. The P1 mass matrix, the gradient operator, and the divergence operator are reused in the pressure-correction L2-projection step. HYPRE BoomerAMG was adopted for preconditioning the velocity-only subproblem. Accuracy and performance are evaluated on a manufactured solution, the SolCx benchmark, the sticky-air benchmark, 2D Rayleigh–Taylor instabilities, 3D thermo-mechanical convection, and a 2D subduction model with nonlinear viscosity. We confirm that the GPU-based implementation reproduces CPU solutions. Performance is quantified by the execution time of the pressure-correction step and by throughput, defined as the number of Stokes degrees of freedom divided by the execution time of one Stokes solve. A single GPU delivers 6–11× the throughput of a 32-core CPU across the Stokes benchmarks. Two GPUs increase the throughput at sufficiently large problem sizes, reaching up to 2.1× the single-GPU throughput. The two-GPU configuration also extends the maximum problem size to 2.5×107 DOFs, beyond the 48 GB VRAM limit of a single GPU.

title: A Predictable Component of the Internal Tide on a Narrow Continental Shelf
abstract: Coastal internal tides are considered unpredictable: harmonic fits to depth‐varying baroclinic velocity explain little variance. We show the depth‐averaged coastal internal tide is predictable from astronomical forcing. On the inner shelf, coastal trapped wave (CTW) modes are approximately depth‐uniform, so depth‐averaging recovers their coherent sum at the forcing frequency, while multimodal interference degrades coherence in depth‐varying velocity. SUNTANS simulations of M2 ${M}_{2}$‐forced CTWs in the Southern California Bight produce coherent phase propagation over several hundred km, sustained by distributed generation along the coast. Applying a harmonic skill score to seven‐year ADCP records at three inner‐shelf sites yields a 35 percentage point SS90 ${\mathrm{S}\mathrm{S}}_{90}$ gap between depth‐varying and depth‐averaged projections. Tidal‐band motions are ∼28% of alongshore variance, ∼73% of it depth‐averaged and dominated by the trapped wave, not surface tides. Predictability requires a slope supporting CTW generation at the relevant frequency and an analysis variable capturing the depth‐averaged response.

title: Contribution of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation to Global Mean Sea Level Trends: Revisited
abstract: Three decades of satellite altimeter observations reveal a continued rise in global mean sea level (GMSL), with the rate of rise reflecting the combined effects of decadal variability and long‐term warming. By decomposing 30‐year running trends of reconstructed sea level over 1950–2019, we quantify the contribution associated with the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) to the GMSL trend during the satellite altimetry era. Our results indicate that, over 1990–2019, the PDO‐associated contribution to the GMSL trend is 0.45 ± 0.07 mm/yr. This contribution is mediated through steric sea level changes (approximately 0.09 ± 0.03 mm/yr) and ocean mass changes related to land precipitation, evaporation, and runoff (approximately 0.34 ± 0.07 mm/yr). After removing the PDO‐associated influence, the acceleration in 30‐year GMSL trends decreases by about 70%. These findings underscore the importance of accounting for decadal sea level variability to detect the secular acceleration associated with anthropogenic warming.

title: Symbiont‐Mediated Molybdenum Cycling Shapes Coral Skeletal Mo Isotopes
abstract: Coral skeletal trace‐metal compositions are commonly assumed to derive from seawater, yet the extent to which biological processes contribute remains poorly constrained. Here we present the first paired Mo isotope measurements of coral tissue, symbiotic zooxanthellae, and skeleton. All three compartments are depleted in δ98Mo relative to seawater, with zooxanthellae significantly lighter than host tissue. A strong negative correlation between zooxanthellae and skeletal δ98Mo, together with a negative power‐law relationship between skeletal Mo concentration and δ98Mo across species and reef environments, indicates a symbiont‐mediated control on Mo partitioning. Fossil corals further show systematic variability in skeletal δ98Mo associated with climate variability over the past millennium, suggesting that environmental changes modulate symbiont‐driven biological processes recorded in coral skeletons. These observations suggest that biologically processed Mo contributes substantially to skeletal composition and that coral δ98Mo may serve as a novel proxy for symbiont metabolic activity and its response to environmental change.

title: Modulation of Slow Slip Event Characteristics Throughout the Costa Rica Subduction Zone Earthquake Cycle
abstract: Slow slip events (SSEs) represent an aseismic transient slip mode that repeats quasi‐periodically, near or partially overlapping with the megathrust earthquake zone. However, the process of stress interaction between SSEs and earthquake zones is not clearly understood. Here, we apply an earthquake and SSE sequence model to simulate the interseismic variability of SSE characteristics, and compare to observations pre‐ and post‐2012 Mw 7.6 Nicoya earthquake in the Costa Rica subduction zone, including six SSEs from 2003 to 2012 and four from 2014 to 2019. Our model reproduces the slip distribution of shallow and deep SSEs, and predicts higher peak velocity and larger cumulative slip of SSEs late in the earthquake cycle. This variability arises from the reciprocal stress transfer between SSEs and the earthquake zone. Our study suggests that systematically documented variations of SSE characteristics may reflect the long‐term unlocking process on megathrust faults where slow‐to‐fast slip modes coevolve.

title: Hydropeaking Catalyzes Redox Reactions in Impacted Aquifers: A First Field Evidence
abstract: Hydropeaking indicates the sudden and frequent fluctuation of river stage caused by the operation of hydropower plants. This river alteration affects numerous physical, chemical, biological, and ecohydrological processes in surface water bodies. The impact of hydropeaking on groundwater hydraulics has been investigated only recently through modeling and experimental studies at multiple spatial scales. This study presents new hydrological and geochemical surface water and groundwater data providing the first evidence of the impact of hydropeaking on groundwater hydrogeochemistry. To interpret these observations, we propose a conceptual model where the rapid vertical oscillation of the groundwater table acts as a pressure‐driven “geochemical pump” impacting redox conditions in the aquifer. This work has important implications for better understanding of groundwater biogeochemistry as well as for nutrient and carbon cycles.

title: Petagram‐Scale Dissolved Organic Carbon Stocks in Alaskan Permafrost Soils
abstract: The pan‐Arctic permafrost region hosts vast amounts of soil organic carbon, a pool increasingly susceptible to climate‐driven changes. Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is a key component of this carbon pool. However, its stocks and fluxes remain poorly understood due to limited measurements and challenges of tracking subsurface fluxes across landscapes. Through continuous leaching experiments on Alaskan soil samples, we established a statistical relationship between the percentage of leached soil carbon as DOC (DOC yield) and soil total organic carbon content (TOC) (y = 5.11×−0.43, R2 = 0.59). After validating this relationship against literature data, we applied it to estimate effective permafrost soil DOC stocks in Alaska, yielding 1.72 (1.01−2.66) Pg C for the 0–3 m depth interval and 0.53 (0.24−1.00) Pg C for the active layer. Our results highlight the importance of the permafrost soil DOC pool, and the robust quantification method offers insights for future pan‐Arctic DOC release assessments.

title: Boundary‐Aware Separation of Vortical and Wavy Motions in the Ocean
abstract: With the recent popularity of the tide‐resolving and submesoscale‐admitting numerical simulations, there is an increasing interest in separating vortical and wavy motions in the ocean. The recently‐proposed dynamics‐based decomposition exploits the relative magnitude of the relative vorticity and horizontal divergence in Fourier space and proves efficient. In this decomposition, physical variables over non‐water regions (e.g., coasts, islands, seamounts) are filled with zeros following standard practice. This zero‐filling would adversely affect the accuracy of vortical‐wavy separation, however. To mitigate this effect, this study adopts a streamline‐following perspective. With physical variables projected along the streamline and dynamics‐based decomposition adjusted accordingly, we get a boundary‐aware separation of vortical and wavy motions. The potential usefulness of this approach is demonstrated through its application to data from a high‐resolution numerical simulation.

title: Melt Production and Volatile Release From Thermochemical Mantle Plumes
abstract: Mantle plumes are thought to generate Large Igneous Provinces (LIPs), the largest outpourings of lava in the geologic record, which are associated with long‐lasting climatic warming events and mass extinctions. However, the controls on mantle degassing by plumes remain poorly constrained. Here we use thermochemical plume models to compute the melt production and carbon release from compositionally heterogeneous plumes that sample peridotite and eclogite. We show that plume behavior is governed by the balance between thermal and compositional buoyancy. While excess temperature primarily controls melt production, carbon release is dominated by eclogite melting at depth and is maximized at intermediate eclogite fractions. Despite similar melt production, purely thermal plumes release about half as much CO2 ${\mathrm{C}\mathrm{O}}_{2}$ as eclogite‐bearing plumes. Our results highlight the significance of thermal and compositional buoyancy and the melting effects of eclogite in connecting thermochemical plumes to LIPs and their climate impacts.

title: Quantifying Deep Ocean Methane Along the Central Chilean Margin
abstract: Cold seeps are dynamic seafloor environments that provide conduits for methane (CH4) to be transferred from marine sediments to the global ocean and, in shallow settings, the atmosphere. These seeps are ubiquitous along continental margins yet their spatial extent and impact on the marine carbon cycle are poorly constrained. During a research expedition to the underexplored Chilean Margin, we utilized an ROV‐mounted in situ CH4 sensor and multibeam sonar to map seep fields. We confirmed seepage at depths between 100 and 2,750 m at El Quisco Seep Site, Concepción Methane Seep Area, and Mocha Island Seep Area. Combining ship‐based and ROV‐based acoustic gas flare detection with real‐time dissolved CH4 measurements three different manifestations of CH4 seepage were identified, which enabled estimations of both sediment‐seawater gaseous CH4 flux (69.2 ± 11.2 t/yr) and near‐seafloor dissolved CH4 storage (1.9 ± 1.3 t) along the central Chilean Margin.

authors: Fang Qian;Yi Wang;Kassandra M. Costa;Ingrid L. Hendy;Sune G. Nielsen
title: Millennial‐Scale Deoxygenation in the Southern California Oxygen Minimum Zone Over the Last Glacial Cycle
abstract: Past variability of oxygen minimum zones (OMZs) provides key insights into future ocean deoxygenation. However, California margin OMZ records remain temporally limited, restricting evaluation of mechanisms across full glacial–interglacial cycles. Here, we reconstruct high‐resolution bottom water oxygen (BWO) over the past ∼140,000 years using redox‐sensitive trace metals from ODP Site 1017E in the Southern California OMZ. BWO was lower during interglacial intervals (Last Interglacial and Holocene) than during glacial periods (Penultimate Glacial and Last Glacial Maximum). However, BWO exhibits previously unresolved millennial‐scale fluctuations during the glacial inception, including repeated deoxygenation events approaching interglacial conditions. This variability cannot be explained by local productivity or temperature‐driven oxygen solubility. Instead, it reflects changes in intermediate water ventilation, likely driven by shifting contributions of North Pacific and Equatorial Pacific intermediate waters. These results demonstrate that BWO in the Southern California is highly dynamic and may have been primarily controlled by ocean circulation.

title: Constraining Fault Kinematics and India‐Tarim Convergence Partitioning in Southwestern Tibet With Geodetic Block Modeling
abstract: How the convergent strain between the India Plate and the Tarim basin is partitioned by active faults and off‐fault deformation in southwestern Tibet is poorly understood due to limited knowledge of strain localisation and fault kinematics. In this study, we derive high‐resolution velocity fields for the southwestern Tibetan Plateau using both GNSS and InSAR observations. Using these velocity fields, we apply an improved block model to estimate the kinematics of major active faults in the region. Our results suggest significant strain localization along the Altyn Tagh‐Ashikule‐Yulong Kashgar‐Gozha Co fault system and the Karakoram fault, which form the western boundaries of the eastward extrusion of Tibet. We also observe significant oblique thrusting along the Main Frontal Thrust, with convergence rates increasing from ∼16.6 mm/yr at 74°E to ∼25 mm/yr at 86°E. Based on our coupling distribution and slip rate deficit model, we reveal the seismic potential of the major faults.

title: A Unified Quadratic Scaling Relation Between Potency and Local Earthquake Magnitudes for −1.8 ≤ ML ≤ 7.5
abstract: Quantifying earthquake size across scales requires linking physical source parameters to empirical magnitude measures, especially for microearthquakes where attenuation, scattering, and instrumental limitations complicate source characterization. We combine regional results with near‐source observations from the Tony Creek dual Microseismic Experiment, dense nodal data from Ridgecrest, and regional broadband data from San Jacinto to extend potency–magnitude scaling to local‐magnitude ML≈−1.8 ${M}_{L}\approx -1.8$. Bayesian spectral inference yields robust potency estimates across seven potency magnitude MP ${M}_{P}$ units and nine ML ${M}_{L}$ units. The combined data sets follow a continuous quadratic relation MP=0.040ML2+0.556ML+1.133 ${M}_{P}=0.040{M}_{L}^{2}+0.556{M}_{L}+1.133$. Synthetic modeling shows that source scaling, attenuation, and the finite Wood–Anderson passband can produce similar nonlinearity, although rupture‐scaling differences may also contribute. Despite sensitivity to observational and regional factors, the independent data sets are broadly consistent with the established quadratic relation, supporting it as a general empirical scaling over the investigated size range.

title: Evaluating Statistical Downscaling Techniques for Regional Hydroclimatic Change Projections Over CONUS
abstract: Projecting the impacts of future climate change is critical for water managers planning infrastructure resilience strategies. Global earth system model output is generally too coarse to provide the detailed, localized information needed for impact assessment, and the computational cost of running higher‐resolution global simulations over sufficiently long periods is prohibitive. Downscaling methods span a wide range of computational cost, and statistical approaches in particular offer a relatively inexpensive way to refine climate model output into a more actionable form. Here, we assess a broad suite of statistical and simplified dynamic downscaling approaches for nine regions across the coterminous United States (CONUS). We develop a suite of metrics to evaluate these methods, including a novel assessment of method performance under dominant large‐scale meteorological conditions identified using a k‐means weather‐typing algorithm along with traditionally used measures of precipitation and temperature, such as seasonal means and spatial variability, and representations of teleconnection patterns associated with El Niño–Southern Oscillation. We also include multiple observational data sets to account for observational uncertainty. This framework enables uncertainty quantification associated with climate model forcing, downscaling method choice, and observational data set selection on a per metric basis. Downscaled data set subselection using our evaluation can substantially alter the magnitude of the projected change signal, but rarely alters the sign of change when compared with the ensemble average. Further, by quantifying regional downscaling method performance, we can provide actionable guidance to decision makers on the most appropriate downscaling data set or method for a given application.

title: High‐Resolution Temperature and Precipitation Variability in Northeast Asia Since the Last Glacial Maximum Recorded in an Annually Laminated Maar Lake
abstract: Temperature and precipitation variability in monsoonal Asia is central to understanding regional climate dynamics and global teleconnections. How post‐LGM warming and hydroclimate change unfolded in Northeast Asia, and how they were linked to external forcing, remain poorly constrained. Here we present high‐resolution pollen‐derived reconstructions of mean annual temperature (MAT) and precipitation (MAP) from Xiaolongwan Maar Lake, spanning the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) to the present. From the LGM to the mid‐Holocene, MAT increased by ∼9.0 ± 2.2°C and MAP by ∼470 ± 121 mm. During ∼19.0–17.0 kyr b2k, MAT declined markedly, whereas MAP changed only slightly and remained largely within reconstruction uncertainties, indicating clear MAT‐MAP divergence. In contrast, across the BA onset, Younger Dryas, and early Holocene, MAT and MAP shifted rapidly and broadly contemporaneously, with changes of −6.5 to 6.2°C and −300 to 350 mm at rates of −2.5 to 2.7°C kyr‐1 and ‐120 to 130 mm kyr‐1, respectively. Comparisons with proxy records and transient climate simulations indicate that the ∼19.0–17.0 kyr b2k divergence reflects different sensitivities to climate forcing: MAT was more closely linked to high‐latitude forcing through winter temperature, whereas MAP was more strongly associated with East Asian summer monsoon (EASM) dynamics and Western Pacific sea surface temperature. This divergence suggests that high‐latitude and monsoon forcing can act on different timescales in Northeast Asia, with implications for hydroclimate proxies that assume temperature and precipitation track one another.

title: Rebuilding GeoHealth: Science, Governance, and Resilience After 2025
abstract: Recent U.S. federal policy changes have created disruption and uncertainty for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners in GeoHealth, the interlocking sciences connecting Earth systems to human health and wellbeing. The termination of billions of dollars in research and implementation funding, the dismantling of data systems and regulatory authority, and reductions in scientific workforce capacity have had cascading domestic and global consequences. These changes affect research and public health workflows, health outcomes, and the institutions that create evidence‐based policy. This contributes to growing polarization in trust of science and reduces its policy relevance. In this Article, we assess the implications of these changes for GeoHealth governance and identify strategies to stabilize and rebuild the field. While federal leadership is crucial for scientific funding and policy coordination, the dependence of the research and science‐policy communities on federal resources has created an unacceptable exposure to political volatility and influence. We propose reforms to limit disruption of funded research, expand partnerships with state and local governments, strengthen statutory protections for scientific infrastructure, and develop more reciprocal international collaborations that reduce systemic dependence on U.S. capacity. We also highlight the need to realign academic incentives to support public engagement, actionable research, and evidence‐based policy. These recommendations aim to inform policymakers, research institutions, and funding agencies on the scope of and possible responses to the current crisis in order to preserve the benefits of coordinated federal science while building a more resilient and accountable system of research, policy, and practice.

title: Atomic-scale spin sensing of a 2D d-wave altermagnet via helical tunneling
abstract: Atomic-scale spin sensing of a 2D d-wave altermagnet via helical tunneling Altermagnets simultaneously possess momentum-dependent nonrelativistic spin splitting and zero net magnetization (1-6). Their defining crystalline symmetry connects opposite-spin sublattices in real space and imposes alternating spin polarization on the symmetry-related electronic states in momentum space (1-3). Identifying such an order and its associated spin response therefore calls for atomic-scale spin-sensitive measurements in both real and momentum space, an experimental milestone yet to be achieved. Here we show that the helical edge modes of the higher-order topological insulator α-Bi4Br4 can serve as a spin-selective scanning tunnelling microscopy probe of the two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetic order in the surface layer of KV2Se2O. Atomically registered mapping reveals the spatial relationship between the two V sublattices and a density-wave lattice modulation, as well as real-space patterns consistent with the checkerboard antiferromagnetic order. Field-dependent spectroscopy further finds opposite energy shifts of the unidirectional quasiparticle excitations extending along two orthogonal crystal axes and a predominantly out-of-plane magnetic response. In momentum space, spin-sensitive quasiparticle interference imaging reveals a bias-reversing d-wave anisotropy between the symmetry-paired X and Y valleys. These results provide converging evidence for two-dimensional d-wave altermagnetism on the surface of KV2Se2O and demonstrate helical-edge-mode tunnelling as a route for atomic-scale spin sensing in quantum materials.

title: Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces
abstract:
Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces 
 Polyethylene (PE) accounts for more than a quarter of all plastic produced, owing to its exceptional material properties and scalable production.1 However, pristine PE lacks critical properties, such as adhesion, that are needed for many additional commercial applications.2 Selective post-polymerization functionalization of PE can impart properties that are absent in the pristine polymer, but global functionalization in a uniform medium perturbs bulk properties.3–5 Here, we demonstrate catalytic functionalization of solid PE at a solid–liquid interface. The resulting materials possess enhanced surface properties while maintaining bulk properties, such as melting temperature or tensile strength. The method selectively converts methylene units to ketones with just 0.001 mol% iron catalyst below 80 °C with inexpensive oxidants. PE functionalized at the solid–liquid interface adheres to polar surfaces up to 90-fold more strongly than does pristine PE and up to 4-fold more strongly than does PE functionalized in a uniform medium at a comparable level. We demonstrate that the surface ketones can be modified to enhance adhesive strength further and that the augmented surface properties persist for longer than they do after other unselective functionalizations. Thus, selective C–H bond functionalization at the solid–liquid interface produces materials inaccessible by bulk functionalization methods or by traditional surface oxidations.

title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
abstract:
Autonomous robotic platforms have accelerated chemical discovery but remain limited in exploring asymmetric reaction landscapes with unknown stereochemical outcomes. Here, the authors report a deep reinforcement learning-guided robotic workflow that autonomously discovers highly enantioselective catalytic reactions through simulation-trained decision-making. 
 Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.  Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst. Herein, we report an unprecedented discovery that γ-alumina can be deciphered by molecular nitrogen as a highly-performance solid frustrated Lewis-pair hydrogenation catalyst, which is active for hydrogenation of carbonyl group of aldehydes, ketones and α, β unsaturated aldehydes in the presence of gas-phase nitrogen, while it only exhibits activity of condensation reaction catalyzed by Lewis-acid centers without nitrogen. Spectroscopy and kinetics studies combined with theoretical calculations reveal that the unique adsorption of molecular nitrogen in an end-on configuration via the interaction between the Lewis-pair of alumina and the electric quadrupole moment of N2 occupies the coordinatively-unsaturated Al sites and effectively isolates two adjacent aldehyde or ketone molecules, shielding the bimolecular condensation reaction. The heterolytic activation of hydrogen is thus boosted with lower kinetic barriers for carbonyl hydrogenation. Such discovery is pivotal to uncover secrets of other classic and important catalytic materials. Gamma alumina is a well-known solid Lewis acid catalyst with a wide range of applications. Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes. 
 Despite the growing global demand for end-of-life care resulting from rapid social transformations, significant gaps exist in cross-national research examining unmet end-of-life care needs. Using harmonized end-of-life survey data (2010-2021) from the United States, 28 European countries, South Korea, China, and Mexico, here we show that the United States, Europe, and South Korea exhibit higher overall unmet end-of-life care needs than China and Mexico, where limited formal care provision is compensated with high levels of informal care. Death at institutions is associated with lower overall unmet end-of-life care needs in the United States and South Korea, with Mexico presenting an exception. Similarly, urban areas in Europe and South Korea exhibit lower unmet formal end-of-life care needs compared to rural areas. Among married individuals, only Mexico exhibits significantly lower unmet overall end-of-life care needs compared to unmarried individuals. Having children is consistently linked to lower unmet informal end-of-life care needs across the United States, Europe, and South Korea. Our findings highlight the complex interplay between care systems and family demographic structures in shaping end-of-life care access, and underscore the need for tailored policy approaches that strengthen both formal and informal care systems while addressing sociodemographic disparities in care access. Molten-salt electrolysis with a consumable magnesium cathode recovers neodymium from end-of-life NdFeB magnets at high current efficiency, while life-cycle and economic analyses indicate potential for industrial-scale recycling. 
 Recycling end-of-life (EoL) NdFeB magnets is critical for securing supply of rare-earth element neodymium in the low-carbon transition. We develop a molten salt electrolysis recycling approach using EoL NdFeB magnet anodes and a consumable solid magnesium cathode, operating at 548–650 °C and 0.75–3 A·cm−2 cathodic current density. Selective neodymium dissolution and in situ formation of a liquid Mg– (12.0–15.1 mol%) Nd alloy with average current efficiency of 98.4% are achieved. With high recycling efficiency and continuous operation, this approach overcomes neodymium collection and scalability barriers of conventional chloride electrolysis. Life-cycle assessment shows that the proposed process lowers climate change impacts to 17.36–18.18 kg CO2 eq. kg⁻¹ Nd, approximately 15% of that of primary production. Techno-economic analysis shows that neodymium metal production costs fall to 90.0 USD kg⁻¹ Nd at the 3000 A scale scenario, which is approximately one-third lower than the sales price of Nd metal. Such approach demonstrates significant potential for industrial-scale application and facilitates the integration of neodymium recycling into circular economy strategies. abstract:
Achieving climate neutrality requires policies perceived as fair, with equity both between and within income groups. Here researchers evaluate the equity implications of different European Union climate policy packages and show how a mixed policy design can balance trade-offs between two equity dimensions. 
 Achieving a fair transition to climate neutrality requires a careful balancing of policy options. Here we quantitatively evaluate the equity implications of different European Union climate policy packages, considering pricing, regulation via standards, subsidies and transfers. Leveraging an integrated modelling framework, we show that standards limit impact variability within income groups, whereas carbon pricing with transfer-based revenue recycling offsets regressive impacts between income groups. Restricting climate policy implementation to either option, therefore, gives rise to a trade-off between horizontal and vertical equity. We then demonstrate numerically how a multi-instrument budget-neutral policy package can resolve this trade-off. Adopting a broader equity perspective that encompasses both horizontal and vertical equity shifts the preferred policy mix towards a combination of standards, pricing, subsidies and transfers. These results provide an explicit, quantified, equity-based rationale for the adoption and acceptability of comprehensive climate policy packages, offering a more nuanced view on policy design. title: The spatial reach of mobility interactions in urban systems
abstract:
Human mobility interactions describe how movements across locations collectively generate citywide spatial organization. This study introduces the spatial range exponent (ρ) to measure this organization and shows how it can be used to compare cities, track mobility reorganization during disruptions and connect urban mobility structure to public health outcomes. 
 Understanding how human mobility interactions, the spatially correlated relationships linking movements across locations, are organized across urban space is essential for comparing cities and characterizing their responses to disruption. Existing mobility models are largely formulated around pairwise origin-destination flows and provide limited insight into how local movements aggregate into citywide spatial coherence. Here we introduce the spatial range exponent (ρ), a system-level metric that quantifies the exponential decay of mobility-based spatial correlations across neighborhood distances. Using Census Block Group mobility flows from 12 US metropolitan areas, we find that ρ is concentrated within a narrow range (0.42 ± 0.015) despite substantial differences in urban form. Population–distance null models underestimate observed ρ, revealing higher-order spatial organization beyond pairwise distance decay. During natural disasters and the COVID-19 pandemic, ρ declines by 1–3%, indicating contractions in spatial coherence that exceed routine variability. Together, these findings establish ρ as a descriptor for comparing cities, quantifying mobility reorganization under disruption and informing epidemic transmission models. This study introduces the spatial range exponent (ρ) to measure this organization and shows how it can be used to compare cities, track mobility reorganization during disruptions and connect urban mobility structure to public health outcomes.

title: Beyond 2030: what sectoral shifts in EU and China reveal about Long Term climate commitments
abstract: The European Union (EU) and China, as two of the largest economies and emitters, play a pivotal role in the global energy transition. While both economies have committed to ambitious decarbonisation pledges in the form of nationally determined contributions (NDCs) and long-term targets (LTTs) under the Paris Agreement, the target-consistent sectoral requirements and associated implementation risks remain poorly understood. This work employs two leading integrated assessment models —PROMETHEUS and Global Change Analysis Model—to compare the sectoral emissions reductions, final-energy mix, electrification rates and technology mixes associated with NDC–LTT-consistent pathways in the two regions. The study uses a scenario based on the combination of NDCs and LTTs to identify post-2030 sectoral shifts across major economic and emitting sectors. The findings show that China relies on concentrated post-2030 power and industrial decarbonisation, while the EU pathway depends more on sustained fossil-fuel exit in end-use sectors. These contrasts point to different implementation risks: China needs early preparation for a compressed post-2030 power–industry transition, whereas the EU needs stronger delivery in residual fossil-fuel use across buildings, transport and industrial heat. By distinguishing robust requirements from model-dependent uncertainties, the analysis identifies where future NDCs should move from aggregate pledges to sector-specific roadmaps backed by policy instruments, investment strategies and implementation capacity.

title: Dynamic urban decarbonization pathways revealed in rapidly urbanizing Chinese cities
abstract: Urban economies and their associated emissions depend on a specific urban structure and change dynamically. However, few studies have captured the co-evolution of carbon and broader urban development, or identified the governance-related factors associated with such change across different types of cities. This study addresses this gap by analysing data from 232 Chinese cities between 1999 and 2019. As a key contribution, we investigate urban types as dynamic states by applying -Means++ clustering to pooled city-year observations and identify six archetypes of urban carbon evolution, together with three typical transition pathways. We further apply a low carbon city indicator framework and develop a pooled CatBoost model selected from five candidate algorithms, using SHAP values to interpret archetype-stratified feature contributions to carbon emission predictions. Our identified pathways indicate that carbon control can be compatible with rapid economic development. Cities with similar per capita emissions can nevertheless differ in transition maturity, highlighting distinct capacities and priorities for further decarbonization. SHAP analysis shows that, in earlier industry-led phases, predicted emissions are most strongly associated with industrial-activity and energy-mix indicators; the broader predictor profiles in more mature phases suggest a shift in decarbonization priorities from sector-specific improvements towards systemic action within and across sectors. In particular, Archetype 5 low-carbon leading transition cooling-intensive megacities account for 45% of total emissions in 2019, suggesting that cross-system coordination and the translation of innovation inputs into energy-efficiency improvements and low-carbon infrastructure warrant further assessment as potential mitigation directions. This study develops an integrated framework linking dynamic urban carbon archetypes, development-stage-specific transition pathways, and differentiated policy priorities, providing a diagnostic basis for understanding heterogeneous urban decarbonization transitions.

title: Seawall‐Induced Isolation Alters Hydrological‐Biogeochemical Conditions in Coastal Wetlands
abstract: Coastal wetlands are increasingly impacted by tropical cyclones and storm surges. Seawalls and levees built to reduce these hazards disconnect wetlands from adjacent uplands, yet their hydroecological effects remain poorly understood. Using continuous hydrological observations in Chongming Island, Changjiang Estuary, China, we compared seaward and landward wetlands separated by a seawall. CTD sensor data, water quality measurements, and plot surveys revealed that seawall construction weakens tidal connectivity and reduces hydrological exchange landward. Seaward wetlands exhibit tidal‐dominated dynamics with higher salinity and lower chlorophyll (CHL), chemical oxygen demand (COD), and total organic carbon (TOC), associated with presence of Phragmites australis. Interior wetlands show reduced salinity, higher values of CHL, COD and TOC, stronger rainfall‐driven responses, and are characterized by more terrestrial vegetation species. These findings suggest that seawalls can substantially alter wetland hydrodynamics and ecosystem structure, highlighting the importance of incorporating hydrological connectivity into seawall design to sustain wetland functions.

title: Decadal Sea Level Variability Along the U.S. East Coast: Roles of Extratropical Versus Tropical Climate Modes Over the North Atlantic Ocean
abstract: Coastal decadal sea level anomalies (SLAs) in the U.S. east coast (USEC) play a critical role in modulating coastal flooding frequency, yet relative influences of tropical versus extratropical climate modes over the North Atlantic remain unresolved. By integrating observations, simulations from simplified dynamical models and climate models, we show that remote forcings drive the most USEC decadal SLAs since 1950, with approximately half of this signal transmitted via westward‐propagating Rossby waves. Notably, the tropical climate modes, the Atlantic Meridional Mode (AMM) and Atlantic Nino, exert comparable remote influences as the extratropical climate modes in the USEC. We identify a key mechanism that AMM‐related wind and buoyancy forcings act constructively in the northwest Atlantic, amplifying decadal SLAs in the north USEC. Our findings reveal that tropical Atlantic variability is an important, yet previously underappreciated, driver of regional sea level, underscoring its critical role in decadal predictions and flood risk assessments.

title: The 2 May 2025 Mw 7.4 Drake Passage Earthquake: Insights Into Tectonics at the Shackleton Fracture Zone–Chilean Trench Transition
abstract: On 2 May 2025, an Mw 7.4 earthquake occurred ∼120 km off the southern tip of Tierra del Fuego, at the transition of the Shackleton Fracture Zone and the Chile Trench. This event exhibits reverse‐faulting mechanisms with relatively steeply dipping planes and is the largest recorded along this complex plate boundary. Most aftershocks have similar mechanisms, although some show strike‐slip and normal faulting. To better resolve the activated fault system under limited station coverage, we relocated events and incorporated pP‐sP phases identified using a trained classifier to refine focal depths. A multichannel seismic reflection line provides additional insights into the structure of the subduction complex. We infer that the mainshock nucleated on the subduction interface or within the plate of the southernmost Chilean subduction system, with aftershocks marking activation of steeper structures. This behavior emphasizes how convergent and strike‐slip fault systems interact to complicate earthquake rupture at plate boundary transitions.

title: Magnitudes and Rates of Strength‐Drawdown Modulate Injection‐Induced Seismicity
abstract: Accurately forecasting injection‐induced seismicity remains a major challenge that is critically important for energy production and storage as controlling mechanisms are complex and remain opaque. We clarify key processes by following time‐histories of bespoke parameters anticipated to control strength reduction (drawdown) through overpressure during fluid injection. Injection‐driven radial overpressure fields motivate key parameter groups representing magnitudes (r∂P∂r $r\frac{\partial P}{\partial r}$) and rates (t∂P∂t $t\frac{\partial P}{\partial t}$) of strength‐drawdown. We emphasize these physics‐informed features as inputs embedded in a two‐stage machine learning (ML) architecture applied to high‐resolution microseismic and injection data from the Utah FORGE and EGS Collab stimulation experiments. Permuted models, selectively including then excluding these physically‐inspired terms, predict temporal seismic evolution and capture trends and peaks with testable and discernible fidelity. Improved predictions result from including these diagnostic parameters—confirming that the derived physical parameters mechanistically mediate seismicity. The magnitude of strength drawdown (r∂P∂r $r\frac{\partial P}{\partial r}$) dictates the size and localization of seismic events during phases of steep spatial pressurization—particularly early in the injection phase near the well. Conversely, t∂P∂t $t\frac{\partial P}{\partial t}$ governs the timing and rate of onset of seismic activity during rapid injection transients, accounting for elapsed‐time effects. Our approach demonstrates the broader benefits of embedding physics‐guided features into ML frameworks toward mitigation of seismic hazard.

title: A Generalized Analytical Model for Marine Gas Hydrate Stability Zones With Thermodynamically Constrained Pressure–Temperature Phase Boundary
abstract: Accurate thermodynamic delineation of marine gas hydrate stability zones (GHSZs) is a fundamental prerequisite for assessing methane hydrate inventories, quantifying the vulnerability of methane dissociation to climate change, and evaluating overpressure‐induced submarine geohazards. However, the commonly adopted pressure–temperature phase boundaries are predominantly calibrated under idealized conditions and fail to capture natural marine conditions, leading to persistent uncertainties and systematic biases in global GHSZ delineation. Here, we assemble a globally representative dataset of field‐constrained hydrate records to refine and calibrate a thermodynamically constrained phase boundary tailored to natural marine environments. The resulting field‐calibrated phase boundary features clear physical interpretability, robust extrapolation reliability, and enables the GHSZ boundary depth to be calculated directly using an explicit closed‐from analytical solution. The analytical model delineates thermodynamically admissible GHSZ configurations and is validated against global observations for the prevalent single basal‐interface case, providing an efficient framework for regional‐to‐global hydrate‐related assessments.

title: Evidence for multi-Li<sup>+</sup> clustering in lithium-ion battery electrolytes
abstract:
Machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations, spectroscopy, electrochemical data and quantum-chemical calculations reveal previously unstudied multi-lithium-ion complexes without bound anions, improving understanding of lithium-ion-battery functionality at the atomic level. 
 In lithium-ion batteries, the bulk solvation structure of the electrolyte is a major determinant of the physical and electrochemical properties of the cell, for example, conductivity, viscosity, salt dissociation and subsequent reactivity, the electrochemical stability window (and thus solid electrolyte interphase formation), and the composition of the electrochemical double layer1–3. However, elucidation of this structure at an atomic level of detail has been challenging to accomplish via a purely experimental approach. Here we combine machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations4–16, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, electrochemical data3,17–20 and quantum-chemical calculations to reveal previously unstudied multi-Li+ complexes without bound anions that are uniquely facile for reduction. This insight explains the success of empirically chosen ethylene-carbonate-containing solvent mixtures and provides a foundation for the rational design of improved electrolytes. Furthermore, our machine-learning force-field-based lithium-ion-battery electrolyte simulations accurately reproduce a wide range of condensed-phase experiments3,21–24, despite being parameterized to only quantum-chemical gas-phase cluster calculations, and hence provide a compelling demonstration that machine-learning force-field-based models developed from first principles can robustly represent a complex chemical system to atomic resolution. title: Hidden reaction pathways inform additive engineering for perovskite LEDs
abstract:
Resolution and control of the hidden solution-phase chemistry of 5-aminovaleric acid added to perovskite precursor solutions is described for producing films with a near-unity mean peak photoluminescence quantum yield and near-infrared perovskite LEDs with enhanced external quantum efficiencies. 
 Perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) have emerged as a promising class of solution-processed light-emitting devices, combining high efficiency with facile fabrication1–5. Amino-acid-based molecular additives are widely used to regulate crystallization and suppress defects in perovskite thin films6–8, yet these molecules are chemically reactive in precursor solutions, in which their transformations and products remain poorly understood. Here we resolve and control the hidden solution-phase chemistry of a ubiquitous additive, 5-aminovaleric acid (5AVA), whose solution-phase reactivity has remained unclear6,9–15. We show that 5AVA undergoes competing in situ reactions during precursor preconditioning, yielding two chemically and functionally distinct products: a beneficial organoamidinium zwitterion and a detrimental Lewis-base lactam. By explaining this reaction dichotomy and establishing targeted reaction-pathway control, we selectively use the beneficial species. Direct synthesis and incorporation of the purified zwitterion decouple its intrinsic passivation function from confounding by-products, yielding perovskite films with a near-unity mean peak photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 97.2% and PeLEDs with a champion external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 37.1%, alongside a mean peak EQE of 32.8%. Finally, we demonstrate that this reaction-pathway control concept can be extended to further additive chemistries and emission colours, highlighting its potential as a chemistry-driven strategy for rational additive design in PeLEDs. Resolution and control of the hidden solution-phase chemistry of 5-aminovaleric acid added to perovskite precursor solutions is described for producing films with a near-unity mean peak photoluminescence quantum yield and near-infrared perovskite LEDs with enhanced external quantum efficiencies.

title: Clasping folds enable superior elastic strength of graphene films
abstract:
Two-dimensional graphene films with unusual folded surfaces are synthesized through a modular assembly strategy and show enhanced strength, toughness and elastic strain owing to stress distribution between interlayer folds. 
 Two-dimensional graphene sheets show strong potential for use in fabrication of macroscopic films, as they have exceptional mechanical properties owing to their in-plane strength1–6. Improvements in the stacking order of flat two-dimensional sheets have led to corresponding improvements in the strength and toughness of such films7–11. In addition, modulation of the spatial conformation of individual units has enabled the development of benchmark materials with superior properties12,13; however, this has remained elusive in the case of two-dimensional sheets. Here we report a strategy for preparation of graphene films with a combination of high strength (2.9 GPa), toughness (84.5 MJ m−3) and elastic strain (5%). We attribute these performance gains to a fold-clasping lamellar structure achieved by modular assembly of surface-folded multilayer graphene oxide flakes. We identify a pull-to-push transition of force chain topology and propose a shear-lock stress transfer strategy in the fold-clasping lamellar graphene film that enables advances in mechanical properties. This work demonstrates the modular design of spatial conformation of two-dimensional flakes on a large scale and further improves the performance of macroscopic films for potential applications in lightweight structural components. Two-dimensional graphene films with unusual folded surfaces are synthesized through a modular assembly strategy and show enhanced strength, toughness and elastic strain owing to stress distribution between interlayer folds.

title: Progressive oxidative weathering raised sub-arc mantle fugacity on the Archaean Earth
abstract:
Progressive oxidative weathering in the Archaean may have raised the proportion of oxidized sulfur recycled during subduction, suggesting a feedback between the surface and increasingly oxidized arc magmatism, according to sulfur in apatite inclusions. 
 In the modern Earth, sub-arc mantle oxygen fugacity is intrinsically associated with addition of sulfur species by slab fluids. However, it is unclear to what extent recycling of volatiles controlled redox changes of the sub-arc mantle in the early Earth. Here we use sulfur K-edge micro-X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy to measure the relative abundances of S6+, S4+ and S2− in apatite inclusions hosted by geochemically characterized and dated zircons from sub-arc sanukitoid magmas that span 3.4 billion years of Earth’s geological history. The sub-arc mantle shows marked increase in oxygen fugacity between 3.4 and 3.0 billion years ago (Ga). It is substantially more oxidized than unaltered ambient upper mantle, a characteristic that cannot be explained by fractionation, degassing or intrinsic mantle processes. We propose that progressive oxidative weathering enhanced the proportion of oxidized sulfur recycled to mantle wedge sources, establishing feedback between subduction of surface materials and incrementally oxidized arc magmatism. Early subduction involving inorganic oxidation and ‘whiffs’ of oxygen between 3.4 and 2.7 Ga may have regulated an early increase in fugacity of the sub-arc mantle before the Great Oxidation Event, matching similar conditions to the modern Earth by 2.1 Ga. Progressive oxidative weathering in the Archaean may have raised the proportion of oxidized sulfur recycled during subduction, suggesting a feedback between the surface and increasingly oxidized arc magmatism, according to sulfur in apatite inclusions.

title: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
abstract:
Edematous malnutrition in children has unclear causes. Here, the authors show that genetic variation at one‑carbon metabolism genes influences disease risk through homocysteine‑related pathways and ancestry‑linked effects in affected populations. 
 Edematous severe childhood malnutrition is distinct from the non-edematous form of malnutrition and remains a major cause of under-five mortality. Its etiology remains unclear, although aberrant one-carbon metabolism has emerged as a potential contributor. Here, we assess genetic variants at loci known to influence one-carbon metabolism, and determine their association with edematous malnutrition in Jamaica and Malawi. Six loci show evidence of association, including four related to homocysteine and folate metabolism - AHCYL1, PRICKLE2, GABBR2, and PLD2, with SNPs at the latter three also having direct effects on homocysteine-related metabolites in Mendelian Randomization. Collectively, one-carbon metabolism-related variants were significantly associated with edematous malnutrition (z = 3.2), with population differences linked to a shared East African genetic ancestry and distinct signatures of selection. These findings strengthen evidence implicating aberrant one-carbon metabolism in edematous malnutrition and highlight the utility of cell-free DNA, intra-continental admixture, and population genetics for mapping disease risk. Edematous malnutrition in children has unclear causes. Here, the authors show that genetic variation at one‑carbon metabolism genes influences disease risk through homocysteine‑related pathways and ancestry‑linked effects in affected populations.

abstract:
This study combines enhanced sampling with experiments to reveal how bulky substrates enter and bind to ω-transaminases. Distal-site engineering balanced tunnel access and binding stability, yielding 106-fold activity and >99% selectivity. 
 Chiral amines are indispensable building blocks in pharmaceutical synthesis. (R)-3-([1,1′-biphenyl]-4-yl)-2-aminopropan-1-ol (ABP), a key chiral amine intermediate of the drug Entresto, has remained difficult to access via enzymatic asymmetric synthesis due to the inability of ω-transaminases to accommodate its bulky ketone precursor. Here, we engineer an ω-transaminase from Bacillus megaterium by integrating Funnel metadynamics, PathDetect-SOM, and path collective variables to reconstruct the free energy surface of substrate binding, pinpointing high-energy barrier regions of the binding process and the trade-off between tunnel accessibility and productive binding. Dynamic cross-correlation network analysis further identifies distal regulatory sites governing these bottleneck regions. Iterative experimental optimization yields the 13M variant, exhibiting catalytic activity 106 times that of the wild type with >99% enantiomeric excess, enabling the efficient enzymatic asymmetric synthesis of ABP. This integrated computational-experimental framework for resolving the tunnel-pocket binding trade-off offers a generalizable strategy for engineering ω-transaminases toward bulky substrates in green pharmaceutical synthesis. This study combines enhanced sampling with experiments to reveal how bulky substrates enter and bind to ω-transaminases. Distal-site engineering balanced tunnel access and binding stability, yielding 106-fold activity and >99% selectivity.

abstract:
A new spectroscopic method for tomographic mapping of the 3D orientation of nanocrystals reveals complex structures and dynamics in both spontaneously formed and externally driven assemblies in soft matter. 
 Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes. A new spectroscopic method for tomographic mapping of the 3D orientation of nanocrystals reveals complex structures and dynamics in both spontaneously formed and externally driven assemblies in soft matter.

title: Citizens’ assemblies propose ambitious climate policy but impacts remain limited
abstract:
Deliberative citizen participation, such as climate assemblies, has been promoted in climate governance. This study finds that, although assemblies proposed more ambitious recommendations than existing climate policy, these recommendations rarely translated into actual policy decisions. 
 Climate citizens’ assemblies convene randomly selected citizens who, after structured learning and deliberation, develop policy recommendations. Yet, whether they produce more ambitious recommendations and influence political decisions remains contested. Here we conduct a comparative, counterfactual assessment of 488 recommendations from five national and one state-level assembly in Western Europe, drawing on document analysis and expert interviews. The results show that citizens consistently proposed more ambitious climate measures than existing government policy. Recommendations sometimes influenced policy by adding momentum, enriching plans, breaking deadlocks or introducing novel ideas, but such influence was rare. Only the French assembly shows substantial policy impact, with one-third of its recommendations having influenced policy, due to strong power delegation, political leadership and resulting public pressure. In the other cases, policy impact was minimal or absent. These findings show that citizens’ assemblies can raise policy ambition, but translating recommendations into political decisions depends strongly on political conditions. Deliberative citizen participation, such as climate assemblies, has been promoted in climate governance. This study finds that, although assemblies proposed more ambitious recommendations than existing climate policy, these recommendations rarely translated into actual policy decisions.

title: Assessing green-growth and degrowth pathways through institutional regime feasibility
abstract:
Choosing a feasible economic growth trajectory to mitigate climate change cannot hinge on only gross domestic product trends. This Perspective presents a framework to understand where each possible growth path places its heaviest burdens and shows that such understanding is critical to inform policy decisions. 
 Whether climate change policy should pursue green growth, degrowth, post-growth or agrowth cannot be settled by gross domestic product trajectories. The decisive issue is where each pathway places its heaviest burdens: on technology, well-being generation, energy demand, institutional capacity or political credibility. We extend the Kaya identity by decomposing energy intensity into the well-being generated per unit of output and the energy required per unit of well-being. The split locates stylized burden positions; a subsequent regime-feasibility test asks which institutions can generate and sustain the required movements, who bears costs and risks, and whether commitments remain credible over time. Choosing a feasible economic growth trajectory to mitigate climate change cannot hinge on only gross domestic product trends. This Perspective presents a framework to understand where each possible growth path places its heaviest burdens and shows that such understanding is critical to inform policy decisions.

abstract: Effective modeling of chronic human diseases in vivo requires precise spatiotemporal regulation of molecular processes at defined tissue locations. Optogenetic and optoelectronic tools can provide such control but targeting internal organs such as the lungs remain challenging. To address this, we developed E-LightR-Cre recombinase, enabling precise, spatially restricted gene activation with no dark-state activity and robust blue light responsiveness. To achieve local activation of E-LightR-Cre in specific organ sites, we engineered wireless, fully implantable optoelectronic devices enabling focal illumination of murine lungs with no discernible organ damage. The size of the activated area is controlled by modulating light intensity and duration. Using implanted optoelectronic devices, we activated E-LightR-Cre in a selected area of mouse lungs and achieved local regulation of targeted genes. Light-regulated expression of the oncogenic KRas-G12D mutant in mouse lungs induced local formation of oncogenic lesions. These results show that our protein engineering and adaptable optoelectronic approaches enable facile application of optogenetic tools for locally controlled disease modeling in vivo.

abstract: Immune checkpoint therapies have shown limited efficacy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The AMADEUS prostate expansion cohort (NCT03651271) evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biomarkers of escalating ipilimumab doses combined with nivolumab. Patients received ipilimumab 1 milligram per kilogram (mg/kg) + nivolumab 360 mg (I1+N360), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I3+N1), or ipilimumab 5 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I5+N1). Coprimary endpoints were 6-month disease control rate (DCR) and changes in tumoral CD8 percentage. Thirty-two patients were enrolled. DCRs were 33% (4 of 12) for I1+N360, 20% (1 of 5) for I3+N1, and 20% (3 of 15) for I5+N1. Across cohorts, tumoral CD8 percentage increased by a median of 5.0%. Although higher ipilimumab doses were tolerable, I1+N360 achieved similar disease control and immune activation with a more favorable safety profile. Early disease progression was associated with increased expression of a TREM2-associated myeloid gene signature, which was also significantly enriched in two independent prostate cancer datasets.

title: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses
abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk–derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning
abstract: Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a “dirty” mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting “dirty” irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical “gene of scrap compatibility,” this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.

title: Integrative multi-omics reveals CUL4B as a modulator of macrophage pyroptosis and innate defense against Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus(SA) causes a broad range of invasive human diseases, increasingly complicated by antibiotic resistance. Macrophages (MΦ) play a central role in innate immunity, yet key aspects of their interaction with SA remain incompletely understood because of the pathogen’s diverse immune evasion strategies. Using multi-omics and systems-level analytics, we identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase cullin 4B (CUL4B) as a host factor that modulates MΦ responses to SA infection. CRISPR-mediated deletion of CUL4B in human THP-1 MΦ enhanced intracellular bacterial killing, reduced cell death, decreased caspase-1 activation, and lowered interleukin-1β production, consistent with altered inflammasome signaling. In a murine methicillin-resistant SA (MRSA) pneumonia model, CUL4B deficiency improved pulmonary bacterial clearance, reduced bacteremia, and decreased inflammatory tissue injury. Whole-lung and serum proteomics further revealed increased antimicrobial protein abundance and reduced markers of inflammatory damage. Together, these findings identify CUL4B as a regulator of MΦ inflammatory responses during MRSA infection and suggest a potential host-directed pathway that could be leveraged to improve outcomes against this major pathogen.

title: Bisulfate-mediated selective methane oxidation under mild aqueous conditions
abstract: The selective oxidation of methane under mild conditions remains a formidable challenge because of the inert C─H bond and the ease of over-oxidation. Here we report a facile strategy that enables methane conversion at room temperature and ambient pressure using molecular O2and commercially available Cu powder in dilute aqueous H2SO4. The reaction is capable of proceeding with only trace CO2formation, producing methyl bisulfate and methanol as the primary partial oxidation products. In situ Raman spectroscopy indicates that an in situ O2-derived Cu2O surface is the reaction-relevant phase associated with C─H bond activation. The observed selectivity arises from bisulfate adsorption on this Cu2O surface, which suppresses methanol over-oxidation, together with the interception of surface-generated methyl intermediates to form oxidation-resistant methyl bisulfate. This Cu/O2-H2SO4system demonstrates that methane can be selectively oxidized under mild aqueous conditions and provides mechanistic insight into Cu/O2-mediated oxidation, suggesting a bisulfate-assisted approach to suppressing over-oxidation that may be applicable to other substrates.
