title: Breaking the tetrahedral constraint of tetracoordination: Square-planar [ICl4] enables unprecedented birefringence in [C(NH2)3][ICl4]
abstract: Birefringent crystals are indispensable for optoelectronic applications, yet commercially available crystals still suffer from the drawback of insufficient birefringence. Meanwhile, tetracoordination units—traditionally confined to a tetrahedral geometry—have long been sidelined from mainstream high-performance birefringent materials due to their intrinsic nearly negligible polarizability anisotropy. Herein, we break this tetrahedral constraint—demonstrating tetracoordinate square-planar [ICl4] anions as a revolutionary platform for unprecedented birefringence. To achieve this, we report an improved synthesis method that avoids the use of toxic Cl2gas, enabling the preparation of [C(NH2)3][ICl4] featuring square-planar [ICl4] units. This compound displays a birefringence of 0.975@550 nm, setting a new record that surpasses all existing compounds containing tetracoordinate structural units. The giant birefringence of this material is attributed to the strong polarization anisotropy induced by the unique square-planar geometry of the [ICl4] tetracoordinate units. This research provides theoretical guidance for designing high-performance polar materials based on tetracoordinate units in giant birefringent materials and promotes applications in related optoelectronic device.

title: Therapeutic-scale CAR-NK microrobots with programmable swarm navigation for targeted solid tumor therapy
abstract: An urgent requirement in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cell therapy [e.g., CAR–natural killer (NK) cells] for solid tumors is to engineer the cells for precise tumor targeting. Meanwhile, medical microrobots can be navigated toward specific target sites using external magnetic fields. Here, by bridging these approaches, we turn CAR-NK cells into magnetic biohybrid microrobots (CAR-NK microrobots) that achieve controllable long-distance targeted navigation at therapeutic doses (∼106cells) in both murine and nonhuman primate animal models in vivo. CAR-NK microrobots are developed through genetic engineering with CAR structures and loading with magnetic nanoparticles for field-based navigation. Different magnetic field inputs reconfigure their swarms between vortex and ribbon modes, allowing dense aggregation for targeted navigation and further broad dispersion for large-area coverage. Using programmable magnetic fields, in vivo CAR-NK microrobot–based therapy is demonstrated for metastatic leptomeningeal carcinomatosis in brain’s cerebrospinal fluid space. After intrathecal injection, the microrobots are magnetically guided long distance through the spinal canal toward the brain in vortex mode and subsequently spread over the target site in ribbon mode, as visualized by real-time angiographic imaging in a nonhuman primate model, providing a proof-of-feasibility demonstration in a nonhuman primate anatomical setting.

title: A comprehensive phylogenomic framework for brachiopod evolution among lophotrochozoans
abstract: Brachiopods appeared early in the Cambrian radiation and represent an important clade for understanding the origin of animal body plans and the evolution of biomineralized structures. A robust phylogenetic framework of the living representatives is needed to answer persistent questions about the evolution of brachiopod mineralogy, shell morphology, and identification of the brachiopod sister group among Lophotrochozoa. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Brachiopoda and related lophotrochozoan lineages using a comprehensive dataset encompassing all five extant brachiopod orders and using a custom-developed data-refining strategy, compositionally heterogeneous substitution models, and a novel implementation of the parametric-bootstrap likelihood ratio test. We recover monophyly of Lophophorata, with strong support for Brachiopoda as sister to Bryozoa plus Phoronida. Within Brachiopoda, we recover the clade of inarticulated phosphatic Linguliformea sister to the inarticulated calcitic Craniiformea, with both sister to the articulated calcitic Rhynchonellata, with miniaturized Thecideida unexpectedly nested within Terebratulida. Our phylogeny implies that at least one evolutionary transition in primary mineralogy occurred in Brachiopoda, a phenomenon not recognized in any other metazoan group.

title: Extended field-of-view two-photon imaging in the deep brain of freely behaving mice using lightweight microfabricated corrective optics
abstract: Investigating neural circuits underlying complex behavior requires high-resolution imaging of large neuronal populations during naturalistic conditions. Miniaturized two-photon microscopes (MINI2Ps) enable deep brain imaging in freely moving animals when coupled with gradient index (GRIN)-based microendoscopes. However, intrinsic optical aberrations in GRIN-based microendoscopes degrade spatial resolution and limit the effective field-of-view (FOV). Here, we address these limitations using lightweight microfabricated optics to correct GRIN aberrations during deep brain MINI2P imaging. The aberration corrected system demonstrated improved and more homogeneous axial resolution across the FOV, resulting in more than fourfold increase in effective FOV. We applied the corrected system to the ventral posteromedial thalamus in freely moving mice and performed optical mapping of head direction (HD) tuned cells. These measurements revealed the absence of spatial clustering of HD preference, suggesting spatially sparse HD coding in sensory thalamus. Combining the MINI2P with aberration corrected GRIN-based microendoscopes is a powerful approach for large-scale and high-resolution functional imaging of deep brain circuits during naturalistic behavior.

title: Dual Nd isotopic archives in fossil teeth reveal bottom-current control of rare-earth element enrichment in deep-sea sediments
abstract: The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar εNdvalues (∼−5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic εNd(∼−10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the εNdsignature of the fish’s living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins.

title: Programmable and selective silencing of oncogenic fusion transcripts by CRISPR-Cas13b via breakpoint sequence recognition
abstract: Oncogenic gene fusions are key drivers of cancer, yet most remain undruggable by current therapies. Here, we establish CRISPR-PspCas13b as a personalizable platform for systematic silencing of various fusion transcripts. We reveal that recognition and cleavage of the breakpoint sequence byPspCas13b disrupt the fusion transcript, resulting in efficient protein depletion.PspCas13b cleavage produces aberrant, translation-incompetent target RNA species, a subset of which harbors internal deletions proximal to the cleavage site. We demonstrate that targeting the BCR::ABL1 breakpoint sequence efficiently degrades both wild-type and drug-resistant BCR::ABL1 mutants, which are the primary drivers of tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance and relapse in chronic myeloid leukemia. Molecular profiling revealed thatPspCas13b impairs BCR::ABL1 tyrosine phosphokinase activity and triggers extensive transcriptomic and proteomic remodeling, leading to erythroid differentiation and apoptosis in drug-resistant cells. Beyond BCR::ABL1, personalized design ofPspCas13b effectively silences other undruggable oncogenic fusions. Collectively, this study establishes a molecular framework for precise targeting of undruggable or drug-resistant oncogenic transcripts.

title: PINK1-mediated mitophagy supports lung cancer initiation and limits the efficacy of KRAS-targeted therapy
abstract: Mitophagy, the selective degradation of mitochondria by lysosomes, is a major mitochondrial quality-control pathway, yet its role in lung cancer initiation and therapeutic response remains poorly understood. We investigated PINK1-dependent mitophagy in human lung adenocarcinoma and directly monitored mitophagy in vivo using mito-QC reporter mice during lung tumor development. We found that PINK1 activity and mitophagy are increased in human tumors and are activated from the earliest stages of tumorigenesis. Genetic inhibition of PINK1 impaired oncogenic transformation but had little impact once tumor cells were established, identifying mitophagy as a critical early adaptation during lung cancer initiation. PINK1 deficiency markedly enhanced the efficacy ofKRAS-targeted therapy in vitro and in vivo. Together, our findings identify PINK1-dependent mitophagy as an early vulnerability inKRAS-driven lung cancer and provide a rationale for targeting mitophagy to improve the efficacy ofKRAS-targeted therapies.

title: Realignment of ferroelectric nematic by photoinduced electric field
abstract: Liquid crystal displays (LCDs) use thin pixels of a paraelectric nematic, confined between two glass plates with transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. A voltage applied to the electrodes realigns the molecules, changing optical appearance of the pixel. Here, we demonstrate that a similar molecular realignment can be triggered by a low-power light irradiation when the paraelectric nematic in the cell with ITO electrodes is replaced with a ferroelectric nematic (NF). Irradiation creates an intrinsic electric field that is strong enough to realign the NFbut too weak to affect the paraelectric nematic. The extraordinary sensitivity of the ITO/NFpair to light irradiation creates a platform for optical control of ferroelectric polarization and applications in photonics, sensing, smart windows, and beyond.

title: Observation of a supersolid phase in a spin-orbit coupled exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensate
abstract: In Bose-Einstein condensates, spin-orbit coupling (SOC) produces supersolidity. It is a peculiar state of matter, which, in addition to the superfluid behavior, shows periodic density modulation typical for crystals. Here, we report the fabrication of an original type of optical microcavity, allowing the achievement of room-temperature supersolidity for a quantum fluid of light. The microcavity is filled with a nematic liquid crystal (LC) and two layers of the organic polymer methyl-substituted ladder-type poly(p-phenylene) (MeLPPP) hosting exciton resonances. We demonstrate exciton-polariton condensation in the two distinct degenerate minima of the dispersion created by the LC-induced Rashba-Dresselhaus SOC. The condensate real-space distribution shows density stripes located randomly from one condensate realization to another despite the presence of a random disorder potential. This demonstrates the immunity of stripes against disorder and the spontaneous breaking of translational invariance. We also report the random appearance of vortices, another feature of superfluids.

title: Methyltransferase RsmB chaperones E. coli ribosome assembly by orchestrating the recruitment of ribosomal proteins
abstract: Ribosomal RNA modification enzymes increase cellular fitness, but it’s little known whether this benefit arises from rRNA modification or a chaperone function of the modification enzyme. Here, we show thatE. colimethyltransferase RsmB chaperones the initial recruitment of ribosomal proteins to the 16S 3′ domain rRNA, a key step in assembly of the 30S subunit. Real-time single-molecule assembly experiments show that the RsmB product, 16S m5C967, has little effect on the rRNA affinity for ribosomal proteins. Instead, RsmB facilitates stable recruitment of primary protein uS7 during transcription while blocking the addition of secondary protein uS19. Completion of the methyltransferase cycle promotes RsmB release, allowing assembly to continue. Dimethyl sulfate footprinting of trapped RsmB-rRNA complexes revealed that RsmB restructures a critical rRNA helix junction. Our results illustrate how an RNA modification enzyme favors the proper sequence of protein addition by temporarily reshaping the energy landscape of co-transcriptional rRNA folding.

title: Substrate-bound structures of yeast ALA synthase reveal protein dynamics initiating heme biosynthesis
abstract: Heme is an essential prosthetic group involved in multiple biological processes in nearly all organisms. Heme biosynthesis is initiated by the pyridoxal 5′-phosphate–dependent enzyme aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS). Mutations in ALAS cause multiple hematological diseases. Despite sharing approximately 70% sequence similarity, ALAS homologs exhibit distinct expression and regulatory mechanisms. However, the molecular basis for their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we used x-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the structure and dynamics ofSaccharomyces cerevisiaeALAS (scALAS) upon substrate binding. We identified critical conformational changes that occur during catalysis, regulating enzyme activity and protein-protein interactions specific to eukaryotic heme synthesis. Using evolution-guided engineering, we generated scALAS variants with altered catalytic activity and cellular metabolic profiles. Our findings reveal molecular and structural mechanisms underlying heme synthesis regulation and establish a framework for developing targeted therapeutics to treat heme-deficiency disorders and inform a rational design of next-generation therapeutic tools.

title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation
abstract: Bacteriophages (“phage”) are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motileEscherichia coliencountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless “escape parameter,” in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection. This work thus provides mechanistic insight into how cell motility shapes phage-bacteria interactions in spatially extended environments.

title: Global River Sediment Retention on Delta Plains
abstract: Fluvial sediments have helped form approximately 830,000 km2 of coastal deltaic land, a large part of which since the Holocene slowdown of global sea‐level rise. The rate at which deltas have retained fluvial sediment to build deltaic land, however, has varied greatly between different deltas. Sources of variability as well as global estimates of sediment retention remain poorly resolved, limiting the assessment of future delta change. Here, we compare delta area and thickness against fluvial sediment supply to derive estimates of delta plain sediment retention for ∼1,700 deltas, representing 93% of the global fluvial sediment supply. We find that 28% ± 14% (standard error of the mean) of the global fluvial sediment discharge is retained on delta plains, totaling 5.8 Gt per year, and equating to roughly 4.3 mm yr−1 as a global average sedimentation rate. The average delta, however, retains much less, about 4% ± 1%, because many smaller deltas do not retain much sediment. We observe a large difference between active and passive margins, with sediment retention much higher along the latter. Tide‐dominated deltas have the most efficient morphology, and retain 11% ± 4% on average but up to 70% when weighted by sediment flux. This is much higher than the 7% ± 2% and 2% ± 1% retained by river‐ and wave‐dominated deltas, respectively. As larger deltas retain a greater proportion of their supply, this study suggests a positive feedback that enables larger deltas to grow faster than smaller ones.

title: Million‐Year Scale Hydrothermal and Hydrocarbon Evolution Hosted Within Stratified Thermohydraulic Systems in Sedimented Ultraslow‐Spreading Settings, Svyatogor and Vestnesa Ridges
abstract: Hydrothermal systems at ultraslow‐spreading ridges are poorly understood, especially where thick sediments overlay detachment faults. The International Ocean Discovery Program Expedition 403 obtained the longest sediment record in Atlantic‐Arctic ultraslow‐spreading systems, reaching ∼628 m below the seafloor. Heat‐flow measurements, fluid geochemistry, and mineralogical analyses, combined with seismic interpretation, revealed thermohydraulic systems within two contourite drifts on ridge flanks. The Svyatogor Ridge site exhibits extreme heat flow and crustal‐fluid migration from two detachment faults, accompanied by newly documented thermogenic hydrocarbons, resulting in stratified thermohydraulic systems. The Vestnesa Ridge site exhibits moderate heat flow, and partial crustal‐fluid migration suggests developing thermohydraulic systems. The results reveal complex, long‐lived hydrothermal systems in the present day with significant, previously poorly understood reservoirs of geological carbon and suggest their million‐year‐scale evolution. This study advances understanding of fluid dynamics, fluid‐sediment interactions, and carbon cycling in sedimented ultraslow‐spreading ridge environments.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning Reveals Global Nonlinear Responses of Soil Respiration to Climate
abstract: Soil respiration (Rs) is a major component of the global carbon cycle, yet its responses to environmental drivers remain poorly constrained. Using 8,111 observations and a SHAP‐interpreted Random Forest model, we identified global response patterns for key environmental drivers of Rs. Temperature contributions showed a peaked association with a descriptive maximum of 27.7°C, precipitation contributions plateaued at high values, and leaf area index contributions increased approximately linearly. These results provide a global, data‐driven characterization of peaked temperature and saturating precipitation associations, including how their shapes and supported ranges vary among climate zones. Our results indicate that monotonic assumptions in Earth system models may overlook important nonlinearities and potentially bias estimates of terrestrial carbon flux responses to seasonal climate extremes. Interpretable machine learning therefore provides a transparent framework for evaluating and improving the representation of soil carbon dynamics under climate change.

authors: R. Minetto;Z. Wang;O. Lengliné;J. Schmittbuhl
title: Analysis of the Correlation Between Post‐Injection Wellhead Pressure Decay and Trailing Seismicity
abstract: Fluid injection during reservoir stimulation aims to enhance reservoir permeability but induces seismic activity that persists for hours to months after injection has stopped. In this study, we investigate the correlation between the post‐injection wellhead pressure decay and the decrease in seismicity rate using data from multiple Enhanced Geothermal Systems injection operations characterized by an abrupt shut‐in. We evaluated several statistical models to represent the seismicity rate and the pressure decay. Using the best fitting model, we show that the time required to reach a given fraction of the initial seismicity rate and of the initial pressure are correlated, with the pressure relaxation being longer than the seismicity rate relaxation. No correlation is observed between seismicity decay and injection parameters such as injection volume, average injection pressure, or injection duration. These observations suggest that the relaxation of the pore pressure drives the decrease in seismicity, which has strong implications for reservoir management.

explanation: 该论文主要研究气候变暖对部落土地上洪水响应的影响，使用高分辨率水动力学模型进行模拟。虽然涉及大气环境变化，但重点在于洪水和水资源管理，而非大气环境遥感技术，如空气质量监测、卫星观测或大气成分分析等。

title: Flood Responses to Climate Warming on Tribal Lands Using High‐Resolution Hydrodynamic Modeling
abstract: Tribal nations across the United States face disproportionate flood impacts yet remain significantly underrepresented in national‐scale assessments, creating a critical equity gap in climate adaptation. We address this deficiency through a climate‐to‐local‐inundation framework for the Santee Sioux Nation, Nebraska, by forcing 10‐m hydrodynamic simulations with a 42‐year paired historical and pseudo‐global‐warming CONUS404 runoff event set. Results show that projected changes in inundation frequency and flood depth are limited, with no evidence of widespread intensification of flood extremes. Instead, changes manifest as localized adjustments in floodplain activation and tributary connectivity. Pixel‐wise return‐period analysis shows small changes in flood depth and only minor deviations in the statistical structure of extremes. These findings demonstrate a transferable pathway for translating climate‐driven hydrologic forcing into locally resolved inundation information for under‐mapped Tribal lands.

title: Sandy Turbidity Current Acts as a Rusty Carbon Pump at the Shelf Edge
abstract: Sandy turbidity currents (STCs) efficiently sequester organic carbon (OC) through rapid burial. Yet our understanding of OC preservation within STC deposits remains far less constrained, especially considering STC deposits as an inferred major sink for iron‐bound OC (Fe‐OC), a long‐term stabilized form of OC. Here, we investigate a sediment core with five STC events from the northern slope of the South China Sea (SCS) and compare our observations against a globally compiled sedimentary Fe‐OC data set synthesized from published literature. We demonstrate that STC deposits host a higher Fe‐OC contribution (22.1% ± 7.6%) than background deposits. STCs drive rapid Fe‐OC transportation from shelf to slope under elevated accumulation rates (185.4 ± 84.6 g m−2 time−1). This process shields Fe‐OC from remineralization and favors the formation of refractory OC stabilized within iron matrices. We propose that STCs constitute a “rusty carbon pump,” and that continental slopes represent potential hotspots for long‐term Fe‐OC preservation.

title: Offshore Freshened Groundwater Distribution Is Controlled by Along‐ and Cross‐Shore Topographic Variability
abstract: Offshore Freshened Groundwater (OFG) reservoirs are regarded as a potentially significant resource stored in continental shelves. While the role of subsurface geological conditions in controlling OFG has been widely recognized, the influence of the topography of the hosting continental shelf on OFG evolution remains poorly understood. Here, using generalized numerical modeling representative of a broad range of systems worldwide, we evaluate how the shelf slope affects the evolution of OFG in subsea aquifers, considering sea‐level rise over paleohydrogeological timescales. Our findings show that shallow dipping shelves are expected to have greater extents of OFG by up to 2.8 times and enhance the longevity of OFG preservation. Crucially, natural‐scale alongshore slope variability substantially influences the cross‐shore salt distribution. Considering alongshore flow shows that cross‐sectional analyses can overestimate OFG volumes by up to 3 times. These findings highlight the significance of shelf slope and lateral (alongshore) dynamics in estimating and predicting OFG resources.

title: Adaptation Potential of Local Water Management Practices to Glacier Loss
abstract: Climate change disproportionately affects mountain river basins, driving cryospheric changes and altering their hydrology. This has detrimental impacts on water resources, accentuating the need for robust adaptation strategies. Traditional engineering approaches can provide buffering capacity but are associated with high costs and limited flexibility. At the same time, local, small scale water management practices are gaining attention, yet evidence on their effectiveness remains limited. We evaluate the adaptation potential of common local practices, that is, headwater grassland regeneration, small surface storage, and artificial recharge, in the Vilcanota‐Urubamba system, Peru. We find that, if properly managed, these interventions can substantially contribute to seasonal and interannual hydrological buffering and dry season water availability. However, when implemented in isolation, they are unlikely to fully offset climate impacts. Our results support the design of catchment‐scale intervention portfolios for adaptation planning, with a combination of large, centralized infrastructure and distributed local interventions likely to provide the most effective solution.

title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
abstract:
Water structures govern the behaviour of solutes across aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. Here the authors use weakly hydrated anions to reshape hydration in the bulk and at interfaces, thereby regulating amine monomer partitioning and interfacial transport while suppressing acyl chloride hydrolysis during polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization. 
 Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. As typical chaotropic Hofmeister ions, weakly hydrated anions (WHAs) can reshape hydration structures and accumulate at water–hydrophobe interfaces. Notably, WHAs paradoxically suppress the solubility of certain small-molecule monomers in water while enhancing that of chemically analogous polymers. Here, we exploit WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control to regulate polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization (IP), using the piperazine (PIP) and trimesoyl chloride (TMC) nanofiltration system as the primary model. Introducing WHAs into the aqueous phase reduces the affinity of amine monomers for water and accelerates partitioning into the reaction front in the oil phase, remarkably reinforcing IP self-limitation. Simultaneously, interfacial WHA enrichment lowers interfacial tension and, together with accelerated amine delivery, potentially intensifies transport-driven interfacial instabilities. WHAs also lower interfacial water availability, attenuating acyl chloride hydrolysis. These synergistic effects yield hollow-ridged polyamide selective layers with reduced thickness and high crosslinking density, delivering enhanced water permeance and salt rejection. Crucially, module-scale fabrication of high-performance membranes demonstrates that WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control is directly compatible with established desalination pipelines. title: Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks
abstract:
Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, the authors report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light as the sole chiral director. 
 Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, we report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light (CP-λ) as the sole chiral director. By exploiting the reversibility of imine condensation, a dynamic self-correction process amplifies the photonic chiral bias into long-range crystalline order without any chiral auxiliaries. Unlike conventional strategies that rely on localized chiral centers, our approach induces chirality directly within the emissive framework backbone. This structural integration results in a luminescence dissymmetry factor of 0.24, representing a substantial value for purely organic systems. Furthermore, we demonstrate spatially programmable encoding with sub-micrometer resolution, enabling the transcription of complex enantiomeric patterns into the frameworks. This methodology establishes a reagent-free platform for the manufacturing of chiral crystalline materials and advances the development of programmable photonic devices. title: Brassinosteroids improve nitrogen utilization by antagonizing BIN2-mediated SnRK1 activation
abstract:
Brassinosteroids are widely used in agriculture, but their modes of action remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that brassinosteroids inhibit BIN2, leading to KIN10 degradation and activation of gene expression and nitrogen assimilation enzymes. 
 Nitrogen is an essential nutrient for plant growth and development, and is central to increasing crop yield. Brassinosteroids (BRs) and their analogs are widely used in agriculture to enhance crop yields and improve nitrogen utilization, yet the underlying mechanism remains fragmentary. Here, we demonstrate that BR conservatively improves nitrogen utilization by modulating the activity of SnRK1, an evolutionarily conserved regulator balancing carbon and nitrogen metabolism. Exogenous BR application increases plant biomass and nitrogen utilization, and enhances key nitrogen assimilation enzyme activities when photosynthesis is inhibited. Metabolomic reveals that BR restores 47.8% of metabolic alterations caused by photosynthetic suppression. Mechanistically, BIN2, a key kinase in BR signaling, interacts with and phosphorylates KIN10, the catalytic α-subunit of SnRK1, at conserved Thr175 and Ser179, thereby stabilizing KIN10. BR inhibits BIN2, promoting KIN10 degradation and thereby activating nitrate-responsive gene expression and enhancing nitrogen assimilation. These findings reveal how BR signaling enhances nitrogen utilization and offer insights for improving crop productivity and sustainability. title: Size-dependent catalysis of Ru nanoparticles for selective reductive amination of PET plastic
abstract:
Turning waste plastic into valuable chemicals requires precise control of competing reactions. This study shows that tuning ruthenium particle size enables selective conversion of polyethylene terephthalate into p-xylylenediamine. 
 Converting waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plastic into high-value p-xylylenediamine (PXDA) is a revolutionary solution to alleviate energy shortages and plastic pollution. However, current catalytic methods are often limited by poor chemoselectivity due to uncontrolled reductive amination and hydrodeoxygenation capabilities. Herein, we report a precision strategy to regulate the aggregation state of Ru on nitrogen-doped carbon, enabling size-dependent control of reaction pathways in the reductive amination of PET. Ultrasmall Ru nanoclusters (~1.3 nm) favor over-hydrogenation to 1,4-cyclohexanedimethanamine, whereas larger Ru nanoparticles (~4.6 nm) promote excessive hydrodeoxygenation to p-xylene. Notably, Ru/NC-SNPs (~2.4 nm) gives a high PXDA yield of 95.5% with a low apparent activation barrier (30.8 kJ/mol) under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies indicate that Ru/NC-SNPs achieve an optimal balance between hydrogen activation and amidation activity, thereby enabling selective amidation through the controlled dehydrogenation of the amide intermediate. The catalyst also demonstrates broad applicability for post-consumer PET, mixed plastics containing PET and other polyester plastics. Techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessments further confirm the economic viability and environmental benefits of this process. This work establishes a size-governed selectivity paradigm for Ru-based catalysts and provides a general strategy for steering competing pathways in heterogeneous reductive amination toward sustainable PET valorization. This study shows that tuning ruthenium particle size enables selective conversion of polyethylene terephthalate into p-xylylenediamine.

title: ADAM17 is a broad HIV-1 restriction factor targeted by Nef to restore Env maturation
abstract:
Here, the authors show that the cell-surface protein ADAM17 blocks HIV-1 by preventing maturation of the viral envelope protein, while the viral protein Nef counteracts this effect by redirecting ADAM17 out of infected cells. 
 HIV-1 uses the accessory protein Nef to enhance the infectivity of newly produced virus particles, but the host defenses counteracted by Nef remain incompletely defined. The membrane protein SERINC5 contributes to this defense but primarily restricts laboratory-adapted HIV-1 strains, suggesting that other cellular factors influence the requirement for Nef. Here we show that ADAM17, a cell-surface protein best known for cleaving inflammatory mediators, restricts both laboratory-adapted and primary HIV-1 isolates. ADAM17 acts independently of its enzymatic activity: its signal peptide, which normally directs proteins into the cellular secretory pathway, binds the HIV-1 envelope precursor gp160 and retains it in the endoplasmic reticulum. This prevents envelope maturation, transport to the cell surface and incorporation into virus particles, thereby reducing viral infectivity. Nef counteracts this restriction through a PxxP protein-interaction motif that promotes the release of ADAM17 in extracellular vesicles, reducing its abundance within cells and restoring envelope maturation. Disruption of ADAM17 in CD4-positive T-cell lines and primary human lymphocytes reduced the requirement for Nef during viral replication. These findings establish ADAM17 as a regulator of HIV-1 envelope production and show how Nef redirects host-cell trafficking to promote the formation of infectious virus particles. title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds
abstract:
Diabetes impairs wound healing by disrupting macrophage metabolism and angiogenesis. Here, authors identify macrophage-specific transketolase (TKT) as a metabolic checkpoint and develop a nanozyme hydrogel that restores macrophage TKT to promote vascular repair in diabetic wounds. 
 Diabetic wound healing is profoundly impaired by macrophage metabolic dysfunction, which compromises angiogenesis. Here, we show a macrophage transketolase (TKT) as a crucial metabolic checkpoint governing vascular regeneration in diabetes. We demonstrate that loss of TKT in macrophages accelerates amino acid and fatty acid catabolism, elevates reactive oxygen species, and disrupts endothelial cell proliferation and differentiation. Mechanistically, hyperglycemia activates the AGEs-RAGE signaling cascade through suppressing TKT expression, establishing a pathological TKT-AGEs-RAGE axis that reprograms macrophage metabolism toward dysfunction. Then, we engineer a nanozyme-integrated hydrogel patch that selectively increases TKT level in macrophages, which rebalances macrophage metabolism, reduces oxidative stress, and rescues angiogenic capacity. In a diabetic pig model, localized delivery of the nano-system markedly accelerates wound closure and vascular repair. These findings not only elucidate a macrophage-specific TKT metabolic reprogramming mechanism for enhancing angiogenesis, but also offer a potential therapeutic strategy for the clinical management of diabetic wounds. Here, authors identify macrophage-specific transketolase (TKT) as a metabolic checkpoint and develop a nanozyme hydrogel that restores macrophage TKT to promote vascular repair in diabetic wounds.

title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
abstract:
Batteries require safe electrolytes without compromising performance. Here, the authors develop a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage, long-lasting, and safe lithium-ion batteries. 
 Achieving high energy density without compromising safety remains a significant challenge for advanced batteries. Nonflammable electrolytes can mitigate fire risk, but poor bulk and interfacial properties of such electrolytes limit their application. Here, a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate electrolyte was developed, achieving a self-extinguishing time of ~0 s and stable cycling in both lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries under high-voltage conditions. The electrolyte comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride, fluoroethylene carbonate, and ethyl methyl carbonate at low concentration establishes a weakly solvating environment, wherein dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride and fluoroethylene carbonate preferentially contribute to stabilize the positive and negative electrodes, while working together to enhance the rate capability, low-temperature performance, and long-term cycling at high-voltage. Accelerating rate calorimetry revealed a delayed thermal runaway onset by 87 °C, correlating with Broadness Index. These findings suggest that preemptive passivation on both electrodes, when coupled with nonflammable electrolyte design, can provide a viable route toward safe, high-energy lithium batteries. Batteries require safe electrolytes without compromising performance. Here, the authors develop a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage, long-lasting, and safe lithium-ion batteries.

title: Artificial intelligence for life-cycle-aware sustainable materials discovery
abstract:
Materials discovery by artificial intelligence rarely considers scalability, environmental impacts or end-of-life management, prioritizing functional performance. This Perspective suggests a roadmap for embedding life-cycle considerations in the discovery process to design sustainable materials from the start. 
 Artificial intelligence has accelerated the discovery of new materials, offering a route towards sustainable development. Candidates are nevertheless evaluated almost exclusively on functional performance. Whether a material can be manufactured at scale, how it behaves once built into a real product, what burden its production places on the environment and what becomes of it at the end of its life are questions addressed only after the choice has been settled, when little can be altered. Bringing these considerations into the discovery process itself is achievable and would yield materials that are sustainable not by accident but by design. This Perspective suggests a roadmap for embedding life-cycle considerations in the discovery process to design sustainable materials from the start.

title: Small-molecule-bound biopolymer networks for sustainable multifunctional composites
abstract:
Combining biomaterials of different nature can yield sustainable composites with otherwise inaccessible properties. This study presents a strategy to overcome interfacial mismatch between individual components, enabling efficient structural integration within mechanically strong, multifunctional films. 
 Multicomponent biopolymer networks are promising platforms for developing sustainable materials. However, weak coupling across mismatched heterointerfaces of different biomaterials limits structural coherence, load transfer and functional integration. Here we establish a natural small-molecule-mediated non-covalent heterointerfacial reorganization strategy and validate it using a collagen–Ganoderma lucidum mycelium–plant-derived anthocyanin (CMpA) model system. By combining molecular simulations, interfacial spectroscopy, mesoscale structural analysis and mechanical modelling, we resolve a cross-scale pathway in which anthocyanin-associated non-covalent contacts at local heterointerfaces are translated into pore-wall consolidation, lamellar orientational coherence and continuous load transfer. This cross-scale structural integration yielded CMpA films with a tensile strength of 63.55 MPa, along with UV-shielding, antioxidant and antibacterial properties, reduced oxygen and water-vapour transmission, and pH-responsive freshness indication, making them promising candidates for active and intelligent packaging. More broadly, the work links small-molecule-mediated local interfacial chemistry with mesoscale anisotropic network formation and macroscopic functional integration, offering a design principle for sustainable biopolymer materials that require both mechanical coherence and multifunctionality. This study presents a strategy to overcome interfacial mismatch between individual components, enabling efficient structural integration within mechanically strong, multifunctional films.

title: Subglacial landforms as proxy for offshore freshened groundwater in formerly glaciated margins
abstract:
Regionally extensive offshore freshened groundwater systems linked to past glaciation can be predicted by subglacial landforms, suggests a study that integrated controlled-source electromagnetic data with high-resolution seismic reflection surveys in the southeastern North Sea. 
 Offshore freshened groundwater (OFG) is a significant yet underexplored component of the global water cycle, and its spatial distribution, particularly its links to past glacial processes, remains poorly constrained. The southeastern North Sea, characterized by extensive tunnel valley networks, provides an ideal setting to test how Pleistocene meltwater shaped offshore groundwater systems. Using newly acquired time-domain controlled-source electromagnetic data integrated with high-resolution seismic reflection surveys, we present a resistivity-based mapping of OFG in this region. The models reveal a laterally continuous OFG body with resistivities of 8–14 Ω·m, extending across multiple stratigraphic units and well beyond individual subglacial landforms. This configuration is best explained by subglacial meltwater flushing of sediment porewaters during Pleistocene glaciations. Subsequent preservation was aided by density contrasts that limit vertical mixing and by fine-grained glaciomarine deposits sealing the system from above. The connection between resistivity anomalies and mapped subglacial landforms shows that the latter can serve as predictive proxies for OFG occurrence. These findings shift the perspective from OFG as isolated anomalies to regionally extensive systems linked to glacial processes, establishing subglacial landforms as a testable screening proxy for locating OFG in formerly glaciated margins worldwide. title: Age‐Period‐Cohort Analysis of the Global Death Burden of Main Diseases Attributable to High Temperature in the Past 30 Years: Based on the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
abstract: High temperatures pose a serious threat to human health. Quantifying the main disease death burden attributable to high temperatures can provide scientific evidence for policy development. Using Global Burden of Disease 2021 data, we identified the death burden attributable to high temperatures across all causes and determined the three leading causes. For each, we used age‐standardized mortality rates attributable to high temperature (HA‐ASMR) and estimated temporal trends via age‐period‐cohort modeling at global, regional, and national levels (1990–2021). Ischemic heart disease, stroke, and lower respiratory infections were the top three causes of deaths attributable to high temperature in 2021. Low‐middle Socio‐demographic Index (SDI) regions had the highest HA‐ASMR for ischemic heart disease (3.49, 95%UI: 0.96–6.57) and stroke (2.55, 95%UI: 0.77–5.01), whereas lower respiratory infections showed the highest HA‐ASMR in low SDI regions (2.52, 95%UI: 0.85–4.35). Age‐period‐cohort analysis generated net drift values for HA‐ASMR in high SDI regions, with values of 0.99% (95%CI: 0.60%–1.39%) for ischemic heart disease, 1.19% (95%CI: 0.99%–1.40%) for stroke, and 2.36% (95%CI: 2.01%–2.70%) for lower respiratory infections. Longitudinal age curves showed elevated mortality risks attributable to high temperature in populations over 60 years. Global period and cohort rate ratios for high‐temperature‐attributable ischemic heart disease mortality increased over time. Global ischemic heart disease and stroke deaths attributable to high temperature continued rising with sharply elevated risks in older adults, while lower respiratory infection deaths attributable to high temperature among youth in high‐income countries are increasing. Therefore, adaptation strategies must be specific to disease and age, varying by regional characteristics.

title: Solvent heterogeneity regulates assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization
abstract:
Supramolecular polymers often require solvent mixtures for their preparation but their impact on supramolecular polymerization remains poorly understood. Here, the authors demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect determined by monomer structure. 
 Supramolecular polymers are fundamental mimics of biological assemblies with diverse functions. However, predicting monomer solubility and controlling the colloidal stability of the resulting assemblies in solution remain major challenges. As a result, their preparation commonly relies on solvent mixtures, which can generate local heterogeneities during sample processing—an effect that remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect modulated by monomer structure. Using an amphiphilic Pd(II) complex as a model system, we uncover a thermally accelerated transition from kinetically controlled discrete nanostructures to thermodynamically stable supramolecular polymers in water/1,4-dioxane mixtures. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that this transformation is mediated by microscopic liquid–liquid phase separation within the mixed solvent, creating 1,4-dioxane-enriched microdomains with increased local monomer concentration. Thermal annealing enhances molecular mobility and promotes the growth and coalescence of these microdomains, facilitating the transition to one-dimensional fibers. Extending the investigation to structurally related monomers further identifies the metal center and hydrogen-bonding motifs as key design elements governing this behavior. By linking molecular design and solvent heterogeneity to pathway complexity, our findings highlight how mixed solvents can be used to control supramolecular polymerization. Supramolecular polymers often require solvent mixtures for their preparation but their impact on supramolecular polymerization remains poorly understood. Here, the authors demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect determined by monomer structure.

title: Bacteroides–Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile
abstract:
Here the authors demonstrate that interactions between Bacteroides and Escherichia shape resistance to Clostridioides difficile and identify ecological and metabolic signatures with the potential to guide microbiome-based therapies. 
 Commensal gut bacteria are key contributors to the resilience against pathogen invasion. This is exemplified by the success of faecal microbiota transplantation in treating recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection. Yet, characteristics of communities that can confer colonisation resistance and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. Here we use a synthetic community of 14 commensal gut bacteria to uncover inter-species interactions and metabolic pathways underpinning the emergent resilience against C. difficile invasion. We challenged this synthetic community as well as faecal-matter-derived communities with antibiotic treatment and C. difficile in a continuous flow bioreactor. Using generalised Lotka-Volterra and genome-scale metabolic modelling, we identified interactions between Escherichia coli and Bacteroides/Phocaeicola sp. as key to the pathogen’s suppression. Metabolomics and targeted validation experiments revealed that fructan-derived fructooligosaccharides, vitamin B3 biosynthesis, and competition for Stickland metabolism precursors causally contribute to suppression across multiple C. difficile strains and donor backgrounds. Analysis of metagenomics data from patient cohorts and clinical trials attested the in vivo relevance of the identified metabolic pathways and the ratio between Bacteroides and Escherichia in successful colonisation resistance. The latter was found to be a stronger discriminator than commonly used alpha diversity metrics. Together, our study uncovers emergent microbial interactions in pathogen resistance with implications for rational design of bacteriotherapies. Here the authors demonstrate that interactions between Bacteroides and Escherichia shape resistance to Clostridioides difficile and identify ecological and metabolic signatures with the potential to guide microbiome-based therapies.

title: Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling
abstract:
This study reveals distinct cell-wall organization in two pathogenic Cryptococcus species, revealing that chitosan loss triggers species-specific structural remodeling that may influence host interactions. 
 Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are fungal pathogens that cause life-threatening infections, including cryptococcal meningitis. A distinctive feature of the cryptococcal cell wall is the extensive deacetylation of chitin to chitosan, a modification that is essential for virulence but whose structural role in cell-wall organization remains poorly understood. Here, we analyze the cell walls of wild-type strains of both species and their avirulent chitosan-deficient mutants, which serve as vaccine candidates. Loss of chitosan disrupted cell morphology and altered cell-wall ultrastructure, with more pronounced defects in C. neoformans. Solid-state NMR reveals that aggregated α-(1→3)-glucans form the principal rigid domain of the cell wall in both species and are closely associated with chitin microfibrils, whereas surrounding β-glucans and mannoproteins constitute a more dynamic matrix. Chitosan modulates hydration and flexibility, and its loss increases chitin exposure and triggers species-specific remodeling of the polysaccharide network. In C. neoformans, chitosan depletion increased α-(1→3)-glucan content and reduced β-glucan levels, whereas C. gattii selectively lost one α-(1→3)-glucan subtype while maintaining β-glucan levels. Although capsule production remained intact, chitosan deficiency altered glucuronoxylomannan linkage patterns and mannoprotein composition. These findings reveal how chitosan organizes cryptococcal cell-wall architecture and highlight distinct structural adaptation strategies among pathogenic Cryptococcus species. This study reveals distinct cell-wall organization in two pathogenic Cryptococcus species, revealing that chitosan loss triggers species-specific structural remodeling that may influence host interactions.

title: High-resolution global groundwater storage anomalies:  a 1 km downscaled dataset
abstract:
We created a global monthly groundwater dataset at 1 km resolution for 2002–2020 by combining satellite observations, environmental data, and machine learning. The dataset reveals spatial groundwater variations that are difficult to see in coarse satellite observations. Evaluation with monitoring wells and regional studies supports its use for broad groundwater assessment, while local and seasonal interpretation should be checked against additional observations. 
 Groundwater depletion poses a challenge to water security, but the coarse spatial resolution of Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) observations limits the characterization of groundwater variability at regional and local scales. Here, we present a 1 km monthly global groundwater storage anomaly (GWSA) dataset covering April 2002–December 2020. The dataset was generated using Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) for temporal gap filling, 19 high-resolution hydroclimatic and geophysical predictors, and aquifer-stratified machine-learning downscaling. Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and deep neural networks (DNN) were evaluated as candidate models, and XGBoost was selected for dataset production based on internal, cross-scale, and in-situ evaluations. When aggregated to the original GRACE scale, the 1 km product agreed closely with the original GWSA (R2 = 0.972, RMSE = 2.10 cm). Independent evaluation used a global archive of 152 069 groundwater-monitoring wells and a 1° spatial-block calibration–validation design. Effective specific yield (Syeff) was estimated from calibration blocks and transferred to held-out blocks before comparison at a common 0.25° grid. For XGBoost, the held-out evaluation yielded R2 = 0.538, RMSE = 0.378 cm yr−1, and Bias = 0.106 cm yr−1. The association between modeled and observation-derived trends remained similar under ± 30 % perturbations in Syeff, although amplitude-related metrics were more sensitive to the conversion coefficient. Standardized time-series comparisons and monthly evaluations of representative aquifers showed better agreement for long-term variability than for seasonal variability. Comparisons with published regional estimates showed close agreement in the North China Plain, weaker depletion magnitudes in northwestern India and California, and a trend-sign mismatch in the High Plains Aquifer during 2003–2013. Experiments using CSR, JPL, H08, and WaterGAP also showed that reconstruction performance and predictor importance depend on the target product. The dataset provides kilometre-scale estimates of groundwater-storage variability under the large-scale GRACE constraint. Local interpretation of the reconstructed spatial patterns requires additional groundwater-level, abstraction, and hydrogeological observations. The 1 km monthly global GWSA dataset is openly available from the National Cryosphere Desert Data Center at https://doi.org/10.12072/ncdc.hydrology.db7323.2026 (Fan et al., 2026).

title: Improving photosynthate allocation dynamic simulations  of crops under water stress conditions
abstract:
This study improves the Agro-C model to better represent how crops respond to changing soil moisture. The updated model adjusts carbon allocation between roots and leaves according to soil moisture and growth stage, and also accounts for leaf aging under water stress. Tests with field data for maize and wheat showed better predictions of plant growth above and below ground. The results can improve estimates of crop production and soil carbon storage under future drought and climate change. 
 Accurately simulating crop photosynthate allocation under water stress is critical for predicting both food security and ecosystem carbon inputs. Current crop models often rely on static or growth-stage-fixed allocation coefficients, which limits their ability to capture the physiological plasticity of crops responding to fluctuating environmental conditions. This study develops a water-driven, stage-dependent carbon allocation scheme within the Agro-C model to better represent crop responses to soil moisture variability. The scheme dynamically adjusts photosynthate allocation coefficients for roots (PR) and leaves (PL), integrates the yellow-to-green leaf ratio (YGR), and incorporates a water stress-induced leaf senescence module. By coupling carbon allocation to both soil moisture and crop development, the approach improves the representation of physiologically regulated allocation processes and enhances the realism of crop simulations. Model evaluation using extensive observation datasets for maize and wheat demonstrates substantial improvements in simulation accuracy, with R2 values reaching 0.77–0.95 for aboveground biomass (AGB) and 0.62–0.83 for belowground biomass (BGB). These results underscore the importance of dynamically representing carbon allocation under water stress and offer an improved framework for simulating carbon–water interactions in agroecosystems.

title: Classification of Summer Extratropical Cyclones Over Northeast China and Their Impacts on Regional Precipitation
abstract: Based on the ERA5 six‐hourly reanalysis data set and objective identification and tracking methods for extratropical cyclones (ECs), this study identified 423 summer ECs that passed through Northeast China (NEC) during 1979–2023. These ECs were categorized into three distinct types using K‐means clustering based on their genesis locations. We further examined the associated atmospheric circulation patterns and the resulting climatic impacts of each EC type on summer precipitation over NEC. The results indicate that: Type 1 (47.04%) originates from NEC and eastern Mongolia, driven by the southward development of an upper‐level trough over the west of Lake Baikal, accompanied by pronounced westerly anomalies. Type 2 (27.66%) originates from western and central Mongolia. Its formation involves an upper‐level trough extending from western Mongolia to the region west of Lake Baikal, accompanied by significant westerly anomalies over central‐western Mongolia and NEC. Both Type 1 and Type 2 primarily track eastward, inducing moisture transport anomalies from the western boundary into NEC, producing precipitation over the northern and central parts. In contrast, Type 3 (25.30%) originates from the eastern coastal regions of China. Driven by a deepening upper‐level trough from North China to NEC and enhanced westerlies toward the Sea of Japan, these ECs move northeastward, steering significant moisture flux anomalies from the southern boundary into the region, producing precipitation over the southern and central parts. This study provides a new perspective on the mechanisms of regional precipitation over NEC.

title: Trade-offs between soil inorganic and organic carbon driven by multiple global environmental changes
abstract:
Global environmental changes can induce contrasting responses of soil organic and inorganic carbon, according to an 8-year field experiment in a semi-arid grassland and a meta-analysis. 
 Dryland ecosystems store large amounts of both soil organic and inorganic carbon, yet the responses of soil inorganic carbon to global environmental change remain largely overlooked despite the potential vulnerability of this carbon pool. Here we aim to determine how soil inorganic and organic carbon respond to multiple global change drivers (warming, reactive nitrogen input and altered precipitation) using an 8-year field manipulation experiment in a semi-arid grassland and a meta-analysis based on 44 observations. We found that altered precipitation has no effect on soil inorganic carbon, but warming and nitrogen input interactively affect it. Specifically, nitrogen input alone does not affect soil inorganic carbon, but it increases soil inorganic carbon loss (~9.1%) when combined with climate warming. This inorganic carbon loss co-occurs with enhanced microbial nitrogen mineralization and nitrification, suggesting that enhancement of proton production due to nitrification controls soil inorganic carbon dissolution and persistence. Furthermore, both the field study and meta-analysis show that nitrogen input and/or warming induce contrasting changes in soil inorganic and organic carbon, suggesting a trade-off between soil inorganic and organic carbon under these two major global change drivers. These results highlight the need to account for the vulnerability of soil inorganic carbon when predicting dryland carbon dynamics under future climate change scenarios. Global environmental changes can induce contrasting responses of soil organic and inorganic carbon, according to an 8-year field experiment in a semi-arid grassland and a meta-analysis.

title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
abstract:
In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Here, the authors directly observe the corresponding Lindhard continuum in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. 
 Understanding the excitations of quantum materials is essential for unraveling how their microscopic constituents interact. Among these, particle-hole excitations form a particularly important class, as they govern fundamental processes such as screening, dissipation, and transport. In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Although central to the theory of Fermi liquids, the corresponding Lindhard continuum has remained experimentally elusive. Here we report its direct observation in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. We resolve a linearly dispersing excitation with velocity comparable to the Fermi velocity and find quantitative agreement with simulations of the non-interacting charge susceptibility. A detailed analysis and decomposition of the simulations reveal the intra-band origin of this low-energy excitation, confirming it as the Lindhard continuum. Our results establish ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering as a momentum-resolved probe of the fermiology in metals. In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Here, the authors directly observe the corresponding Lindhard continuum in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering.

title: Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions
abstract:
Imaging large cell populations below the cortex in the intact brain is key for understanding brain function. LIFT, a multiscale three-photon microscope, tracks activity in over 1,500 cells across the hippocampus and adjacent regions in behaving mice. 
 Monitoring large-scale neuronal activity in deep brain circuits is crucial for understanding the principles of brain function. However, existing large-scale cellular-resolution imaging techniques are limited in imaging depth and cannot monitor activity in areas deeper than the cortex in the intact brain. To address this challenge, we developed a Large Imaging Field of view Three-photon (LIFT) microscope with a FOV of  > 3 mm2. LIFT combines high-numerical-aperture optimized sampling, using a custom scanning module, with deep learning-based denoising, to enable population imaging in subcortical brain regions of mice and deep cortical regions of rats. We demonstrate calcium imaging in the intact mouse brain from more than 1500 cells across CA1, the surrounding white matter, and adjacent deep layers of the cortex, and show population imaging with high SNR at a depth of 1.2 mm in the rat cortex. The LIFT microscope offers versatility in imaging scale and rate and was built entirely from off-the-shelf components. Imaging large cell populations below the cortex in the intact brain is key for understanding brain function. LIFT, a multiscale three-photon microscope, tracks activity in over 1,500 cells across the hippocampus and adjacent regions in behaving mice.

title: Passive abortive infection mechanisms targeting phage long tail fiber proteins
abstract:
Cheng et al. characterize two bacterial anti-phage systems that act via either protease-mediated cleavage or kinase-dependent phosphorylation to target phage tail-fiber proteins, establishing the concept passive abortive infection. 
 Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies against phage infection, yet mechanisms directly targeting viral proteins remain scarcely documented. In this study, we characterize two bacterial defense systems: TFAD1 featuring a serine protease and TFAD2 featuring a Ser/Thr kinase. We show that TFAD1 and TFAD2 act on phage long tail fiber proteins via protein degradation and phosphorylation, respectively. Intriguingly, both systems allow complete phage replication cycles but generate non-infective progeny—a mechanism distinct from classical abortive infection (Abi), which we term “passive Abi”. Our findings expand the paradigm of bacterial immunity by unveiling protease- and kinase-mediated incapacitation of phage structural proteins, offering insights into the molecular arms race between bacteria and phages. title: Transforming electrified railway into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization
abstract:
Coordinating train operations can transform electrified railways into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization, reducing the need for newly built storage while lowering system costs and carbon emissions. 
 Decarbonizing electricity requires vast energy storage capacity worldwide, but constructing dedicated storage assets creates substantial capital, material and embodied carbon burdens. Electrified railways already exchange energy with electricity systems through traction and regenerative braking, but their inherent potential as mechanical energy storage remains unexploited. Here we show that modulation of train operations can transform electrified railways into Electrified Rail-Based Energy Storage. By analyzing 326,034 inter-stop train operations, we estimate its global potential at 190 gigawatts in 2025 and 315–579 gigawatts by 2050. Capacity expansion models for China, Europe and India indicate that it can reduce investment in conventional storage by 11.9–20.0%, corresponding to an extrapolated global value of US$14.9–35.1 billion annually. Without increasing total system cost, electricity systems with this flexible resource could further reduce operational CO2 emissions by 94.3–258.9 million tonnes per year. Electrified railways can therefore complement conventional storage technologies for electricity system decarbonization. Coordinating train operations can transform electrified railways into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization, reducing the need for newly built storage while lowering system costs and carbon emissions.

title: A systematic review of nature-based solutions for climate action in African cities
abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS), including ecosystem-based adaptation, are increasingly proposed for climate action in African cities, but the evidence base is fragmented and lacks systematic synthesis of what is being implemented, where, and how effectively. We analysed 112 studies retained from a systematic review, covering 134 urban areas across 42 countries and including 45 informal settlements. Five NbS typology classes are inductively derived including: Green spaces; Rivers, catchments and drainage systems; Coastal systems; Green buildings; and Urban agriculture and multi-use gardens. Urban green spaces dominate the evidence (49% of studies) and are the most multi-functional class. Urban agriculture and multi-use gardens are under-recognised in headline framings, named as primary in only 5% of studies but appearing in 34% of the wider intervention mix. Evidence is increasing but concentrates geographically on larger cities. Successful climate change adaptation and mitigation outcomes are reported by 72% and 27% of studies, respectively. Heat mitigation is the most frequently quantified adaptation outcome, with temperature reductions up to 12.2 °C reported in proximity to urban green and blue spaces across the continent. Qualitative evidence links urban NbS to effective coastal protection, flood risk reduction, and increased water security. Multi-stakeholder governance anchored by local actors, and meaningful community participation are consistent enablers of effective implementation. However, insufficient long-term funding and livelihood disruptions and displacement raise concerns about long-term impacts. Priority research gaps include longitudinal effectiveness monitoring, financing mechanisms for informal contexts, systematic assessment of mechanisms behind inequitable outcomes, and evidence from under-represented regions and smaller cities.

title: A review of Last Interglacial sea-level proxies  in South Asia and the Indian Ocean
abstract:
We compiled a database of 54 ancient shoreline markers from Iran, Oman, India, the Maldives and the Cocos Islands, dating to Marine Isotopic Stage 5. The records show that the same past ocean level can appear far above today's sea on rising coasts, near today's level on stable coasts, and many meters underwater where land is sinking. This helps separate true ocean change from land motion and improves future sea-level planning. 
 In this work, we present a standardized database of Last Interglacial (LIG, ∼132–80 ka) sea-level proxies across the South Asian and Indian Ocean region, including the coasts of Iran, Oman, India, the Maldives, and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands. The database stems from a systematic review of the data included in 17 peer-reviewed studies, structured according to the World Atlas of Last Interglacial Shorelines (WALIS), and is available as Ali et al. (2026, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18512769). Within this framework, a total of 54 sea-level index points were re-evaluated to recalculate paleo-RSL elevation and associated uncertainties. This was achieved through updated determinations of their indicative meaning (i.e., reference water level and indicative range), considering the original stratigraphic context, elevation measurement techniques, depositional environments, and chronological constraints. The chronological framework relies on U-Th, luminescence, electron spin resonance, and cosmogenic nuclide dating. These data are characterized by regional differences in the elevation of past relative sea-level proxies that are driven primarily by tectonics, dynamic topography, and glacio-hydro-isostatic forcings. On the active margins of southern Iran and northern Oman, marine terraces dated to Marine Isotope Stage (MIS) 5e (∼125 ka), 5c (∼100 ka), and 5a (∼80 ka) are preserved at 20–60 m a.s.l., reflecting uplift linked to the Zagros foreland and Makran subduction system at least since the Last Interglacial. On the coasts of western and southern India, MIS 5e relative sea-level proxies are found at 1–4 m a.s.l., more in line with near-zero vertical land motion. On Indian Ocean islands, such as the Maldives and Cocos (Keeling) Islands, MIS 5e reefs are now submerged at depths of 10–17 m b.s.l., indicating subsidence since the LIG.

title: Stable isotope bioarchaeological atlas from the post-Soviet space
abstract:
Chemical traces in ancient bones and teeth reveal what people ate, where they lived, and how far they travelled. We compiled results from over a hundred studies, spanning more than one hundred thousand years across the former Soviet space, much published only in Russian and largely absent from international literature. The result is a large, open collection of ancient human and animal remains from Asia and the Caucasus, now freely accessible to researchers worldwide. 
 Results of stable isotope analyses from 435 locations in the countries of the former USSR were collected from 114 papers presenting the results of their research and compiled in two datasets stored in the IsoArcH database. The literature research was conducted using Google Scholar, Web of Science and Science Direct using keywords both in English and in other relevant languages, such as Russian, Ukrainian, Azerbaijani, Georgian or Kazakh. The datasets contain information on the originating site, including GPS coordinates, information on the samples (as available) such as source of origin, dating and details of deposition, and results of stable isotope analysis, namely the measurements of carbon (δ13C), nitrogen (δ15N), oxygen (δ18O), sulphur (δ34S) strontium (87Sr//86Sr) and lead (206Pb/204Pb). All source articles are connected to relevant data within the datasets. This compilation can serve as a comprehensive source for further research as well as a reference set for the geographical and temporal area.

authors: Mingwei Zhang;Wenzhe Fa;Jiaqi Tong;Yang Liu
title: Degradation Rate and Lifetime of Small Impact Craters on the Moon
abstract: Knowledge of crater degradation rates on the Moon is fundamental for dating individual craters, understanding material transport, and investigating crater equilibrium, with broader implications for water ice exploration, regolith evolution, and impact flux reconstruction. However, direct observational constraints on the degradation rates of hundred‐meter‐scale lunar craters remain scarce, and regional variations between mare and highland terrains are poorly quantified. Here, we measure the diameters and depths of 56,229 small impact craters across the Apollo, Luna, and Chang’E landing regions using high‐resolution optical and topographic data. We then systematically simulate the production and evolution of crater populations from geological unit emplacement to the present, accounting for both diffusive degradation and catastrophic obliteration. By comparing observations with forward simulations, we provide the most extensive observational constraints to date on the degradation rates and lifetimes of small craters with diameters of 50–500 m. At these scales, the estimated topographic diffusivities increase from 0.62 to 2.33 m2 ${\mathrm{m}}^{2}$/Myr in the maria and from 2.27 to 4.54 m2 ${\mathrm{m}}^{2}$/Myr in the highlands. Regional variations in degradation rates are most strongly associated with meter‐scale slope rather than adopted proxies for target properties. The inferred lifetimes imply that subhectometer micro cold traps are short‐lived (<100 Myr) and thus host only recently delivered water ice, whereas larger cold traps of several hundred meters can persist over geological timescales and are favorable for water ice accumulation. Our results further indicate that crater equilibrium at small diameters is achieved mainly through diffusive degradation rather than superposition, and that equilibrium crater abundance is expected to vary across the Moon.

title: How Microporosity Shapes Carbonate Hydraulic Behavior: A Digital Rock Physics Perspective
abstract: Carbonate hydraulic behavior emerges from flow through pore structures spanning resolvable macropores and sub‐resolution microporous regions, yet the effects of microporosity level and heterogeneity remain poorly understood. We develop and validate a CUDA‐accelerated lattice Boltzmann model that unifies pore‐resolved and continuum flow. Simulations show that low‐velocity microporous regions substantially contribute to bulk flow by activating connections between macropores. Across three carbonate samples, permeability increases nonlinearly with microporosity, with reference permeabilities spanning over two orders of magnitude. Moreover, at fixed bulk porosity, amplifying the observed phase‐wise contrast increases permeability, while spatial permutation controls reveal a dominant contribution from the original spatial organization. Three‐dimensional spatial and pressure‐gradient analyses further indicate that high‐microporosity phases preferentially adjacent to macropores become increasingly conductive as heterogeneity increases, reducing local flow resistance. These results show how naturally organized microporosity controls hydraulic behavior and bulk permeability in multiscale geological porous media.

title: Decadal Creep Acceleration on the Northern Japan Trench Driven by Erosion of Heterogeneously Locked Asperities
abstract: Geodetic and seismic observations before the 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku‐oki earthquake indicate decadal‐scale acceleration of aseismic slip along the northern Japan Trench, but the mechanism remains debated. We show that this transient can be explained by creep‐front propagation that progressively erodes heterogeneously locked asperities. We invert GNSS velocity fields from 1998 to 2009 using a mechanically motivated model in which locked regions are confined to historical rupture areas while their effective sizes and process‐zone stressing rates evolve. The models fit both velocity fields and predict slip accelerations consistent with repeating‐earthquake estimates. Inferred asperities occupied about 66% of their corresponding rupture areas in 1998 and about 37% in 2009, indicating substantial expansion of aseismic creep over the decade before rupture. The inferred shrinkage rates are consistent with fracture‐mechanics predictions for plausible coseismic stress drops. These results suggest that megathrust locking can evolve substantially over decadal timescales.

authors: Haozhe He;Brian J. Soden;Ryan J. Kramer
title: Improved Estimates of Equilibrium Climate Sensitivity From Non‐Equilibrated Climate Simulations
abstract: Calculating equilibrium climate sensitivity (ECS) requires simulations of a thousand years or more for the climate to re‐establish equilibrium, but most ECS estimates are derived from shorter model integrations. The widely used “Gregory method” for such estimates systematically underestimates ECS, a bias previously attributed to the time‐dependence of climate feedbacks. Here we demonstrate this underestimate instead arises primarily from an underestimate of radiative forcing. We present a modified method that corrects for the underestimate in forcing, producing ECS estimates that closely align with results from “long‐run” millennium‐scale simulations. This method is robust across models and offers an easily obtainable estimate of ECS with significantly higher accuracy. It enables reliable ECS estimates for full CMIP model ensembles, including models without millennium‐scale simulations. Using this method, we show one of every three CMIP6 climate models has an ECS greater than 5K—the upper bound of the “very likely” range in prior assessments. To further verify this method, we introduce an “integrated feedback parameter” which provides a more physically‐meaningful way to average a time‐evolving climate sensitivity by weighting the differential feedback in consecutive, non‐overlapping time segments by the fraction of energy imbalance that each segment restores. This parameter agrees well with that derived from our modified method, lending further credibility to this simplified approach.
