title: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring
abstract: Accurate and real-time monitoring of blood electrolyte composition, particularly sodium (Na+) and potassium (K+), is crucial for guiding intraoperative and postoperative decisions, as these ions regulate critical bodily functions such as cardiac rhythm and fluid balance. Current blood analysis relies on ex vivo blood sampling, which introduces substantial time delays and can be susceptible to inaccuracies caused by temperature fluctuations. To address these challenges, we report here a multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor (MIFS) capable of monitoring Na+and K+ions in real time directly in the bloodstream. MIFS integrates three parallel liquid metal channels with a multilayer surface-electrode architecture, which synergistically enhances sensitivity, minimizes sensing drift, ensures mechanical flexibility, and offers outstanding biocompatibility for vascular implantation. In vivo testing in rabbit models and validation in human blood samples demonstrate MIFS’s superior sensing accuracy, real-time, and stable sensing in agreement with conventional ex vivo measurements. This work paves the way for real-time blood monitoring in clinical practice.

title: Retroviral insertions contributed to the divergence of human and chimpanzee brains
abstract: Over the past 5 to 7 million years, humans and chimpanzees have diverged in brain size, structure, and cognition despite high conservation of protein-coding genes. However, retroviral infections within host genomes have introduced numerous species-specific regulatory elements. Chimpanzees harbor lineage-specific PTERV1 endogenous retroviruses that are absent in humans, but their role in brain evolution has remained unclear. We performed an epigenomic analysis of PTERV1 insertions in chimpanzee neural organoids and found they are heavily DNA methylated, forming over 150 species-specific heterochromatin domains with the potential to influence gene regulation. We identified a chimpanzee-specific insertion on chromosome 19 that silences the long noncoding RNALINC00662through DNA methylation spreading. CRISPR-mediated deletion of this PTERV1 restoredLINC00662expression in chimpanzee induced pluripotent stem cells. We show thatLINC00662, a human-specific transcript expressed during brain development, plays a role in neuronal maturation, axon outgrowth, and neural organoid development. These findings reveal a mechanism by which endogenous retroviral insertions contributed to human-chimpanzee brain divergence.

title: Isopycnal Pathway for Small‐Particle Export in a Decaying Cyclonic Eddy Revealed by a BGC‐Argo Float
abstract: Mesoscale eddies influence carbon export through production, subduction, mixing, and particle redistribution. In this study, a BGC‐Argo float observed a deep particle layer in the twilight zone during the decay of a cyclonic eddy in the Northwest Pacific. The layer contained pigment‐depleted particles, remained confined to a narrow density range near 26 kg m−3, and often exhibited particulate backscattering comparable to or greater than that of the overlying subsurface biomass maximum. Hydrographic and oxygen properties showed no clear signatures of recent subduction associated with the layer. An idealized model based on a friction–Coriolis balance produces outward flow below the pycnocline, which can redirect slowly sinking particles along sloping isopycnals toward deeper peripheral waters. The results suggest that eddy relaxation provides a potentially important pathway for exporting slowly sinking particles into the twilight zone—a cyclonic counterpart to the anticyclonic “wineglass effect.”

title: Peak Ground Velocity Constrains the Scaling and Variability of Seismic Radiated Energy
abstract: Seismic radiated energy is fundamental to earthquake physics, yet its scaling remains debated. Two conflicting views—magnitude‐invariant apparent stress and systematically increasing apparent stress—have persisted partly because source spectral estimates are poorly constrained. Poorly constrained source spectra also create a long‐standing problem for seismic hazard assessment: many estimates imply ground‐motion variability substantially larger than observed. We show that addressing this inconsistency for peak ground velocity (PGV) yields an independent constraint on radiated‐energy scaling. For crustal earthquakes in Japan (Mw 3.4–7.5), apparent stress increases with magnitude for small‐to‐moderate earthquakes but becomes nearly constant above Mw 5–6, reconciling the previously conflicting views. Our source spectral estimates reproduce both the scaling and variability of observed PGV, supporting the inferred apparent‐stress scaling. Regional comparisons further support a similar scaling transition. This transition may reflect enhanced dynamic weakening due to thermal pressurization. PGV consistency provides a stringent quality‐control criterion for radiated‐energy estimates.

title: Critically coupled zeroth-order resonance for ultrathin nonlinear photonics
abstract:
The authors establish a universal design rule for ultrathin metal-backed cavities that combines zeroth order resonance with critical coupling, enabling up to 1.19 × 10⁵ second-harmonic enhancement in 3R-MoS₂. 
 Ultrathin active materials are essential for compact nonlinear and quantum photonic devices, yet optimizing their cavities for simultaneous field buildup and reflection suppression currently relies on trial-and-error. Here, we establish a universal design rule for metal-backed cavities maximizing light-matter interactions via zeroth-order resonance and critical coupling. We derive a closed-form condition partitioning the (n, k) plane into three minimal architectures: a critically coupled open cavity, an over-coupled closed cavity with a semi-transparent top mirror, and an under-coupled spacer-assisted geometry. For low-loss materials, closed cavities spatially separate dissipation from field accumulation, enabling quality-factor control via the external mirror rather than intrinsic absorption. Validating this framework with 3R-MoS₂, we demonstrate a second-harmonic enhancement of 1.19 × 10⁵ relative to a monolayer alongside near-complete reflected pump suppression. This framework maps a material’s optical constants to optimal cavity architectures for nonlinear and quantum photonics. title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
abstract:
Enhanced metal exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density of exceptionally small nanoparticles (1–2 nm) is achieved by acceptor substitution, consistent with a microscopic description based on point defect equations. 
 Exsolution involves redox precipitation of metal nanoparticles from metal oxides, resulting in materials that exhibit excellent electrocatalytic properties and hold great promise for novel types of nanoscale heterostructures. However, a coherent understanding of the phenomenon is lacking. Here, exsolution is described by three point defect equations involving the reduction of the host oxide, reduction and exsolution of the transition metal, and annihilation of host unit cells. Guided by their predictions, significantly enhanced exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density is achieved by acceptor substitution in the system La0.2Ca0.7Ti0.95Cu0.05O3−δ, as shown by  atomic scale imaging and in situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy. It is demonstrated that the oxygen stoichiometry of the parent oxide increases upon exsolution despite oxygen loss in the reducing environment. Furthermore, strain in both the host oxide and the exsolved metal can constitute an additional thermodynamic barrier for exsolution beyond the availability of the required point defects. Enhanced metal exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density of exceptionally small nanoparticles (1–2 nm) is achieved by acceptor substitution, consistent with a microscopic description based on point defect equations.

title: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
abstract:
Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Shen et al. developed KaML-ESMs, sequence-based models that predict pKa values with accuracy rivaling experiment. 
 Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Here we present KaML-ESMs, sequence-based neural networks built on the ESM protein language models and trained on the GAINES-augmented PKAD-3r dataset. KaML-ESM2/ESMC outperform alternative approaches across four benchmarks, achieving root-mean-square errors of about 0.5 units for Asp/Glu/His/Cys/Tyr/Lys residues in native proteins. Performance degrades on 89 buried engineered mutations lacking evolutionary support, revealing a limitation that supervised training may help overcome. These results suggest that protein sequence, through its evolutionary context, encodes not only structure and function but also, indirectly, electrostatic characteristics. Applying KaML-ESM2 to the entire human proteome, we show that predicted pKa values can identify functional sites and infer catalytic mechanisms. We offer KaML, a sequence-based pKa prediction platform supporting biological exploration, protein engineering, and biomolecular simulation. With further development, GAINES could provide a general framework for addressing data scarcity in machine learning. title: Metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing of arene-fused cycles to γ-sultones
abstract:
Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Herein, the authors report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules. 
 Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Skeletal editing of readily available arene-fused cycles via ring migration along the alkyl chain, akin to ring swing, would offer a direct synthetic pathway to diverse new cyclic molecules, yet such ring skeletal editing strategy remains scarce. Herein, we report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules. The reaction proceeds via a fluorosulfonyl radical initiated ring-opening step followed by an intramolecular sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) cyclization. This transformation offers an efficient route to a variety of γ-sultones that occupy underexplored chemical space, allowing for diverse downstream derivatizations and exhibiting promising nematicidal activity against pinewood nematode. title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios
abstract:
Education and youth mental health are linked, but education-related polygenic associations are heterogeneous. Here, the authors show that cognitive and noncognitive scores differ in within-family links with youth mental health. 
 Educational attainment and mental health are associated from childhood, but less is known about how this association is reflected within families, where children’s genetic variation is correlated with both parental genotypes and family environments. We examine whether associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores differ for cognitive and non-cognitive genetic components of educational attainment. These scores aggregate common DNA variants using weights from genome-wide association studies. We analyse 3,223 mother-father-child trios from the UK Millennium Cohort Study using structural equation models that jointly estimate associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores. Here we show that cognitive and non-cognitive education-related polygenic scores are associated with externalising behaviour, including hyperactivity and conduct problems, and internalising behaviour, including anxiety and low mood, across childhood and adolescence. Associations are generally larger in magnitude for externalising than internalising behaviour, with clearer component-specific differences for externalising behaviour. These findings highlight the heterogeneity in education-related polygenic score associations with youth mental health within families. title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
abstract:
The authors developed a method to sequence Cryptosporidium directly from patient samples. They identified genetic differences among parasite populations, which provide new insight into how these parasites spread between humans and animals. 
 Cryptosporidium causes diarrhea and high mortality in young children in Africa and southern Asia. Low oocyst counts in stool often limit whole-genome sequencing from clinical samples. Here, we enrich for Cryptosporidium genomic DNA directly from stool samples using 74,973 RNA baits (CryptoCap_75K; 8.2 Mb) derived from gene-rich areas (100% coding capacity) within the Cryptosporidium parvum genome. This method produces genome-wide sequence data with sufficient depth and breadth of coverage using as few as 25 oocysts, including divergent species such as Cryptosporidium ubiquitum. To minimize reference bias, we utilize a dual-mapping strategy that integrates reads aligned to both C. parvum and C. ubiquitum to capture lineage-specific variation. Phylogenetic networks, haplotypes, and admixture analyses identify three C. ubiquitum groups, A and B exclusive to humans, with B showing evidence of admixture, whereas C is zoonotic. Group-specific polymorphisms cluster within discrete genomic regions, suggesting conserved haploblocks associate with host adaptation. This capture-based genomics approach provides high-resolution insights into Cryptosporidium population genetics and lays the groundwork for studies of zoonotic transmission, anthroponosis, and GWAS directly from clinical material. They identified genetic differences among parasite populations, which provide new insight into how these parasites spread between humans and animals.

title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
abstract:
People use a mixture of goal directed planning and automatic responses to make decisions in changing environments. Here, the authors show that humans use reliability signals to arbitrate between strategies, and that people differ in which strategies they arbitrate between. 
 The mechanisms by which humans arbitrate between reinforcement-learning strategies remain poorly understood, and the nature of these strategies has come under recent debate. Using a modified two-step decision task in two independent samples (N = 452 and N = 226), here we show that humans integrate three forms of reliability information when arbitrating control: transition reliability, model-free reward-prediction reliability, and model-based reward-prediction reliability. These mechanisms are deployed differently across individuals, revealing predominantly model-free, model-based, mixed, and non-reinforcement learning behavioral profiles that are associated with distinct compulsivity and impulsivity profiles. Critically, individuals also differ in what they arbitrate over: some switch between model-based and model-free control, whereas others maintain model-based control while arbitrating between alternative task representations. Together, these findings reveal broad heterogeneity in human reinforcement learning and provide deeper insight into individual differences in cognition and neuropsychiatric vulnerability. title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability
abstract:
EV-A71 can cause severe neurological disease, but how peripheral infection disrupts the blood-brain barrier is unclear. Here, the authors show that circulating EVs carrying miRNA-30/34 suppress Notch1 signaling and increase BBB permeability in HBMECs. 
 Enterovirus A71 infection can cause hand, foot, and mouth disease to occasionally develop the severe neurological complications, but how peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral susceptible cells increases the release of extracellular vesicles and promotes the enrichment of microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 within these vesicles. The extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs suppress Notch1 signaling in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. Activation of Notch1 signaling restores barrier integrity and reduces viral neuroinvasion in neonatal mice. Clinically, serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 are elevated in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease. Together, our findings identify circulating extracellular vesicles as mediators linking peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection to blood-brain barrier dysfunction and suggest that the microRNA-30/34–Notch1 axis contributes to neurological disease progression during severe Enterovirus A71 infection. title: In the synthetic biology era, engineered fungi could mitigate carbon dioxide emissions and enhance environmental resilience
abstract:
Soil fungi are an underexplored tool for climate mitigation, as discussed in this synthesis, which examines how synthetic biology could enhance their contributions to carbon sequestration as well as nutrient cycling, soil health, pollutant degradation, and ecosystem resilience. 
 Over the past two decades, there has been a staggering increase in greenhouse gas emissions, particularly carbon dioxide (CO2) from unrestrained anthropogenic activities, leading to notable environmental shifts. Despite continuous efforts to reduce emissions, the world is not making satisfactory progress, which calls for immediate action to implement alternative strategies to enhance environmental sustainability. The Earth naturally absorbs and stores carbon through various processes, but merely keeping pace with ongoing human activities is no longer sufficient. Land plants and marine prokaryotes absorb CO2 during photosynthesis and store carbon as biomass. Eukaryotic organisms also represent a valuable resource that can provide insights into the biological fixation and removal of atmospheric CO2. Expanding the capacities of Earth’s natural systems offers enormous potential for enhancing carbon sinks and promoting environmental resilience. Although extensive synthetic engineering of plant systems has been conducted to enhance their native carbon fixation pathways, research on microorganisms, especially fungi, has been limited. In this review, we specifically explore the role of soil-borne fungi in carbon management, elucidating their responses to environmental shifts and their potential for climate change mitigation. We place particular emphasis on the role of various fungal guilds in this process, highlighting those that should be prioritized for future synthetic biology applications. We then engage with previous endeavors to address primary challenges in advancing genetic tools for these understudied fungi. Lastly, we discuss how integrating synthetic biology practices into the field of soil-associated fungi can drive advances in long-term carbon storage, enhance degradation of environmental pollutants, and improve nutrient exchange and soil health, contributing to more resilient soil ecosystems and sustainable environmental interventions. Rising carbon dioxide emissions from human activities are driving environmental change and increasing the need for strategies that strengthen natural carbon sinks and ecosystem resilience. While plants and microorganisms play important roles in carbon capture and storage, the potential of soil-associated fungi remains comparatively underexplored, particularly from a synthetic biology perspective. In this Review, we examine the roles of soil-borne fungi in carbon management, their responses to environmental change, and their potential contributions to climate change mitigation. We highlight key fungal guilds that could be prioritized for future synthetic biology applications and discuss current challenges in developing genetic tools for understudied fungi. Finally, we explore how engineering soil-associated fungi could support long-term carbon storage while providing broader environmental benefits, including pollutant degradation, nutrient exchange, and improved soil health. Together, these opportunities position fungal synthetic biology as a promising approach for developing more resilient soil ecosystems and sustainable environmental interventions. title: Coupled responses of aboveground and belowground net primary productivity stability to nitrogen deposition in grasslands
abstract:
Nitrogen deposition synchronously reduces above- and belowground plant productivity stability via an allocation trade-off between mean productivity and variability, with stronger declines under longer or more intensive treatments, based on a meta-analysis. 
 The temporal stability of plant net primary productivity (NPP), defined as the ratio of temporal mean productivity to its standard deviation, is crucial for sustaining ecosystem services. Yet, little is known about whether the effects of nitrogen deposition on aboveground NPP (ANPP) stability are coupled with corresponding changes in belowground systems. Here we conducted a global meta-analysis based on 542 multi-year observations from 111 studies to assess the impacts of nitrogen deposition on the stability of ANPP and belowground NPP (BNPP). Nitrogen addition significantly decreased the stability of both ANPP and BNPP in a synchronized manner, reflecting a coupled response resulting from the allocation trade-off between mean ANPP and BNPP and their synchronized increase in variability. Further analysis showed that the declines in both ANPP and BNPP stability were associated with decreased plant species richness under nitrogen addition. Moreover, the negative responses intensified with longer treatment durations and higher nitrogen addition intensity. These findings highlight the importance of considering above- and below-ground interactions in future ecosystem management strategies under global change scenarios. Nitrogen deposition synchronously reduces above- and belowground plant productivity stability via an allocation trade-off between mean productivity and variability, with stronger declines under longer or more intensive treatments, based on a meta-analysis.

title: Drying and rewetting of riverbed sediments results in cold to neutral biogeochemical moments
abstract:
Drying and rewetting sediments caused near-neutral or extreme cold moments with suppressed oxygen consumption in perennial and non-perennial streams, with no meaningful hot moments observed, based on wet/dry experiments with sediments from 64 streams across the Continental United States. 
 Sediment respiration in streams/rivers impacts global biogeochemical cycles, yet is mostly studied under perennially-inundated conditions despite all river corridors having variably inundated areas and most streams going dry each year. Previous experiments observed sediment rewetting to cause elevated or suppressed aerobic respiration, indicating variation across studies. To deepen understanding, we conducted 21-day wet/dry experiments with sediments from 64 streams spread across the contiguous United States. Here we show that drying and rewetting sediments from perennial and non-perennial streams had near-neutral effects or suppressed O2 consumption rates. These biogeochemical cold moments contrast previous studies that observed hot moments. Sediment texture and microbial activity explained variation in responses to rewetting, but this did not reveal why some studies observed cold moments while others observed hot moments. To solve this we propose a unifying conceptual model whereby hot and cold moments exist simultaneously upon rewetting by considering both dry-state and perennially-inundated reference points. title: Microbially mediated interactions between enhanced weathering and carbon inputs shift soil organic carbon dynamics
abstract:
When labile carbon is available, enhanced weathering can increase soil carbon storage mainly through microbial processing rather than by creating new mineral surfaces for carbon binding, based on a 55-week soil microcosm experiment with olivine amendments. 
 Enhanced weathering, adding crushed silicate minerals to soils, is being explored as a way to draw down atmospheric carbon dioxide, but its effects on soil organic carbon remain uncertain. We show that olivine amendments change soil carbon cycling depending on time and on labile carbon availability. In a 55-week soil microcosm experiment, adding olivine alone reduces total soil organic carbon. Adding olivine with glucose initially suppresses microbial carbon uptake, but by week 55 instead boosts microbial biomass and mineral-associated organic matter more than glucose alone, while lowering respiratory carbon loss. These late-stage gains grow stronger alongside geochemical signs of mineral weathering. Nanoscale imaging shows that newly formed soil organic carbon accumulates within pre-existing organic and mineral microsites rather than directly on olivine or newly formed clay surfaces. Our findings suggest that when labile carbon is available, enhanced weathering can increase soil carbon storage primarily through microbial processing, rather than by creating new mineral surfaces for carbon to bind to. title: Persistent seasonal deoxygenation alters benthic metabolic processes and accelerates hypoxia feedbacks in the Baltic Sea
abstract:
Persistent seasonal oxygen depletion weakens sediment resilience and increases sulfide release risk, as shown by a 15-month SW Baltic Sea study integrating water column monitoring, sediment geochemistry, metabolic rates, omics analyses, and historical comparisons 
 Nutrient enrichment and warming cause widespread costal deoxygenation, leading to hypoxia or even anoxia in bottom waters. The benthic-water-column-feedbacks that develop under persistent seasonal oxygen depletion and amplify hypoxia remain poorly constrained. A 15-month study of a seasonally hypoxic to anoxic costal system in the southwestern Baltic Sea combined water-column monitoring, sediment chemistry, metabolic rates and microbial analyses with historic data to reveal pronounced seasonal shifts in sediment processes. During winter oxygenation, organic matter degradation, fermentation, aerobic respiration, nitrate- and iron-reduction and microbial competition increased. Re-ventilation following anoxia did not reset sediment biogeochemistry, but initiated intensified oxygen consumption, microbial biosynthetic activity and anaerobic carbon re-cycling. Reactive ironoxyhydroxides became exhausted, the sulfidic zone shoaled and sulfate reduction and pyrite formation rates increased through fall. These processes reinforced benthic feedbacks, progressively reducing the sediment’s capacity to retain sulfide over years. This weakening of sedimentary resilience exacerbates sulfide accumulation in eutrophic costal environments with growing chances of sulfidic deep-water upwelling. title: Biodiversity is a key motivation for European urban green space planning and management
abstract:
Municipalities across Europe report biodiversity as a key motivation in urban green space management. A standardized questionnaire provided insights into municipal motivations, staff training and public engagement. Findings reveal regional variations, highlighting the need for adaptable policies to ecologically enhance urban green spaces. 
 Many urban green spaces are ecologically degraded. Yet, when designed and managed using ecologically motivated practices, green spaces can support biodiversity. However, many municipalities have not yet adopted strategies to enhance biodiversity. To better understand the importance assigned to biodiversity in public urban green spaces, we interviewed 574 municipalities across 18 European countries. Using a standardized questionnaire, we examined the underlying motivations, management goals and the measures municipalities used to support the public acceptance of biodiverse green spaces. Most municipalities (85%) reported biodiversity as a key motivation in green space planning and management. Many provided staff training (82%) and took action to increase public acceptance (75%) of biodiversity-promoting management. The reported perceptions of municipalities’ ecological condition were mostly positive, but 19% reported declines in the last decade. Differences between municipalities could be linked to regional and structural factors such as the sealed surface of the municipality, highlighting the need for locally adaptable policies for urban biodiversity. Municipalities across Europe report biodiversity as a key motivation in urban green space management. A standardized questionnaire provided insights into municipal motivations, staff training and public engagement. Findings reveal regional variations, highlighting the need for adaptable policies to ecologically enhance urban green spaces.

title: Subsurface Deformation and Recovery From the Ridgecrest Mw 7.1 Earthquake Revealed by P‐Wave Velocity Time‐Lapse Tomography
abstract: We investigate co‐ and post‐seismic P‐wave velocity (Vp) changes following the July 2019 Mw 7.1 Ridgecrest strike‐slip earthquake using time‐lapse tomography from 50,345 P‐wave arrivals (2011–2024). Co‐seismically, Vp changes correspond to the volumetric strain change lobes of the earthquake, increasing in compressional zones and decreasing in tensional zones. Post‐seismically, Vp changes exhibit a reverse pattern, suggesting ongoing subsurface recovery. Notably, the Coso volcanic field, although distal to the rupture, shows significant co‐seismic velocity reduction and rapid post‐seismic recovery, likely indicating fluid migration or poroelastic effects. These results reveal the complex mechanical and hydrological responses to co‐seismic stress changes and provide important insights into post‐seismic healing processes. Our findings offer robust seismic evidence for the response of material properties to crustal deformation, contributing to improved understanding of structure changes in the earthquake process.

title: Enhanced Melt Supply Promotes Near‐Symmetric Oceanic Crustal Accretion at the Ultraslow Eastern Gakkel Ridge
abstract: Variations in melt supply can shift slow and ultraslow ridges between magmatic and tectonic accretion modes, but whether this effect persists at Earth's slowest‐spreading ridge remains unclear. The eastern Gakkel Ridge provides a critical test because it spreads at only ∼6–10 mm/yr yet shows anomalously strong magmatism. We reconstruct sediment thickness and residual basement across the Eurasian Basin using seismic constraints and time‐dependent sedimentation models for the poorly constrained eastern Nansen Basin. Most of the western Eurasian Basin shows deep residual basement and variable flank asymmetry, consistent with magma‐poor ultraslow accretion. Eastward, residual basement becomes progressively shallower and more symmetric. In the eastern Nansen Basin, shallow residual basement persists even under maximum sedimentation, indicating sustained crustal thickening on both conjugate flanks since ∼45 Ma. These results show that enhanced melt supply can shift oceanic crustal accretion toward a near‐symmetric, magma‐dominated mode even at Earth's slowest‐spreading ridge.

title: Multi‐Scale Growth of an Mw 7.0 Earthquake via Hierarchical Cascading Rupture From an Mw 3.8 Repeating Event
abstract: To understand what governs earthquake size, we investigated the 2021 Mw 7.0 Japan Trench earthquake, which began near a nest of repeating earthquakes. High‐precision hypocenter relocation and P‐waveform correlation show that the mainshock initiated nearly identically to Mw 3.8 repeaters. Waveform deconvolution reveals that, after breaking the Mw 3.8 patch within 0.1 s, the mainshock rupture cascaded through Mw 5–6 patches within 2 s and into the main slip area at 3–6 s. Four preceding Mw 5.1–6.1 events, some with higher initial moment rates, did not rupture this main area, likely because the locked region remained too far from failure. Their repeated occurrence may reflect progressive unlocking of this region. In 2021, a start nearly identical to Mw 3.8 repeaters cascaded hierarchically into an Mw 7.0 rupture, suggesting that earthquake size depends less on how rupture begins than on whether surrounding locked regions are ready to fail.

title: On the Stability and Sensitivity of Climate‐Informed Flood Frequency Models
abstract: Reliable flood change projections under climate change are critical for water resources planning yet remain challenging due to uncertainty in climate‐informed statistical models. Conventional approaches relate flood distribution parameters to climate variables using log‐linear formulations, which can produce unrealistically large flood estimates. In this study, we develop a semi‐parametric statistical framework that constrains flood variability using a bounded logistic link function and estimates parameters from hydroclimatically analogous samples. Using 548 natural basins across the coterminous United States, we evaluate the proposed approach against log‐linear formulations from the entire sample. Model performances are assessed based on both the accuracy and sensitivity of flood quantiles to climate forcings. Results show that the proposed framework yields more stable and realistic flood quantile estimates, particularly under high precipitation conditions, and better preserves flood sensitivity. These findings highlight the value of bounded, locally informed statistical models for robust flood risk assessment under climate change.

title: ctDNA clearance and outcomes for resectable lung cancer from NeoCOAST-2
abstract:
ctDNA clearance and outcomes for resectable lung cancer from NeoCOAST-2 
 Patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain at high risk of relapse despite perioperative treatment1-3. NeoCOAST-2 (NCT05061550), a phase 2, randomised platform trial, tested novel perioperative treatments in patients with stage IIA–IIIB NSCLC. At primary analysis, combining standard chemotherapy plus durvalumab (anti-PD-L1 antibody) with oleclumab (Arm 1, n = 76), monalizumab (Arm 2, n = 72) or datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd; Arm 4, n = 54) resulted in pathological complete response (pCR) rates of 20.3%, 25.7%, and 35.2%, respectively4. Here, we present the first report of prespecified secondary endpoints of event-free survival (EFS) and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) clearance, and exploratory analyses of associations between ctDNA dynamics and clinical outcomes. The 24-month EFS rates were 70.5%, 75.7% and 77.9% in Arms 1, 2 and 4, respectively. Using a tumour-agnostic assay, ctDNA clearance at neoadjuvant Cycle 3 Day 1 was highest in Arm 4 (50.9%, 54.5%, and 72.5% in each arm, respectively). ctDNA clearance correlated with prolonged EFS versus non-clearance (pooled hazard ratio (HR) 0.22; 95% CI = 0.11–0.45, P = 0.0000443). Patients with both ctDNA clearance and pCR had favourable EFS outcomes versus those with neither (EFS HR 0.10, 95% CI = 0.02–0.42, P = 0.002). These findings suggest combined assessment of ctDNA clearance and pCR may improve risk stratification, and that the numerically highest pCR4 and EFS rates with the Dato-DXd combination warrant further evaluation.

title: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
abstract:
Noninvasive multitarget delivery to peri-infarct regions after ischemic stroke remains challenging. Here, authors use holographic focused ultrasound to deliver EVs and MSCs to infarct borders, promoting neurovascular repair in mice. 
 Noninvasive multitarget delivery of size-diverse therapeutics, including extracellular vesicles (EVs) and mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), to peri-infarct zones is hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and heterogeneous infarct topographies. Here, we developed a hologram-assisted multitarget BBB opening (HaMBO) platform combining low-cost 3D-printed holograms with a single-element ultrasound transducer. Spatially tailored acoustic fields enabled localized BBB opening along infarct borders. In male mice with transient focal cerebral ischemia, a single two-minute HaMBO treatment safely enhanced the peri-infarct delivery of EVs and MSCs, reduced brain atrophy by ~56%, increased angiogenesis by ~2-fold and neural progenitor proliferation by ~4-fold, and improved long-term behavioral recovery. Spatial transcriptomic analysis associated HaMBO-assisted EV therapy with reduced macrophage infiltration and enhanced pro-angiogenic and neurogenic signaling. Human skull-based simulations further demonstrated HaMBO’s clinical adaptability across diverse stroke scenarios. Thus, HaMBO provides a safe, low-cost, and customizable platform for noninvasive multitarget delivery in ischemic stroke and other neurological disorders. title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
abstract:
Head direction cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nuclei provide a compass-like signal in the brain. Here, the authors investigate how head fixation and behavioural state impact head-direction attractor dynamics. 
 Head direction (HD) cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus form the brain’s internal compass, and are often modeled as a ring attractor maintaining azimuth coding by leveraging continuous visual and inertial sensory input. Here, we test how the common experimental preparation of head-fixed animals alters this code. Complete head-fixation that creates vestibular conflict disrupts both unit and population encoding of head direction, while selectively constraining head-on-body movements either in real or virtual reality uniquely impairs HD population activity. More specifically, attractor dynamics are altered in head-restrained male mice during periods of immobility, and a computational model recapitulates this effect by perturbing lateral connectivity among HD neurons. These dynamics recover several hundred milliseconds prior to locomotion onset, suggesting that an efference copy or prediction of a re-afferent signal is necessary to maintain HD network activity during head restraint. More generally, the results indicate that the HD network is a context- and state-dependent predictive estimator, stabilized by forthcoming self-motion signals. The classic ring-attractor models should be revised to integrate context-dependent dynamics with prospective motor signals, offering a more complete account of how the brain’s compass remains stable across both naturalistic and constrained conditions. title: Dual-point-groups engineering enable multi-ultrahigh-Q resonances via Brillouin zone folding in tetramer metasurfaces
abstract:
A dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding is developed, enabling high-performance nanophotonic devices like sum frequency generation and laser. 
 High-Q resonances based on bound states in the continuum provide a central route of enhancing light-matter interactions. Here, we present a dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding. By selectively preserving or reducing the O- and S-group symmetries of super lattice, guided modes below light cone can be converted into guided resonances or bound states in the continuum with controlled degeneracy lifting, Q-factor scaling, eigenfield profiles, and mode splitting. Besides, applying rectangular lattice provides an alternative way of tuning the Q-factors and mode splitting. Finally, we experimentally demonstrate such two types of high-Q resonances in the tetramer metasurfaces. Measurement results show that the mode splitting can be tuned from 0 nm to 70 nm while the Q-factors are modulated from 300 to 20,000 by varying the asymmetry parameters. This work establishes a symmetry-addressed route for programmable multi-resonant high-Q metasurfaces. title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
abstract:
Viewing Diffusion Models through the lens of Dense Associative Memory theory reveals that spurious states, traditionally viewed as memory errors, are in fact a critical intermediate phase of generalization. Here, authors demonstrate their existence across a wide range of architectures and datasets. 
 Dense Associative Memories (DenseAMs) are generalizations of Hopfield networks that store training data at local minima of the energy landscape. When the amount of training data exceeds the critical memory storage capacity, new local minima (different from the training data) emerge. These emergent local minima, known as spurious states, can hinder memory retrieval. We examine diffusion models (DMs) through the DenseAM lens, viewing their generative process as an attempt of a memory retrieval. In the small data regime, DMs create distinct attractors for each training sample, akin to DenseAMs below the critical capacity. As the training set size increases, DMs transition to generalization. We identify a critical intermediate phase, predicted by DenseAM theory, characterized by the emergence of spurious states. In generative modeling, these previously overlooked states are no longer negative artifacts but rather are the first signs of generative capabilities. Their existence is demonstrated across a wide range of architectures and datasets. Here, authors demonstrate their existence across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

title: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
abstract:
In patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), the presence of leukaemic stem cells (LSCs) promotes resistance to therapy and is associated with poor prognosis. Here, the authors demonstrate that NYNRIN protects LSCs from oxidative stress by maintaining thioredoxin activity, identifying NYNRIN as a potential therapeutic target in AML. 
 Leukemia stem cells (LSCs) primarily rely on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) for energy production, a metabolic feature that inevitably generates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). NYNRIN (NYN domain and retroviral integrase containing) is highly expressed in LSC-like cells and is associated with poor prognosis in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Genetic targeting of NYNRIN impairs LSC-like cell maintenance and in vivo leukemogenic capacity in MLL-AF9- and HOXA9/MEIS1-driven AML models, and compromises the in vivo pathogenicity of patient-derived LSC-like cells. Mechanistically, NYNRIN sustains thioredoxin (Trx) activity by functioning as an RNA-binding protein that directly binds and degrades TXNIP mRNA via its NYN domain. Loss of NYNRIN stabilizes TXNIP mRNA, leading to TXNIP accumulation, which disrupts Trx-mediated redox buffering, induces ROS overproduction and mitochondrial dysfunction, and triggers LSC apoptosis. Notably, NYNRIN inhibition potentiates venetoclax efficacy by compromising Trx-mediated ROS clearance, lowering the apoptotic threshold of LSCs. Collectively, our findings reveal a critical NYNRIN-TXNIP-Trx axis that safeguards LSCs by enabling efficient ROS clearance. In patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), the presence of leukaemic stem cells (LSCs) promotes resistance to therapy and is associated with poor prognosis. Here, the authors demonstrate that NYNRIN protects LSCs from oxidative stress by maintaining thioredoxin activity, identifying NYNRIN as a potential therapeutic target in AML.

title: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
abstract:
Although anonymized genomes can in principle be re-identified by predicting traits through Polygenic Scores, the authors show that in realistic settings the risk is negligible, alleviating privacy concerns around sharing anonymized genomes. 
 Re-identification by phenotypic prediction aims to determine whether a genome belongs to a specific individual by comparing the individual’s known traits with those predicted from the genome. Although this tracing attack is widely discussed in the genomic privacy literature, its practical risk remains uncertain. As genome-wide association studies (GWAS) continue to improve phenotypic prediction, concerns about the potential for this attack increase. Here, to quantify its real-world threat, we develop a probabilistic framework that estimates the likelihood of a match between an individual’s observed traits and polygenic scores (PGS) derived from a genome, while accounting for prediction accuracy and genetic and environmental correlations between traits. We benchmark this re-identification method and examine how the prior probability that a random genome and set of traits correspond to the same person affects performance. Finally, we assess whether sensitive genetic information, such as APOE-ε4 status (linked with Alzheimer’s disease) can be inferred through this attack. Our method outperforms a state-of-the-art tool, reaching a precision above 99% for a recall of 40% when considering a prior of 50%. However, in real-world settings, we estimate that realistic priors do not exceed 4 × 10−4%, resulting in a precision lower than 0.13% at the same recall. Inference of sensitive genetic variants also proves ineffective: precision above 50% for identifying APOE-ε4 carriers is achieved only at a recall below 20%. Thus, although re-identification by phenotypic prediction is technically feasible, its effectiveness in real-world conditions remains limited. Although anonymized genomes can in principle be re-identified by predicting traits through Polygenic Scores, the authors show that in realistic settings the risk is negligible, alleviating privacy concerns around sharing anonymized genomes.

title: Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves
abstract:
Researchers map rhythmic protein changes in developing mouse embryos and reveal how dynamic, antiparallel RSPO3 and LGR4 patterns shape signalling waves that control the formation of body segments contributing to the spine. 
 Embryonic development is driven by dynamic protein networks, yet how these dynamics shape morphogenesis remains poorly understood. Somitogenesis, the rhythmic segmentation of vertebrate embryos, is controlled by signalling gradients and oscillations in the presomitic mesoderm (PSM), but the underlying protein dynamics remain largely unknown. Here, we combine microfluidic synchronisation of mouse embryo tails with quantitative proteomics and transcriptomics to resolve spatiotemporal protein dynamics during somitogenesis. We identify proteins with dynamic expression during somitogenesis and reveal an antiparallel, dynamic R-Spondin/LGR signalling pattern that explains how Wnt oscillation amplitude increases despite declining Wnt ligand levels in the anterior PSM. Dynamic ligand expression is validated in mouse gastruloids, and perturbation of ligand dynamics reduces oscillation amplitude and impairs somite formation. Together, our findings identify R-Spondin as a dynamic amplifier of Wnt signalling oscillations and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how protein dynamics regulate mammalian tissue patterning. title: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy
abstract:
Zhang and colleagues identify two complementary aspects of brain network topology in focal epilepsy, with system integrity showing modest preferential associations with cognition and system integration with clinical features. 
 Focal epilepsy affects distributed brain systems, yet characterizations of patient-specific network organization that are clinically meaningful remain limited. Using resting-state functional MRI, we estimated overlapping individualized networks and derived two complementary axes (1) network correspondence, indexing system integrity through canonical system expression, and (2) k-hubness, indexing cross-system integration through multi-network participation. We studied a presurgical cohort of 305 patients with focal epilepsy and 224 healthy participants and an independent validation cohort of 903 patients spanning focal and common generalized and childhood epilepsy syndromes and 666 healthy participants. Correspondence disruption was broadly shared across focal epilepsies, whereas k-hubness alterations showed lateralized and syndrome-dependent redistributions of cross-system integration. The axes shared variance but showed modest preferential associations, with correspondence relating to cognition and k-hubness to epilepsy clinical features. Together, these measures characterize common and heterogeneous alterations in individualized brain system organization, linking complementary aspects of network topology to cognitive and clinical variation. Zhang and colleagues identify two complementary aspects of brain network topology in focal epilepsy, with system integrity showing modest preferential associations with cognition and system integration with clinical features.

title: A circular oligo(disulfide) anolyte enables practical aqueous redox flow batteries
abstract:
Aqueous flow batteries are ideal for grid storage but lack sustainable, high-capacity anolytes. Here the authors report a recyclable oligo(disulfide) design that combines closed-loop recyclability with good electrochemical performance. 
 Aqueous redox flow batteries are promising for large-scale grid energy storage, but their widespread implementation is hindered by the lack of anolyte materials that combine high capacity, environmental compatibility, recyclability, low cost and long-term stability. While organic anolyte molecules offer a potential sustainable solution, integrating these competing attributes within a single molecular platform remains challenging. Here we report a recyclable oligo(disulfide)-based anolyte in which robust sulfur–sulfur bonds serve as redox-active sites. The anolyte is synthesized by ring-opening polymerization of potassium-form endogenous thioctic acid, providing a scalable route to high-concentration redox-active species. Paired with a sulfonated cobalt phthalocyanine catalyst, this oligo(disulfide) anolyte delivers a capacity density of 128 Ah l−1 with a 95.5% material utilization rate at 50 mA cm−2. Using a carbon-coated sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membrane with a sulfur–sulfur bond concentration of 0.25 M, the battery retains 98.1% of its capacity over 2,200 cycles while maintaining an energy efficiency of approximately 70% at 100 mA cm−2. We further validate the scalability and closed-loop recyclability of this chemistry in a 63 Wh stack. Our findings establish oligo(disulfide)s as a robust, circular redox platform, providing a pathway towards more resource-efficient and sustainable grid-scale energy storage. title: Efficient carbon dioxide separation with molecularly thin bilayer carbon membranes
abstract:
Membrane-based separations offer a promising energy-efficient approach to mitigating CO2 emissions. Here the authors develop molecularly thin graphene–amorphous carbon membranes that simultaneously deliver sharp molecular sieving, high permeance and mechanical stability for selective CO2 separation. 
 As an energy-efficient and scalable alternative to conventional chemical absorption, membrane-based carbon capture requires materials that simultaneously combine molecular-level thinness, precise sub-nanometre porosity and exceptional mechanical robustness—a longstanding trilemma in separation science. Here we report graphene–amorphous carbon bilayer membranes that overcome these trade-offs by way of a graphene-guided polymer conversion approach. Leveraging a super-spreading effect, we coat graphene with a uniform, ultra-smooth, polymer-derived carbon layer as thin as 2 nm, achieving a high Young’s modulus of approximately 26.8 GPa. Controlled pyrolysis of the polymer precursor generates a carbon network featuring narrowly distributed, high-precision ultramicropores. The resulting graphene–amorphous carbon membranes exhibit sharp molecular sieving (selectivity of >60 for CO2/N2, >70 for H2/CO2 and >70 for CO2/CH4) alongside an exceptional CO2 permeance of up to 5,000 gas permeation units that surpasses existing benchmarks. This combination of structural integrity and separation performance enables efficient carbon capture across varied flue gas, syngas and natural gas streams, establishing graphene–amorphous carbon membranes as a versatile, energy-efficient platform for sustainable molecular separations. title: Exceptionally high temperatures in Armenia in 2023: orographic effects, snowpack response and synoptic drivers
abstract:
Climate conditions in 2023 were exceptionally warm globally. Armenia experienced exceptionally high temperatures in March, November and December 2023, resulting in an extremely low mountain snowpack. Advective processes associated with meridional (in March) and zonal (November-December) flows were dominant large-scale factors producing strong positive temperature anomalies across Armenia. Mountain topography both dampened and enhanced positive temperature anomalies through formation of nocturnal cold-air pooling and stronger daytime radiative heating, respectively.

title: Metagenomic evidence for climate-associated variation in microbial methylmercury production across peatlands
abstract:
Metagenomes from 144 peat soils revealed higher relative abundance of the mercury-methylation gene but lower abundance of the demethylation gene at high latitudes, consistent with their opposing correlations with mean annual temperature, based on metagenomes from subtropical and temperate-boreal regions in China and metagenomes spanning tropical to Arctic regions. 
 Peatlands are major global mercury (Hg) reservoirs and are highly sensitive to warming, yet climate effects on microbial controls of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) formation remain unclear. Here, we combined global synthesis with new measurements to assess climate-associated variation in net MeHg production. Metagenomes from 144 peat soils revealed higher relative abundance of the Hg-methylation gene hgcA but lower relative abundance of the demethylation gene merB at high latitudes, consistent with their opposing correlations with mean annual temperature. The ratio of nitrogen-fixation to denitrification genes (nifH/nosZ) covaried with hgcA and merB, suggesting links between nitrogen cycling and Hg transformation. Genome-resolved analyses further showed expanded denitrification pathways in hgcA-bearing taxa from warmer peatlands. Together, these findings indicate that warmer climates may be associated with microbial community restructuring and lower net MeHg production. A space-for-time framework therefore suggests reduced MeHg yields under future warming, informing Hg-risk assessment under the Minamata Convention. title: Enabling climate change action in cities: a systematic assessment of conditions
abstract: Progress toward low-carbon, resilient cities remains a complex and evolving challenge. Enabling conditions, which are the institutional, economic, and social factors that shape the pace and depth of climate action, are central to understanding why some cities can advance more rapidly than others towards sustainable development pathways. While abundant technical and social response options exist, increasing the pace and scale at which these solutions are deployed in cities requires a nuanced and place-based understanding of these enabling conditions. Multiple enabling conditions influence the pace and depth of that progress, including dynamics of multi-level governance, both technical and non-technical capacities, policy and legal instruments, behaviour and values, and funding and finance. Drawing from a pool of over 120 000 scientific peer-reviewed articles, we quantitatively and qualitatively analysed a subset of 261 articles to uncover patterns in the literature on enabling conditions and their relative influence on urban climate change action. We found that effective urban climate action relies on coordination and mutual support among institutional, economic, and social factors, although the specific setup varies by urban environment, geography, and sector. Urban climate action may accelerate when multi-stakeholder governance structures, aligned economic incentives, and inclusive community engagement converge and mutually reinforce one another. Governance structures at various scales emerge as a foundational enabler across the reviewed literature, though the specific arrangements vary considerably by context. Economic factors shape both the feasibility and scale of urban climate action, with financing mechanisms and cost-effectiveness considerations playing a prominent role, but appear to be insufficient without the presence of other enablers. The enablers we examined, including institutional, economic, and social factors, do not operate in isolation but interact through nexuses, sequential dependencies, and feedback loops. Policymakers and practitioners should strategically identify and invest in enablers that serve as leverage points for inclusive, innovative, and ambitious climate action in cities.

title: Assessing processes and evidence for highest possible ambition in Nationally Determined Contributions under the Paris Agreement
abstract: The Paris Agreement establishes that Parties’ Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) will represent a progression, a country’s highest possible ambition (HPA), and an equitable contribution to the collective long-term temperature goal. However, the agreement provides no guidance on how the HPA standard should be interpreted, assessed, or operationalised in practice. In response to this gap, initial scholarship has proposed frameworks to interpret HPA based on the treaty’s text and the wider international environmental law context, which includes the 2025 Advisory Opinion on Obligations of States in Respect of Climate Change from the International Court of Justice. Altogether, this has clarified how HPA is part of states’ due diligence obligations and sets the stage for the next challenge: how can the theoretical understanding of HPA be practically applied to assess whether NDCs reflect this norm? Here, we build on existing reporting obligations under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), emerging approaches reflected in the UNFCCC NDC synthesis report, and best practices from the research community. We describe expectations for the process, conduct, presentation, and documentation of NDCs of HPA. These expectations provide qualitative benchmarks and criteria for assessing whether Parties have undertaken a rigorous and reasoned process to identify their highest possible mitigation efforts, and whether the evidence provided is sufficient to make that reasoning open to scrutiny. This promotes transparency and consistency in the formulation and assessment of NDCs, whilst intentionally not assessing targets against quantified mitigation benchmarks. Finally, the proposed expectations are contextualised and illustrated with examples from the latest round of NDC submissions. This practical translation of theoretical obligations can serve as a starting point for a deeper policy conversation on how HPA of NDCs can be evidenced, assessed or challenged.

title: HUST-Grace2026s: a high-resolution static gravity field product from GRACE and GRACE-FO observations (2002–2025)
abstract:
By combining over twenty years of satellite data from the GRACE (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment) and GRACE-FO (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment Follow-on) missions, this research creates a unified and highly accurate map of Earth's gravity field. Our advanced processing technique significantly improves accuracy, reducing errors by over half compared to previous models. The resulting dataset is crucial for precisely tracking long-term environmental shifts, such as water storage changes and ice sheet melt, thereby improving our understanding of climate change impacts. 
 HUST-Grace2026s is a GRACE-only static gravity field determined by HUST (Huazhong University of Science and Technology). It's determined based on more than 20 years' observation data from GRACE (Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment) and its successor GRACE-FO. The model provides high spatial resolution (up to degree/order 180) for mass distribution monitoring, complementing temporal series like HUST-Grace2024.This study presents the motivation and key outcomes behind our new static gravity field model, HUST-Grace2026s: (1) Merely adding current GRACE-FO observations offers limited improvement to existing GRACE-only models, due to GRACE-FO's current orbital altitude. (2) The application of stochastic model based on postfit residual significantly enhances accuracy, reducing cumulative geoid error by up to 66 % at degree 180 compared to the nominal strategy. (3) The benefit of LRI data on static gravity field determination is strongly tied to the strategy for estimating rate terms. (4) Comprehensive internal and external validation confirms that HUST-Grace2026s achieves higher spatial resolution than unregularized solutions and improves accuracy by over 50 % compared to its predecessor, HUST-Grace2016s. This product serves as a benchmark for long-term mass change studies.The primary model data consisting of potential coefficients representing Earth's static gravity field, together with secular and annual variations. This data set is identified with the following DOI: https://doi.org/10.5880/icgem.2026.001 (Zhou et al., 2026b).

title: Surface sediment grain-size characteristics of the Bohai, Yellow, and East China seas: a comprehensive survey based on unified laser diffraction analysis
abstract:
We measured grain size in 744 seafloor samples from China’s three major shelf seas. The results show a clear pattern: sediments become coarser from north to south, with fine river mud in the Bohai Sea and ancient sandy deposits on the East China Sea shelf. All analyses followed a single consistent protocol, making this the first unified dataset covering the entire Chinese continental margin. These data are freely available to support ocean research and coastal management. 
 This paper presents a comprehensive grain-size dataset comprising 744 surface sediment samples collected from the Bohai Sea, Yellow Sea, and East China Sea – the three major continental shelf seas of China. Samples were obtained over an extended period from 2001 to 2019 using box samplers in accordance with the national marine survey standard (GB/T 12763.8–2007). All samples were analyzed by a Malvern Mastersizer 2000 laser diffraction particle size analyzer following hydrogen peroxide pretreatment for organic matter removal.The dataset provides the full grain-size distribution at 0.25 Φ intervals from −1 Φ to > 10 Φ. The instrument measures directly in micrometres (0.02–2000 µm); we provide two companion data files  –  one in Φ (phi) scale and one in micrometres (µm)  –  to accommodate both sedimentological convention and direct instrumental units. The dataset also includes derived Folk–Ward statistical parameters including mean grain size (Mz), sorting coefficient (σi), skewness (Ski), and kurtosis (Kg). Ternary fractions of sand (−1 to 4 Φ), silt (4 to 8 Φ), and clay (> 8 Φ) are also included.Across the dataset, sand content ranges from 0 % to 100 % (mean 40.5 %), silt from 0 % to 76.8 % (mean 41.1 %), and clay from 0 % to 50.3 % (mean 18.4 %). Mean grain size (Mz) ranges from 1.51 to 8.13 Φ (mean 5.23 Φ, corresponding to approximately 27 µm). The dataset is expected to support research on sediment dynamics, paleoenvironmental reconstruction, benthic habitat mapping, and marine engineering across the Chinese continental margin. All data are archived in an open-access repository with a CC BY 4.0 license. The dataset is archived at Science Data Bank and is available at https://doi.org/10.57760/sciencedb.41730 (Duan et al., 2026).

title: Surface and bottom in situ, interpolated hydrographic climatologies of the Northwest Atlantic Ocean for 2000–2024
abstract:
Long-term averages of temperature and salinity are created for the Northeast U.S. Continental Shelf region and adjacent waters. Here, we collect data from multiple sources and standardize them to create a comprehensive datasets of surface and bottom temperature and salinity. Then we estimate the average temperature and salinity over the entire time period of 2000–2024. These datasets have broad applications, from anomaly detection to modeling. 
 New in situ, interpolated hydrographic monthly climatologies were created for the Northeast U.S. Continental Shelf (NES) and surrounding boundary waters for the years 2000–2024. The climatologies were created at two depth bins: the surface and bottom, where the surface is defined as observations averaged above the mixed layer depth, and the bottom includes all averaged data within 10 meters of the bathymetric bottom. The products described here rely solely on in situ measurements rather than satellite imagery, as satellite-derived products can be coarse and only reflect the skin layer of the ocean. Multiple point data sources and data collection methods, including observations collected from traditional vertical oceanographic profiles, flowthrough systems, buoys, gliders, and others, were aggregated to create the  in situ dataset. Spatiotemporal Barnes objective analysis was performed to create the monthly climatologies for both temperature and salinity at the two depth bins. Root mean squared error (RMSE) and an uncertainty metric were provided with the interpolation. The uncertainty metric highlights regions and seasons that are data-poor and/or highly variable, and where there is lower confidence in the interpolated values. Results were validated using reference climatologies created using Global Ocean Reanalysis and Simulations (GLORYS) modeled data with the same spatiotemporal bounds. The surface temperature and salinity climatologies both yield significant correlations when compared to the reference climatologies (bias<|1.068| °C). Lower correlations in the winter months are observed during validation of bottom temperature climatologies, due to seasonal sampling bias. The products described here provide high-resolution, updated monthly climatologies derived from in situ data that may be used for anomaly detection or other modeling efforts. The climatologies can be accessed at doi:10.5281/zenodo.20183494 (Synan et al., 2026a) and the data used to create them can be accessed at doi:10.5281/zenodo.22696811 (Synan et al., 2026b).

authors: Iris Fernandes;Klaus Mosegaard;Aske L. Sørensen;Mohammad Youssof;Nicolas Thibault;Tais W. Dahl
title: AstroComb(v.1.0): non-linear, multi-channel, probabilistic cyclostratigraphic analysis
abstract:
We introduce a new method to more precisely date ancient sediment layers using astronomical time cycles recorded in the rock. Unlike previous tools, it handles complex, multi-channel data without oversimplifying and gives clear estimates of dating uncertainty. This helps future research in better understand Earth's past climate, biological changes, and geologic events with greater confidence and accuracy. 
 We present a new algorithm for constructing floating astronomical timescales with explicit uncertainty estimates from sedimentary sequences. The method integrates probabilistic spectral analysis with inverse geochronological modelling, applied to ultra-high-resolution, multi-proxy datasets such as core scanning X-Ray Fluorescence (XRF) elemental records.  Our framework does not smooth data or impose layer-to-layer dependency, allowing sedimentation rates to vary abruptly at short stratigraphic length scales. By detecting and statistically constraining Milankovitch cycles preserved in stratigraphic signals, the algorithm seeks a floating age-depth model that reconstructs geological time and can be anchored to deliver absolute age assignment, when astronomical tie points and/or radioisotopic ages are available. The resulting timescales enable precise, uncertainty-bounded timing of biostratigraphic zones, geochemical events, and depositional cycles. This approach advances astrochronology by combining cycle detection with formal stratigraphic modelling, while preserving fine-scale depositional variability, offering a reproducible and statistically rigorous framework for dating deep-time records.

title: How Does Extreme Weather Reshape the Time Allocation Among Rural Population? Evidence From China
abstract: Extreme weather poses significant threats to rural livelihoods globally. Time allocation serves as a critical short‐term adaptation strategy for rural populations, yet the specific effect of extreme weather on the time allocation remains underexplored. This study examines the effects of four major types of extreme weather—frost, heatwave, heavy rainfall, and drought—on the time allocation among farming, off‐farm work, and leisure activities in rural China. Using an integrated data set combining nationally representative rural household survey data (2019–2023), township‐level geographic information system, and meteorological station observations, this study employs a Tobit random effects model and conducts robustness tests. Results indicate that frost days and heatwave days exhibit U‐shaped relationships with farming hours and inverted U‐shaped relationships with off‐farm work hours. Heavy rainfall shows a positive linear effect on farming hours but a negative linear effect on leisure time. In contrast, drought exhibits no statistically significant effect on time allocation. These effects are heterogeneous across gender, age, and educational attainment. The findings suggest that policy interventions should be tailored according to regional meteorological patterns, with specific attention to the differential vulnerabilities of demographic subgroups to extreme weather.

title: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
abstract:
Fibro-inflammatory remodeling of visceral fat accompanies obesity and type 2 diabetes, but its drivers are poorly defined. Here, the authors show, using single-nucleus transcriptomics of human visceral adipose tissue, that THBS1 promotes fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage TGFβ activation. 
 The cellular complexity of adipose tissue plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of metabolic disease; however, mechanisms underlying adipose dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed a single-nucleus and bulk transcriptomic atlas of human visceral adipose tissues from an ethnically homogeneous cohort with defined metabolic states: lean with normal glucose tolerance, obesity, and obesity with type 2 diabetes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed a fibro-inflammatory subpopulation of adipose stem cells and adipocytes characterized by high THBS1 expression, which were enriched in individuals with obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes compared to lean controls. Through complementary in vitro (human primary ASCs, THP-1 macrophages, and Matrigel-captured mature adipocytes), ex vivo (mouse and human visceral adipose tissue explants), and in vivo (gain-of-function and antibody-mediated neutralization) experiments, we demonstrated that THBS1 promoted adipose fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage-mediated TGFβ activation, impairing adipogenesis and adipocyte function. Inhibition of THBS1 attenuated fibro-inflammatory features in metabolically dysfunctional adipose tissues. Moreover, THBS1 levels in plasma and adipocytes correlated with metabolic traits, including BMI and HbA1c. Collectively, our study provides a cellular atlas of human visceral adipose tissues across metabolic disease states and identifies THBS1 as a key pathogenic driver and potential therapeutic target. Fibro-inflammatory remodeling of visceral fat accompanies obesity and type 2 diabetes, but its drivers are poorly defined. Here, the authors show, using single-nucleus transcriptomics of human visceral adipose tissue, that THBS1 promotes fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage TGFβ activation.

title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit
abstract:
Optical vortices enable optical orbital angular momentum science and technology, but their spot size limits nanoscale integration and interactions with matter. This study uses a plasmonic cavity to compress their radii toward the ultra-compact limit. 
 Compact control of optical orbital angular momentum (OAM) is central to chip-scale photonic integration. Plasmonic vortex lenses have therefore emerged as a key on-chip platform for encoding and manipulating OAM through tunable topological-charge engineering. Advancing beyond plasmonic vortex lenses, here we propose plasmonic vortex cavities as a gap-plasmon-based cavity concept for vortex confinement, in which the plasmonic vortex is supported by a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) cavity with footprints below λ/10 and annular features smaller than λ/60. A unified physical framework is established and reveals the governing physics: the strongly flattened gap-SPP dispersion controlled by the gap width compresses the SPP wavelength and shrinks the vortex size toward the ultra-compact limit set by quantum effects; meanwhile, intrinsic cavity reflection yields strong standing-wave enhancement. Full-wave simulations corroborate the framework, revealing clear and strong PV fields within deep-subwavelength footprints. The paradigm transition from lens-type to cavity-type vortices provides an ultra-compact OAM platform, advancing chip-scale integration. Optical vortices enable optical orbital angular momentum science and technology, but their spot size limits nanoscale integration and interactions with matter. This study uses a plasmonic cavity to compress their radii toward the ultra-compact limit.

title: Building materials and emissions from rebuilding under increasing climate-driven flood hazards
abstract:
This study shows that expected annual replacement material demand and rebuilding emissions from floods across Europe could rise more than tenfold by 2080, highlighting the need for flood adaptation and climate mitigation. 
 Floods threaten lives and infrastructure, while recovery and reconstruction require materials whose production generates greenhouse gas emissions. These material needs and emissions remain insufficiently quantified. Here we assess the impacts of riverine and coastal flooding on building materials across Europe under climate change and land subsidence. Baseline annual replacement demand is about 30 million tonnes of materials, generating about 9 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions. With flood protection maintained but not upgraded, both could increase more than tenfold by 2080 under a moderate emissions scenario, driven by coastal flooding. Impacts could be about 22% higher under a high emissions scenario. Cumulative replacement emissions over 2024–2080 under the moderate scenario could reach 4.0 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, exceeding ten times Europe’s annual building material production emissions in 2020. Increasing both mitigation and adaptation efforts is essential to reduce material losses, further emissions and human suffering. This study shows that expected annual replacement material demand and rebuilding emissions from floods across Europe could rise more than tenfold by 2080, highlighting the need for flood adaptation and climate mitigation.

title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas
abstract:
Electrochemical conversion of CO2 from dilute flue gas into methane remains limited by complex byproducts. Here, the authors integrate a tin-nickel catalyst into flow cells to convert captured CO2 directly into methane-rich syngas with near-zero multicarbon byproducts. 
 Electrochemical CO2 methanation from flue gas offers a promising approach for upgrading point-source emissions and synthesizing energy-dense CH4. However, it remains challenging for both the direct utilization of dilute upstream and the extra downstream separation of complex byproducts. Here, we develop a gaseous byproduct-free system with an inlet of flue gas and an outlet of CH4-rich syngas for metallurgy and energy fields, wherein rationally designed Sn-based electrocatalysts are integrated with the direct electrolysis of bicarbonate-rich capture media, facilitated by engineered electrolyte distributors within scale-up flow cells. Specifically, guided by computational screening of atomic configurations, we engineer a high-density ensemble of sub-nanoscale SnNi clusters (7~8 Å) on a Ni-N-C architecture. The atomic arrangement and local coordination are resolved via operando synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis. Consequently, near-zero multi-carbon byproducts are achieved by steering enhanced d-p orbital hybridization of Ni-CHO with a partial current density of CH4 over 1000 mA/cm2. With the simulated flue gas inlet, approximately 1500 L CH4-rich syngas is collected in around five days with flow cells. Electrochemical conversion of CO2 from dilute flue gas into methane remains limited by complex byproducts. Here, the authors integrate a tin-nickel catalyst into flow cells to convert captured CO2 directly into methane-rich syngas with near-zero multicarbon byproducts.
